General Course Objectives: This course in Advanced Interaction Design introduces more advanced topics in Interaction Design: speculative design, tangible interaction design, shape-changing interfaces, experiences in interactive systems, and emotion in Human-Computer Interaction. The course is expected to further develop the students’ knowledge of design, their creative skills, critical thinking, and skills pertaining to the development of more complex solutions. Please note: In order for this course to go ahead there needs to be at least 10 participants. I fewer people enroll there may be a change of going ahead with a 'special course'. If you have any questions please contact the teacher at kifr@dtu.dk.
Content: The students must work in groups to create a speculative concept and an interactive prototype involving several different types of interaction and interfaces and creates an experience for the user/audience. Validation of the concept/prototype happens via different kinds of user involvement; research, tests and/or experiments. The concept and prototype are expected to be based on thorough research, but all of the work involved in the development and validation can in itself be seen as research where a topic is explored. Students taking this course must be prepared to be challenged on their creativity. Speculative design explores a question or topic in a creative way - it doesn't necessarily focus on marketable solutions.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Develop and interactive prototype combining several types of interaction and interfaces, Tangible User Interfaces (TUI), among others, that are validated through user tests or other types of user involvement - Create an effective experience, that causes an impact within the audience/user - emotional - or otherwise - Create a convincing creative speculative concept. Creativity is judged on whether the concept is different, new, original, thought provoking, provoking/challenging – or even humourous. - Document and analyse findings from research, tests and/or experiments and apply results in a design in a coherent and convincing way - Apply the course theory in an interaction design - Select and apply relevant supplemental theory in accordance with the chosen theme - Choose and apply relevant methods for user involvement – e.g. research, tests and/or experiments – in a well thought out way - Reflect over personal learning in a nuanced way - Describe and reflect on the process in a nuanced way - Present and discuss results of the work in a clear and well-argued way - Discuss perspectives: The possible applications of the concept and possible perspectives connected to larger ethical or societal discussions
62051:
Name English: Product development - tools and design strategies
Danish Title: Produktudvikling – værktøjer og konstruktionsstrategier
General Course Objectives: The course builds on the previous courses in product development, ie. the courses 62008 and 62030, and 62039. Additionally, the calculation techniques of course 10935 are applied. The course is aimed at the students who wants to improve their skills in development of physical products. Course has a more technical approach than the mentioned courses. The course consists partly of: - a series of tools for products development, e.g. how statics and strength of materials can be used in product development, - introduction of different design strategies, e.g. Design for Manufacture.
Content: Product development, basic statics and strength of materials, design strategies, CNC, specification, concept generation, prototyping, CAD
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use and select systematic and creative methods for concept generation. - Illustrate and communicate problems, solutions etc. - Have achieved knowledge of how statics and strength of materials in practice can be used in product development. - Use the basic functions of the CAD software such as SolidWorks, Sketchup etc. - Carry out detailed design of a product'. - Complete overall cost calculations in a design process. - Use a CNC milling machine. Herein lies designing and manufacturing parts using CNC. - Use and select design strategies for a development project.

62053:
Name English: Introduction to Entrepreneurship
Danish Title: Introduktion til Entreprenørskab
General Course Objectives: - the students gain an understanding of / knowledge of how innovation, intra- and entrepreneurship are defined - the students develop / understand what an entrepreneurial mindset is and how it can be used. - the students gain knowledge of different process models and approaches to innovation and entrepreneurship - the students learn to understand and use different types of tools and to work systematically with development of idea to opportunities by use of test and to be able to structure a process from idea to concept - the students reflect on the use of the tools / methods and process that the students have - the students are trained in the use of feedback and can reflect on feedback
Content: In the beginning of the the course various definitions are introduced and selected methods are reviewed. Theory is tested in practice by exercises. An individual portfolio is written based on the use of the methods and tools (report 1). The students will in groups develop a business opportunity and write a business plan and in the process use entrepreneurial methods. The groups present their result at a poster presentation (one of the last days in the last week). Subsequently, each group prepares a final report and submitted it on the last day of the course (report 2). During the course, the students will work with peer feedback, thereby training them to give and receive feedback.

62054:

62130:
Name English: Sustainability and Life Cycle Assessments
Danish Title: Bæredygtighed og livscyklusvurderinger
General Course Objectives: To provide students with an understanding of the impacts of engineering solutions on climate, environment, and nature, including solutions within their own field of study (e.g., new products, processes, buildings, infrastructure, energy supply, chemicals, and food). Through life cycle assessments, students will learn to quantify environmental impacts on climate and nature, including ecosystems, biodiversity, and the aquatic and marine environment. The course is based on a fundamental understanding of planetary boundaries and absolute sustainability. Building on life cycle assessments, students will work with solution development addressing the use of resources, including energy, materials, and land.
Content: The course introduces environmental sustainability in an engineering context, linking technical solutions to impacts on climate, environment, and natural systems. It is grounded in absolute sustainability, planetary boundaries, and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. Students gain a systems understanding of key environmental challenges such as climate change, biodiversity loss, and impacts on ecosystems and aquatic environments. A core element is life cycle assessment (LCA), where students learn to quantify environmental impacts across product life cycles, including data collection, modelling, and use of relevant tools, with emphasis on interpretation and critical evaluation. Building on this, the course focuses on developing more sustainable engineering solutions through approaches such as Design for Sustainability, circular economy, and digital technologies for resource efficiency. Students work with solution-oriented methods that address energy, materials, and land use. Finally, the course introduces corporate sustainability reporting, enabling students to understand and critically assess how environmental performance is measured and documented in practice.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand absolute sustainability, planetary boundaries, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals - Understand society’s impacts on climate, ecosystems, biodiversity, and the aquatic and marine environment (e.g., CO₂e emissions, deforestation, overexploitation, eutrophication, and pollution of water, soil, and air) - Understand principles of sustainable engineering solutions, including Design for Sustainability, Circular Economy, and the use of digital technologies (e.g., for energy efficiency) - Quantify and analyse the environmental sustainability of a product system using life cycle assessment (LCA) - Plan and conduct data collection on material and energy consumption, as well as emissions across the life cycle of a product system - Apply state-of-the-art tools to quantify and interpret life cycle impacts - Critically interpret life cycle impacts in the context of absolute sustainability, planetary boundaries, and principles of sustainable consumption - Interpret and apply life cycle assessments conducted by others, and perform critical reviews of LCA studies - Identify and critically assess the main strengths and limitations of LCA studies (own and others’) - Propose solutions that leverage new technologies (e.g., electrification, material passports, and recycling processes) or improve resource efficiency in energy, materials, land use, and impacts on nature, biodiversity, and ecosystems - Understand corporate sustainability reporting, including the data, documentation, and calculations underpinning such reporting

Danish Title: Strategisk analyse og udvikling
General Course Objectives: To give students experience in assessing and developing sustainable business strategies for different business situations and industries. Furthermore, the students acquire skills in collaborating and communicating in English.
Content: - Corporate vision, mission, and purpose - Stakeholder mapping - Strategic analysis (internal & external) - Identification of critical success factors and needs for developing new strategic capabilities - Generic business and corporate strategies - Identification of strategic options - Evaluation and selection of strategies - Introduction to the implementation of new strategies - Change management - Sustainable strategies and ESG risk analysis - Business cases
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Demonstrate knowledge of key concepts and models within strategic management and communicate this in English - Apply the course concepts and models to analyze the business environment of an organization to identify strategic threats and opportunities - Apply the course concepts and models to analyze a company's resources and competencies to identify strategic strengths and weaknesses - Explain how company culture and history affect the strategic development in an organization - Explain the importance and impact of cultural differences - Identify the stakeholders of an organization and analyze their impact on the organizations choice of a sustainable strategy - Explain different types of generic business strategies as well as specific strategies for innovation and internationalization - Evaluate the suitability of different types of business strategies based upon an analysis of a company's strategic position - Explain methods and challenges associated with implementation of strategic changes
62135:
Name English: Quality Management
Danish Title: Quality Management
General Course Objectives: To give the student an insight into Quality Management in service and manufacturing businesses.
Content: Basic concepts of Quality, company wide assessment, Quality Function Deployment, Quality Improvements, ISO 9000, Quality culture, Quality in regulated areas (FDA etc), EFQM model.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Knowledge about Total Quality Management in service organisations - Knowledge about Total Quality Management in manufacturing processes - Able to explain about continous improvement programs - Knowledge about Quality management in regulated industries - Knowledge about FDA - Knowledge about ISO 9000 - Knowledge about EFQM model - Knowledge about Six Sigma and LEAN programs
62136:
Name English: Macroeconomics and Globalisation
Danish Title: Makroøkonomi og globalisering
General Course Objectives: The growing internationalization means that private enterprises are increasingly exposed to developments in domestic and international macroeconomic variables. A proper development of corporate strategy and financial management therefore requires that decision-makers are aware of - and able to analyse – how macroeconomic development affects business opportunities and performance.
Content: - Basic macroeconomic relationships between economic growth, employment, inflation, international competitiveness and balance of payments - Foreign exchange rates - including Denmark's fixed exchange-rate system - Interest rates and financial markets - Macro-economic forecasting models - Domestic and international macroeconomic forecasting - Economic policy in particular fiscal policy, monetary policy and policies for international competitiveness - International trade and globalization - Labour-market and developments in overall productivity - Current macroeconomic issues
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain basic macroeconomic concepts and relations - Present the main causes of business cycles and their impact on the socio-economic development - Discuss the main economic causes and effects of increasing international trade and globalization - Explain the overall objectives and instruments of fiscal, monetary and competitiveness policy - Analyze macroeconomic variables influence on the companies financial performance, strategic development and international competitiveness - Collect relevant information from national and international economic forecasting-reports as well as from the database of Statistics Denmark. - Demonstrate knowledge of major current issues in the Danish and international macroeconomic situation - Analyse and present a socio-economic issue
62139:
Name English: Advanced Financial Management
Danish Title: Videregående økonomistyring
General Course Objectives: To give the students a deeper understanding and more practical knowledge about the financial management issues which are introduced in the mandatory courses. The students are furthermore introduced to a number of contemporary financial management tools used by companies in addition to the traditional budget-based financial management practises. Moreover, the course contain a number of current financial management issues originating from large Danish companies.
Content: • Strategic accounts analysis • Activity Based Costing and Activity Based Management • Financial project control – Earned Value Project Management • Cost-benefit analysis • Shareholder value • Capital Asset Pricing Model • Enterprise Risk Management • Balanced Scorecards • Non financial reporting - sustainability, ESG, Climate and environment and SDGs
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Prepare a strategic financial analysis - Estimate the cost of equity and WACC based upon the CAPM-model - Estimate the value of a company based on the DCF-model (Discounted Cash Flow) and multiples - Explain the shareholder value philosophy - Explain the financial management tasks in the various sub-phases of a project, including which tools can be used - Undertake project controlling based upon EVPM model - Calculate product and customer profitability by use of the Activity Based Costing - Explain the key elements of Enterprise Risk Management - Explain the structure of Balanced Scorecards and identify relevant critical success factors and key performance indicators - Integrate sustainability, ESG, climate and environmental account and the SDGs in connection with economic decision making
62142:
Name English: Digitalization and Industry 4.0
Danish Title: Digitalisering og Industri 4.0
General Course Objectives: Digitalization and Industry 4.0 have, in recent years, had a significant impact on the value chains, production systems, and processes. Digitalization and Industry 4.0 have affected the production of products as well as the production of services (for example in the financial sector, health care and in the transport sector). Digitalization and the application of data provide new opportunities to develop and optimize the company’s value chains, production systems, and processes. However, there is a challenge for many companies about creating real value from digitalization. This course will, based on the ongoing movement towards Industry 4.0, will provide students with an overview of the opportunities that digitization provides to develop and optimize value chains, production systems and processes
Content: The course is based on the ongoing development of digitalisation and Industry 4.0. Among the topics that will be considered during the course are: - Selected digitization and Industry 4.0 technologies and systems - The importance of digitalisation and Industry 4.0 for the company's value chains, production systems and processes - Importance of digitalization and Industry 4.0 at strategic, tactical and operational level - Digitization and Industry 4.0 in production and service companies - Process optimization in relation to digitization and Industry 4.0 - Market opportunities due to digitalisation and Industry 4.0 - Production economics in relation to digitalisation and Industry 4.0
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have insight into selected technologies and systems related to digitization of value chains production systems, and processes as well as Industry 4.0 - Understand the importance of digitizing and Industry 4.0 in relation to the company's strategy and the company's development of value chains, production systems and processes - Understand how digitalisation and Industry 4.0 affects the company's ability to optimize processes and flow - Understand how the company's supply chain as well as production planning and management tasks are affected by digitalisation and Industry 4.0 - Understand the market opportunities and potentials of digitalization and Industry 4.0 - Design and develop the company's production planning and management tasks using models and concepts from digitalization and Industry 4.0 - Select relevant technologies and systems related to optimization, design and development of the company's processes, production systems and value chains - Assess how digitalisation and Industry 4.0 implementation will impact the company's costs and earnings
62145:
Name English: Documentation of Products
Danish Title: Produkters dokumentation
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is that the students: - Get a basic insight into the functioning, structure and manufacturing of mechanical engineering products. - Will be able to communicate professionally using sketches, technical drawings and other graphic models. - Will be able to use an advanced CAD system. - Will be able to perform technical records, including using DTU's IT facilities.
Content: Sketching techniques, basic projection rules and standards for performing drawings of machine components. Dimensioning, including indication of simple tolerances and surface roughness. General introduction to graphic communication, including presentation of results in technical journals. Use of CAD for product modeling, production of technical drawings as well as illustrations and animations. Students will typically study delivered mechanical engineering products individually or in smaller groups and try to clarify a number of industrial, economic, quality, product development and technical aspects. The products are modeled descriptively and analytically in a variety of models, including describing and analyzing the features of the used machine elements. The work on product analysis is documented in the form of drawing documentation and journals.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the characteristics of the projection (double-orthogonal and axonometric projection) and choose the most appropriate projection form for a given task. - Perform the drawing types, principles sketches and diagrams that describe machine construction and function and apply them to spatial visual drawings and sketches, mechanical engineering and design drawing. - Read a mechanical drawing and judge whether it is clear and unambiguous. - Produce a high-quality mechanical engineering drawing suitable for manufacture in an external workshop, including having demonstrated knowledge of relevant standards. - Model a product of multiple components in an advanced CAD system and apply the models as a basis for the production of simple machining drawings and Rapid Protyping of the models. - Use drawing (graphic modeling and communication) for problem solving, including proposition and presentation. - Document the results of the project work in a technical journal or poster with a high academic content. - Perform simple calculations in order to investigate, understand and document mechanical products from everyday life. - Identify standard elements, machine elements and machine parts in a simple product.
62146:
Name English: Mechanical Product Analysis
Danish Title: Mekanisk produktanalyse
General Course Objectives: - Being professionally introduced to engineering, including the construction of a professional vocabulary - get a basic insight into the functioning and construction of mechanical engineering products - engages in disciplines such as problem solving, collaboration, documentation and presentation (oral as written) - Introduced to a machine engineer's complex tasks and that these are solved in an interaction between applied mechanics, mathematics, product documentation, etc.
Content: Experimental examination of mechanical product, eg. motor mower. Analysis of the kinematics of the leverbar mechanism and the internal combustion engine's mechanical work. Dimensioning of simple machine elements. Use of graphical communication, including presentation of results in the form of posters, slides and reports. Use of CAD for product modeling and manufacturing of technical drawings in connection with its own design project. Visit to major production companies. In groups of typical 4, students analyze a larger, mechanically-engineered product to try to illuminate a number of industrial, economic, quality, product development and technical aspects. The product is documented descriptively and analytically, including describes and analyzes the functions of the used machine elements. Function, design, manufacturing method and consequent production costs are sought. The work on product analysis is documented in the form of journals or minor reports. CDIO is an integral part of the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe an industrial product by its processes, components and machine parts - Analyze a technical solution in relation to eg. Forces and losses using knowledge from, among other things, Courses in mathematics and mechanics - Make a simple analysis of the thermodynamic conditions of a mechanical product, eg. Internal combustion engine circuitry - Use engineering software such as Maple, LaTeX, SolidWorks, etc. - Use drawing (graphic modeling and communication) for problem solving, including proposition and presentation - Document a project work both verbally and in writing (reports and records). - Plan and implement a small construction project in groups. - Get experience in team working
62147:
Name English: Individual Project in Engineering
Danish Title: Individuelt Projekt i Engineering
General Course Objectives: To acquire new knowledge and skills within the students engineering field of expertice, where the quality of the project work and documentation are the main issues. After attending this course, the student shall have a better picture of the requirements for methods to be applied for the upcoming BSc project.
Content: The project work can be a theoretical or practical investigation of an engineering problem. It can also be made in cooperation with a company or a research institute, either in Denmark or abroad. Relevant technical topics and engineering methods shall be applied, and non-technical considerations and assessments may be included.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Demonstrate independent critical reflection - Demonstrate the ability to collect data and to relate these to a technical context - Demonstrate the ability to set preconditions (requirements), and to relate these to a selection process for a technical solution - Apply and attain knowledge and skills in relation to real-life complex problems - Demonstrate holistic understanding and use non-technical aspects which could be social, cultural, financial etc., if so found relevant - Demonstrate ability to formulate a clear problem statement - Demonstrate ability to perform an analysis in relation to mapping solution(s) to a problem, and to select a solution(s) based on established criterias - Demonstrate ability to establish a project report with correct methodology with a professional conclusion based on a statement and an analysis of the problem
62148:
Name English: Building robots and devices for industrial automation
Danish Title: Opbygning af robotinstallationer for automation
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to give the student a professional competence to simulate and develop grippers for use with industrial robots. The Gripper design focuses on sensor technology, Me-chanical design and material. All designs are to be made in Solidworks and build as a digital twin in RoboDk for simulation . The electronics is based on but not limited to ESP32 microcontrollers, RaspberryPi and is to be programmed in MicroPython, Python and Arduino. Gain an understanding of methods for analysis, design and implementation of control electrorabbit robotic system that uses grippers. Gain an understanding of interactions between mechanics, electronics, Software and Regulation
Content: Robot simulation program (RoboDK) Practical exercises in robot lab.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Introducing students to digital electronics and circuits, embedded systems, microcontrollers, Interfacing systems and communication. - Microcontroller / microcomputer hardware and programming - Use of hardware prototypes (physical and digital twin) from grippers using microcontrollers and computer platforms and various additional components for sensorics to perform special tasks - Get a basic knowledge of the interface and configuration of industrial robots - Control and programming of grippers via PLC and various communication protocols e.g. but not limited to Modbus, MQTT and others - Build prototypes and gripper for materials such as fabric, plastic, metal parts - Experiments using different types of sensors and programming and regulation - carry through an applied case
62158:
Name English: Basic Mathematics 1
Danish Title: Grundlæggende matematik 1
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide students with knowledge of basic mathematical, statistical and probabilistic concepts, methods and ways of thinking so that they can use these to formulate, analyze and solve problems in the various disciplines of engineering. The course will also provide students with knowledge and understanding of mathematical, statistical and probabilistic description and modelling tools in physical, technical and economic subjects. Learning objectives: A student who fully meets the objectives of the course is expected to know the following in accordance with the main content below
Content: Trigonometric functions. Calculus. Statistics. Probability.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Know the basic characteristics of the tigonometric functions - Formulate and solve simple optimization problems - Antiderivatives for simple functions - Rules for definite- and indefinite integrals - Application of integrals - Describe a data material by simple statistical descriptors - Know the basic statistical concepts in probability calculation, estimation of parameters and test theory - Make probability calculations in the basic probability distributions - Perform hypothesis test regarding ratio and population value
62159:
Name English: Basic Mathematics 2
Danish Title: Grundlæggende matematik 2
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to provide the students with concepts, methods, and way of thinking in the areas of basic applied mathematics (primarily calculus). Real-world problems, drawn from a wide variety of scientific, technological, and economic subjects, are central to the course. Of particular interest are methods – part algebraic, part numerical – for the solution of differential equations. The course also presents functions of two variables
Content: Differential equations and multivariable functions
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Set up and manipulate simple infinitesimal models - Analyse and characterize differential equations by means of fields of line elements and by studying the relationships between complete and partial solutions - Solve first order linear differential equations and first order differential equations with a separable right hand side by algebraic means - Solve second order linear differential equations with constant coefficients by algebraic means - Apply numerical methods for ordinary differential equations - Set up and apply multivariable mathematical models - Analyze and solve select classes of multivariable problems - Determine derivatives of multivariable functions and make use of Taylor’s polynomial of first and second order in two variables, as well as Newton’s method in two variables to find approximate (or exact) minima etc.
62171:
Name English: Marketing Management
Danish Title: Afsætningsøkonomi
General Course Objectives: To develop students’ understanding of marketing management's basic theories, terminology, and methodologies. It is important that the student gains a clear understanding of the models used in decision-making processes to solve problems and address challenges that companies face. This course emphasizes the understanding of a societal market orientation; that all company activities start with customers and their needs in a people, profit, planet context.
Content: The core concepts and frameworks of marketing science include: Marketing research and information systems Understanding customers: Buyer behavior, value creation, and customer experience Market segmenting, targeting, and positioning Stakeholder analysis and the marketing environment Market-oriented strategic planning Industry analysis and competitive positioning Product life cycle and portfolio analysis Pricing, distribution, and integrated marketing communications
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand marketing as a business discipline and value-creation process - Demonstrate an understanding of the core concepts, frameworks, and terminology in marketing - Be able to apply the fundamental theories and methods in marketing - Analyze a market and choose appropriate marketing strategies and tactics - Demonstrate an understanding of planning and managing marketing offerings - Understand and apply the societal marketing concept - Demonstrate a solid comprehension of the fundamental paradigms of marketing management in context - Analyze cases and present findings
62174:
Name English: Managerial Economics 2
Danish Title: Erhvervsøkonomi 2
General Course Objectives: The student should achieve an overall understanding of investment, finance, budgeting and sustainable business management. At the end of the course, the student should have acquired knowledge and ability to apply tools to understand, develop and analyze business cases, including transferring technological knowledge into potential business development. The student should also be able to integrate global economic perspectives into the analysis and have knowledge of sustainability and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) aspects of business conduct.
Content: Business understanding Strategic analyses (PEST, Porters Five Forces, Porters Value Chain, the Boston-model, PLC, SWOT) Financial Management Budgeting (Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet, Cash Flow) What is a Business case? Preparing a cash flow statement for an investment project Evaluating an investment; methods and choices Optimal life span, tax and inflation Risk analysis International aspects of investment Scenario analysis and real options Equity and debt Criteria for choice of financing including costs, flexibility, liquidity and financial risk Take into account Sustainability and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) aspects of investments
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - have the ability to use and apply course specific terminology - be able to account for and distinguish between purpose and the actual application of models in relation to business economic decision making - apply course specific methods to describe and analyze a concrete problem statement and recommend one or more suggestions for a solution - take into account sustainability and Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) aspects, and be able to reflect on social return and impact of investments and business cases - describe principles and application for a number of key strategic analyses: PEST, Porters Five Forces, Porters Value Chain and the Boston-model, PLC, SWOT - understand and apply the 3 management objectives: activity management, capacity management and treasury management in relation to the 3 management levels: strategic, tactical and operational - use budgeting as an important management tool helping to reach the company's objectives - understand, apply and prepare budgets (Profit & Loss, Balance Sheet and Cash-Flow budgets) - prepare cash flow for an investment in a specific business case by applying financial theories, models and arguing for e.g. the discount rate - evaluate investments projects based on methods such as net present value, internal rate of return, pay back time, risk analysis, scenarios and real options - Argue for the use of investment methods under different circumstances, e.g. time horison - describe and analyze advantages and disadvantages of various financing alternatives and calculate effective interest rates for a given financing
62191:
Name English: Road traffic simulation
Danish Title: Vejtrafiksimulering
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to provide the students with a basic knowledge of road traffic engineering and micro simulation of road transport as concerns behavioral models for road transport, and to make the students able to use, run, calibrate and validate an existing software for the most common types of roads.
Content: Theoretical background for road traffic technique, simulation of road transport, model integration in simulation programs and evaluation of solutions.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the basic principles in building a micro-simulation model - Use the basic tools in a micro simulation software - Describe elements and parameters for the following node types: Priority intersections, roundabouts, signalized intersections (time controlled) and merging sections - Code these nodes (see above) in a micro-simulation model - Code public transport in a micro-simulation model - Carry out an analysis of delays and queue lengths using the tools in a micro-simulation model - Analyse and validate the results of a simulation - Produce presentation material including still pictures and movies - Create a presentation for the oral exam
62194:
Name English: Programming
Danish Title: Programmering
General Course Objectives: To give students a basic understanding of structured and object orientated programming that allows them to cooperate with IT-developers on projects involving programming.
Content: The students will learn structured and object oriented programming by programming LEGO Mindstorms robots as well as PCs. The students will work with: - installation of software - crossplatform development - different operating systems such as Windows and Linux - the organization and programs use of RAM During programming students will learn to use: - controll structures, conditions, and loops - classes and objects - user defined classes - variables and datatypes - text strings - arrays and lists - methods, parameters, and return values - console input/output - read and write text files - the structure of object orientated programs - programs with several source files - an IDE for program development By developing their own robots and programs students learn: - to analyze, design, and implement software systems - to use common UML diagrams - to describe IT systems in words and writing By building the LEGO robots students learn about: - what robots can be used for - motors that enables robots to move - different sensors providing robots with input - quality of sensors and handling of sensor data - communication between PC and robot - external factors that might influence robot operation - autonomes robots
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Develop a simple objectoriented program. - Read and describe an objectoriented program. - Read and develop basic UML diagrams. - Have experience with installation and configuration of software development tools. - Understand the relation between program and computer. - Use the terms of the academic discipline. - Communicate within the discipline object oriented software. - Work in a group on analysis, design, and implementation of a program.
62199:
Name English: Road design and traffic safety
Danish Title: Vejprojektering og trafiksikkerhed
General Course Objectives: This course provides introduction to road design and traffic safety, and gives students the ability to work with real-life municipal road and traffic development. Students will - acquire basic knowledge of modern municipal infrastructure - acquire basic skills in the design of road and transport facilities - acquire skills to develop projects to improve existing infrastructure - and acquire tools to constructively engage in and contribute to group collaboration.
Content: The course is organized based on the FRI and Danish Association of Architectural Firms' Description of Services for Civil Works and Planning. - Traffic Planning and Spatial Planning - Road Safety - Traffic Engineering - Road Design
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Design roads in urban areas - Identify and locate traffic problems - Develop and assess the implications of solutions to traffic problems - Analyse and understand traffic accident data - Develop and assess proposals for traffic safety measures - Describe and analyze a project organization for an infrastructure project - Develop schedule and economic estimate for the design and construction - Communicate, argue, and document the solution in writing and orally - Reflect on team cooperation, team development, and the use of personal and interpersonal skills
62200:
Name English: The Business Potential of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)
Danish Title: Forretningspotentialet i Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)
General Course Objectives: Emphasis is placed on students' work in exploring AI and relating it to job tasks, work functions, business economics, business potential, and macroeconomics. A series of videos and online tools will be provided for students to use and familiarize themselves with. The course is not designed as a technical AI course but rather as one that connects the technical understanding of AI’s opportunities and risks with economics and business operations. Where possible, guest lecturers will be involved to provide up-to-date insights. The course concludes with a presentation in which student groups present the tasks they have worked on and the expected consequences for business economics, business potential, and macroeconomics.
Content: Goal: Explore AI's impact on business, economy, and the labor market. Approach: Not a technical AI course, but focused on economics and business operations. Methods: Videos, online tools, guest lectures, and case studies. Every two weeks. Conclusion: Students present AI's business implications. Exam: Oral group presentation. 30 minutes in total. Max. 10-page report. Main Topics per Session: 1. Introduction to AI and business potential 2. AI’s history and development 3. AI’s economic significance and cost-benefit analysis 4. Case studies and workshop 5. Mid-term presentations and feedback 6. Ethics, risks, and macroeconomic aspects 7. Final presentations and summary
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand why Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) has a significant economic potential across sectors of industry and public administration. - Possess knowledge and ability in applying relevant concepts of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI), including a variety of risks for privacy and security. - Possess insight in the transformation of business functions and in using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) - Be able to analyze and assess Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) business case studies focusing on the business potential for effectiveness, efficiency and innovation - Be able to analyze key dilemmas in using AI not least by dissolution of truth, by fake generation and fake authenticity, and by allowing for higher complexity. - Be able to elucidate consequences of using Generative AI for the organization of work and its significant challenges for businesses and society - Have the skills to independently present, critically assess, and analyze theoretical contexts and fundamental concepts as scrutinized in the course - Have the skills to account for business cases in Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI) - Have the skills to convey the options for managing change in an organization using Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI))
62202:
Name English: Life Cycle Assessment
Danish Title: Life Cycle Assessment
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to provide the students with an understanding of environmental impacts of products seen from a lifecycle perspective, and experience in different methods of life cycle assessment.
Content: Environmental effects, resources and waste disposal. Methods for life cycle assessment. Inventory of processes (process tree), data collection and impact assessment. Improvement of products by the use of new materials, improved production process (ecodesign), change in business models.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe environmental impacts - Define goal and scope / make a problem statement for an LCA - Define a relevant functional unit for a product system - Model an inventory of in- and outputs - Execute a life cycle assessment of a product system using LCA tools - Use a software tool to calculate life cycle impacts - Develop proposals for the application of the results and for further analysis based on the results. - Discuss environmental labelling and environmental product declarations (EPD) - Relate life cycle assessment of a product system to the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals
62204:
Name English: Manufacturing Technologies
Danish Title: Produktionsteknologi
General Course Objectives: To give the student the ability to independently choose the most suitable processes to manufacture given products.
Content: Metal casting, forming and shaping processes, material-removal processes, joining processes, advanced manufacturing processes, rapid prototyping.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - relate material properties, design and functionality with the traditional manufacturing processes - characterize processes and groups of processes in order to determine realistic materials, geometric possibilities, tolerances and surfaces - general knowledge about process possibilities, tolerances and surfaces - identify which processes will be relevant for manufacture of a given component - identify relevant processes in a given production situation - determine appropriate parameters for machining operations such as feeds and speeds, tool life, etc - determine appropriate parameters for forming operations such as minimum bend radius, spring-back, etc - apply the above objectives through two written assignments (see below) to a specific product or products and consider the advantages and limitations of these choices
62210:
Name English: Project leadership - Leadership, Flow and Impact
Danish Title: Projektlederskab - Lederskab, Flow og Effekt
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to heighten the students' understanding of their role as project managers with focus on impact, flow and leadership. The course gives the students insight into and training in the use of specifik methods and tools for the following three core elements: - Leadership: focus on the cooperation with project owner and projectmembers. - Flow: Ensure optimal workflows and processes for the project. - Impact: ensure impac ASAP and at the same time ensure satisfied stakeholders. The course will also work with change management and motivation. The course gives the students insight into and training in the use of tools, theories along with metods for analysing and dealing with challenges within project leadership.
Content: Leadership Flow Impact Leadership theory The workform are in groups. Each group has to complete a project report and each student has to elaborate a individual process report which form part in the complete assessment. Each student produce 3 indivduel videos regarding effect, flow and leadership
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have an understanding of methods and tools within Leadership, Flow, Impact and project management, and must be able to reflect on their use in practise while using correct terminology. - Apply and reflect on experience from internship in a project context. - Discuss, develop and adapt chosen theories and methods to own management practise, whithin project leadership - Apply presentation technique in connection with project meeting with peers - Plan own project trom start to end (use of project libre or similar) - Identify and categorize challenges within leadership within own case and possible solutions - Identify and categorize challenges within flow within own case and possible solutions - Identify and categorize challenges within impact within own case and possible solutions
62211:
Name English: Business Science and Technology Management
Danish Title: Forretningsvidenskab og teknologiledelse
General Course Objectives: The general purpose of the course is to help the student understand relevant technologies and technology trends in order to identify strategic business problems and challenges, as well as apply analytical approaches in order to contribute to sustainable business development, including Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) assessments. The point of the departure for the course cases is the students' internship experiences and current business challenges.
Content: Understanding how a company can assess their technology management in order to respond to rapidly changing customer demands and develop new product and market opportunities. This course aims to give the student insight and knowledge about technology as a source of competitive advantage and growth for companies. Subject areas include: Systems Thinking Technology management as a dynamic capability Identifying innovation needs Customer-centric strategy development and Voice of the Customer Ambidextrous Organization and organizational design and development Team structure, leadership, and management Collaboration strategies outside of the organization Decision making and learning Conscious Capitalism (people, planet, profit) Environmental, Societal, and Governance (ESG) metrics
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand opportunities and challenges technology affords - Identify and evaluate alternative and emerging technologies in light of business strategy and impact on the environment and society (ESG) - Understand the importance of technology acquisition, management, and exploitation in business development - Understand the role of absorptive capacity in creating technological competencies - Analyze how to decrease the time to market of new products and services through effective identification and exploitation of technologies that provide competitive advantage - Analyze organizational models for implementing technological innovation strategy - Understand the role of technology management in knowledge and expertise protection, as well as understand potential collaboration forms with other firms - Evaluate value analysis as an engineering tool and a strategy tool in innovation management - Involving customers and suppliers in the product development process
62212:
Name English: General business: introduction to marketing and international business
Danish Title: Forretningsforståelse: introduktion til markedsføring og international business
General Course Objectives: To develop students’ understanding of the role of marketing in a firm and the environmental forces, domestic and international, which inevitably influence a company’s business. Through an understanding of marketing management's basic theories, terminology, and methodologies, students should gain a clear understanding of the models used in decision making to solve problems and address challenges that companies face. This course emphasizes the understanding of a market orientation; that all company activities start with customers and their needs, including Corporate Social Responsibility (CSR) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) metrics.
Content: Introduction to marketing management: key concepts and nomenclature Marketing environment analysis (global trends, customers, competitors, PESTLE) Problem formulation and methodology in product development Introduction to marketing research design Value proposition and buyer behavior, particularly B2B Core competency and strategy Industry and Stakeholder analyses Distribution, value chains, pricing Relationship marketing and communication
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Demonstrate a solid comprehension of the most important concepts, terms, and theories in the marketing environment - Reflect and discuss the role of marketing in the firm - To understand customer needs and marketing’s role in product and business development - Present solution suggestions in order to analyze a specific problem by applying marketing theories and models - Apply the fundamental theories, models, and methods in marketing to inform strategy as well as tactical and operational challenges - To be able to methodically analyze a market, domestic and international, including the competitive landscape, and choose appropriate marketing strategies and activities - Apply marketing research methods and techniques - Understand and craft problem statements in a business development context
62213:
Name English: Managerial economics and project management
Danish Title: Erhvervsøkonomi og projektstyring
General Course Objectives: Managerial economics To develop the students' ability to apply economics theory in analyzing specific situations of company decision-making as well as provide one or more suggestions for potential solutions. The student should also be able to choose and apply specific models that best fit a given situation and give reasons for model choice and why it is particularly applicable. Name English: International Business
Danish Title: International Business
General Course Objectives: The goal is for the student to identify the complexity (changed conditions) a company faces in a marketing, economic and cultural perspective when exporting to the BtB market. International marketing provides methods for assessing the company's potential for export on the international market. The focus is on internationalization methods and strategy, which will enable the student to carry out analyzes that form the basis for the choice of market and the development of business models. This must also enable the student to assess opportunities / limitations on the international. To provide students with basic knowledge of economics - the influence of international economics on companies' market opportunities. Enable them to understand the impact of globalization not only on business but also on society. To give students an understanding of how economic policy directly impacts both nations and companies and their competitiveness and thus market opportunities. The aim is, that the student gains knowledge of how to interact culturally intelligently in complex, international and intercultural contexts, e.g. intercultural meetings with customers, suppliers, project managers, co-workers and management. Furthermore, emphasis is placed on enabling the student to understand and apply relevant theories in practice, as well as to understand the significance of his / her own cultural background for an intercultural interaction. The 17 world goals will be included in the teaching.
Content: International marketing: the purpose is to give the student insight and knowledge about the use of macro, meso and micro tools in connection with international market analysis, as well as assessment of the company's international competitiveness. The focus will be on the individual markets, where the goal is to assess the sales and sales potential of the company. The student must be able to analyze the individual markets and relate critically and constructively to the opportunities / challenges that arise when exporting, and from there make decisions about the attractiveness of the market. Subject areas included in the teaching are: -internationalization -company's international competitiveness -market selection process -development of business strategy We will work with sustainability, innovation, distribution, Intellectual property rights, relationship marketing and digitalisation, including CRM, databases, Big Data, IoT, Social media and other relevant tools. International economy: The national economy is rich in conflicts about what resources should be used and how to manage them; and the whole world is in the sign of change. Economic theory can give students a relevant understanding of the decision-making on which political choices are made. The national accounts, including GDP, GNI, BVT and BFI, are reviewed and, by extension, a number of macroeconomic indicators. Competitiveness, from an international perspective, is a key issue for understanding each company's international market opportunities. The UN's 17 World Goals are reviewed and integrated into an integrated consideration of the impact on national economic and political conditions. Method considerations for use in project work are focused on secondary and primary sources as well as quantitative and qualitative methods. Cultural understanding and intercultural communication: The course provides an introduction to the academic theories and concepts in culture, cultural understanding/​management, intercultural communication, the importance of language and cultural intelligence. Furthermore, an introduction to negotiation, negotiation strategies and the complexity of negotiations is given in an intercultural perspective. The teaching is based on practice, i.e. understanding, use and analysis of concrete cases, exercises, experiments, marketing campaigns, negotiations, video conferencing, etc.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Demonstrate an overview of the subjects and terms in international marketing finance and culture - Use the terminology of international marketing, finance and culture correctly - Identify and use analytical models in international marketing, finance and culture - Explain the different marketing theories and concepts and be able to apply them in the right context. - Develop marketing strategies on international markets and assess the consequences - Explain the most common economic models and key figures - Explain the general principles of price formation and interest arbitrage within and outside the EU. - Explain the influence of national and international economies on business and business opportunities - Explain the leading international economic policy and its consequences, including the importance of competitiveness - Understand and account for academic theories, concepts and variables within cultural understanding and intercultural communication - Apply cultural theories and concepts in practice - Understand and analyze negotiations, select appropriate negotiation strategies, and explain and relate to the complexity of intercultural negotiations
