62416:
Name English: Advanced Mobile Application Development
Danish Title: Videregående mobilapplikationsudvikling
General Course Objectives: Equip students with the skills to develop and deploy mobile applications that meet current technical standards and provide high-quality, user-centered experiences, including evaluation and emerging technologies.
Content: ● Human-centered design guidelines for touch-based mobile platforms ● Gesture- and touch-based interactions and implementation principles ● Context-aware and ubiquitous interaction concepts (location, sensors, adaptive behavior) ● Visual and interaction design: graphics, animations, and feedback for smooth and usable interfaces ● Responsive design: adapting user interfaces to different screen sizes and orientations ● Prototyping and using Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) or cloud backends ● Network communication, caching strategies, and handling intermittent connectivity ● Mobile application evaluation: usability testing, empirical methods, surveys, and analytics ● Quality assurance: testing strategies, crash monitoring, and iterative improvement Optional topics based on student interests: ○ Security on mobile platforms ○ XR / immersive interaction techniques ○ Advanced mobile optimization and performance techniques
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze and evaluate mobile application designs, identifying functional and non-functional requirements with attention to usability, accessibility, and user experience. - Apply human-centered interaction principles, including touch, gesture, and context-aware interactions, in the design and implementation of mobile applications. - Design and implement effective mobile application architectures that support performance, scalability, and secure communication with backend services. - Integrate cloud-based or third-party backend solutions, and manage network communication, caching, and offline functionality. - Create responsive, visually engaging, and user-friendly mobile interfaces through the application of interaction, animation, and feedback principles. - Apply empirical evaluation methods—such as user testing, surveys, or analytics—to assess usability and inform iterative design improvements. - Optimize mobile applications for performance, responsiveness, and energy efficiency in real-world usage contexts. - Deploy and maintain mobile applications, monitor usage and crashes, and apply quality assurance practices. - Understand and address challenges related to emerging mobile technologies, including XR, context-aware computing, and ubiquitous interaction.
62417:
Name English: Mobile Application Development with Swift
Danish Title: Mobil applikationsudvikling med Swift
General Course Objectives: The objective of the course is to provide the skills required to develop applications in Swift. The student should acquire an understanding of the major concepts, fundamental design patterns and best practices in mobile application development.
Content: Swift Xcode App architecture design patterns Creating user interfaces Declarative UI - SwiftUI Handling touch events and gestures Tabbars and navigation controllers Persistence Core Data Networking and asynchronous programming Localization and internationalization Background execution Testing and debugging
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Design and implement apps in Swift. - Use the appropriate frameworks. - Implement user interfaces conforming to guidelines. - Use and explain relevant design patterns. - Use and explain app architectural patterns. - Consider device and localization variations. - Implement testing. - Assess and discuss the quality of an app.
62418:
Name English: Processing of Biomedical Signals
Danish Title: Biomedicinsk signalbehandling
General Course Objectives: Biomedical systems are to a high degree based on, among other things, the measurement and analysis of physiological data. The aim of the course is to introduce basic analysis methods and their application to typical physiological signals, such as ECG, EEG, and speech signals.
Content: Physiological signals, e.g. temperature, blood pressure, pulse rate, oxygen saturation, electrocardiogram, electromyogram, electroencephalogram, and speech signals. A physiological measuring and analysis system consisting of analog sensors, amplifiers, filters, A/D conversion as well as analysis and presentation of the analysis result. Stocastic signals, probability density function, mean, variance, stationarity, white noise, Gaussian noise, auto-correlation, cross-correlation, detection of signals in Gaussian noise. Spectral analysis using Discrete Fourier Transform, window functions, time/frequency analysis (spectrogram). Design of digital filters and application of these for noise reduction and estimation of specific signal components from physiological signals. Use of Matlab as a simulation tool to aid the learning process.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe and apply principles for the design of a biomedical analysis system, including the concepts of mesurement, amplification, A/D conversion, sampling, aliasing, and quantization of signals. - Explain the basic representation of continuous and discrete, deterministic and stocastic signals, and the application of these. - Explain correlation and its application. - Explain and apply spectral analysis. - Explain and apply methods for time/frequency analysis (spectrogram) and the application of these. - Describe digital filters in terms of: difference equation, impulse response, convolution, and frequency response. - Design digital filters in terms of a set of appropriate specification parameters; use e.g. Matlab functions to implement these filters. - Apply digital filters for reduction of noise and extraction of parameters from physiological signals. - Use simulation tools, e.g. Matlab. - Communicate health technology issues in both written and oral forms.
62419:
Name English: System and Network Security - Project
Danish Title: System- og netværkssikkerhed - Projekt
General Course Objectives: Focus is development/deployment and evaluation of advanced security principles/solutions within computer system, embedded system, LAN, cyberspace, Internet of Things, and/or cloud domains - depending on chosen project. You should become able to evaluate security principles/solutions within domain of your chosen project and deploy, perhaps development, security principles/solutions in this domain. Results shall be presented in an English article formatted for a conference or journal as target, 8-12 pages long.
Content: Development/deployment and evaluation of advanced security principles/solutions within computer system, embedded system, LAN, cyberspace, Internet of Things, and/or cloud domains; writing an English article.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Evaluate advanced security principles/solutions within chosen domain - Develop and/or deploy advanced security principles/solutions within chosen domain - Detailed knowledge about security principles/solutions within chosen domain - Detailed knowledge about security attacks within chosen domain - Knowledge about standards within chosen domain - Knowledge about available products within chosen domain - Describe and analyse a full system with respect to security and possible attacks - Understand and analyse articles within the problem domain - Document a project on advaned security principles/solutions in an article in English with a conference or journal as target
62420:
Name English: Information technology 1
Danish Title: Informationsteknologi 1
General Course Objectives: To introduce the student to microcomputers and their use for modeling of specific problems. The course focuses on the modeling of systems consisting of sensors, controllers, and similar components.

System development: - Introduction to the Unified Process. UML: - Class diagrams - Activity diagrams - Sequence diagrams Basics: - Introduction to computer hardware. - Introduction to digital representation of information.

62422:
Name English: Bio-medical electronics 1
Danish Title: Medicoteknik 1
General Course Objectives: The overall objective is to provide students with an introduction to the basic problems of electronic circuits as well as an introduction to their use in transforming human physiological parameters to detectable electrical measurements and useful signals.
Content: Basic component knowledge Circuit analysis Digital electronics. Number systems and codes. Basic digital functions and numeric concepts. Boolean algebra. A/D and D/A conversion Microcontrollers Sensors Exercises with analysis software Laboratory exercises
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use correct terminology - Explain the basic models of electric circuits - Explain operation of basic digital components - Explain the basic rules of D/A and A/D conversion - Explain the structure of programs to a microcontroller - Implement simple programs for a microcontroller - Demonstrate understanding of the use of electronic measuring instruments - Explain the issues related to biomedical measurement technique - Use analysis software for circuit analysis
62423:
Name English: Semester project 1 Healthcare technology
Danish Title: Semesterprojekt 1 Sundhedsteknologi
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide students with practical experience in • planning and implementation of a monitoring program for biological parameters in subjects • developing software to collection and analysis of measurement data • analysing the obtained measurements. • explaining the physiological processes that cause the measurements carried out in the practical part
Content: Planning of the monitoring program carried out by all members of each project team. Development of simple software for the analysis of measured data. Preparation of a project report per project team.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe the heart and relevant vessels and other anatomical structures with the correct Latin names - Explain the physiological processes that cause the measurements carried out in the practical part - Explain how a measurement program is planned and implemented - Understand the structure and use a measuring system for measuring the pulse - Perform laboratory measurements on sensor(s) - Develop, test, and use a simple program for collection and transfer of measurement data from the sensors to the computer - Develop, tes,t and use a simple program for analysis of data from the planned measurement program - Plan and prepare a project report with results from the monitoring program
62426:
Name English: Cyber defence and legal aspects
Danish Title: Cyber defence og ledelsesansvar
General Course Objectives: In this course, the catagorization of information with CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability) will take place. The course also addresses the security responsibilities of the company towards customers and authorities. The course has a holistic approach to information security and risk management. All employees are requested to work with cyber defense - not just individual employees. The course will systematize the cyber defense work. Danish law (the Privacy Act) is reviewed as well as privacy principles. Also discussed is EU privacy regulation. The upcoming EU legislation GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation), which includes a regulation and directive is reviewed carefully. GDPR must be fully implemented in 2018.
Content: - Cyber Security Framework (NIST) - CIA - Legislation (cyber related) - Audit - GDPR
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Develop a cyber security mission / vision in organizations - Know, understand and use danish and EU cyber security legislation - Develop a risk management program in a chosen organization - Know, understand, explain and use catagorization of security - Know, understand and explain CIA (confidentiality, integrity, availability) - Know, understand and use privacy principles and protect personal data - Identify security risks in an orgnization - know, understand and use the Cyber Security Framework (NIST) - Suggest and apply methods for security audits
62427:
Name English: Network Defense and attack handling
Danish Title: Netværksforsvar og angrebshåndtering
General Course Objectives: The course covers the principles of defense / attacks based on various NIST (National Institute of Standards and Technology) directions. In addition, the course has a review of legislation and implementation of the vision / mission related to the course Cyber defense and management responsibilities The course also covers threats and vulnerabilities, malware and recommended cryptographic solutions with reference to the course "selection of cryptographic solutions" The course also addresses safety guidelines for data during transport, storage and processing. Intrusion Preventing System (IPS) and Metasploit are introduced as well as Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS) and setting up firewalls. Finally, principles around the recovery of data and security audit and evaluation are introduced.
Content: • IDS • IPS • Metasploit • Firewalls
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - know the legislation in cyber security - know, understand, and explain the threats to a system - know, understand, explain, and apply anti-malware - know, understand, explain, and apply the most common used cryptographic algorithms - know, understand, and apply IDS - be able to identify security risks in a system - know, understand, and apply IPS - work with a firewall in operation - suggest methods for the recovery of data and perform security audit
62428:
Name English: Secure implementation of systems
Danish Title: Sikker implementation af systemer
General Course Objectives: When the company must secure data in transit and storage, it is important to choose a safe and sufficiently fast cryptographic algorithm. In order to make a sensible choice, it is necessary to know the most commonly used algorithms. It is also important to create a secure network and databases. It is also necessary to work with strategic planning in cyber security. The course provides an overview of secure network architecture and data storage as well as the most commonly used security algorithms. The course introduces to symmetric and asymmetric algorithms and ECC (Elliptic Curve Cryptography). In addition, the course reviews HASH algorithms and the use of digital signatures. The course covers the most commonly used security protocols (Diffie-Hellman key distribution, Kereberos, X.509, PgP SSL/TLS). The course also contains implementation of backup systems and use of honeypots. The course uses Cybersecurity Framework from NIST. This framework is used to identify security risks and create protection strategies as well as strategies to detect cyber security events in the system.
Content: - Secure system design - Cyber Security Framework (NIST) - Cyber riscs and response - Documentation of security
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Design a secure system - Document the secuirty in the system - Know, understand, explain, and apply the Cyber Security framework (NIST) - Know, understand, and explain the most used cryptographic algorithms - Reflect on the cryptographic algorithms used in a system - Identify security risks in a system - Describe methods for securing networks and databases - Argue for the choice of protective strategies - Reflect on how to respond on a given security incident
62429:
Name English: Data visualization and analysis - tools and methods.
Danish Title: Data visualisering og analyse - værktøjer og metoder.
General Course Objectives: The course objective is to provide the student the understanding of a selection of data types and their distributions and how they can be visualized and analyzed using open source tools. Furthermore it is the objective to understand and apply methods for estimation of the mean, variance, spread, confidence interval, and regression of a data set targeting the application in a statistical model for hypothesis test. Finally the course objective is the introduction to fundamental concepts in cluster analysis and classification of data sets. The mathematical models are introduced through the application of open source tools and hands-on examples.
Content: Continuous, ordinal, and categorial datatypes; scatterplot; histogram; boxplot; Quantile-Quantile plot; 3D plot; probability distribution, continuous and discrete; uniform-, binomial- and normal distribution; estimation mean value, spread; CLT; confidence interval; linear regression; hypothesis test, H0, H1; cluster analysis; classification; R; RStudio; hands-on.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand datatypes: continuous, ordinal, categorial. - Understand and apply data visualization, including plot, scatterplot, histogram, boxplot, Quantile-Quantile plot, 3D plot with user defined view. - Understand probability and probability distribution, continuous, and discrete. - Understand and apply discrete probability distributions, uniform, binomial. - Understand and apply the normal distribution. - Understand and apply estimation of mean, varians, spread of a data set. - Understand the Central Limit Theorem (CLT). - Understand and apply confidence interval for mean value and confidence interval for difference between means. - Understand and apply linear regression. - Understand and apply a hypothesis test as a basis for statistical analysis. - Understand and apply introductory concepts in cluster analysis. - Understand and apply introductory concepts in classification.
62434:
Name English: Applied cryptography
Danish Title: Anvendt kryptografi
General Course Objectives: The module reviews the latest and most widely used algorithms within public key cryptography and private key cryptography (symmetric key cryptography). Additionally, the most commonly used MAC (Message Authentication Code) is reviewed. The module enables the student to evaluate how secure the individual algorithms are against attack. In addition, the student will be able to build entire cryptographic systems within the above areas. Also, the course introduces standard implementations of cryptographic solutions.
Content: - Public – private key cryptography - Symmetric algorithms - Hash algorithms - MAC - Authentication
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - describe the most widely used algorithms in public key cryptography - describe the most widely used algorithms in symmetric key cryptography - describe the relationship between the various cryptographic systems - describe relevant theoretical methods - describe public key and private key cryptographic solutions - describe authentication principles and the use of hash functions - implement a public key and a private key cryptographic system - implement a MAC solution - test cryptographic systems for security - analyse the need for cryptographic solutions - make necessary decisions in relation to implementation of cryptographic solutions on the basis of relevant analyses and evaluations - document the security of a cryptographic system
62437:
Name English: Advanced Mobile Application Development  w./ project
Danish Title: Videregående mobilapplikationsudvikling m./projekt
General Course Objectives: To implement and deploy applications for mobile devices where the user interface and overall quality meets or exceeds current standards in the field. To lead the experienced developer up on a professional level
Content: • Design Guidelines on leading touch-based mobile platforms (iOS, Android) • Gesture-based actions and their implementation • Implementation and optimization of graphics for smooth display of animations and visual feedback • Responsive design - user interfaces that adapt to the screen size • Use of 3rd party libraries for visual and non-visual components • Prototyping and using BaaS - Backend as a Service • Security on mobile platforms - encryption, including HTTPS with certificate pinning, obfuscation, de-obfuscation • Caching of network responses and handling of fluctuating network access • Quality assurance - testing, crash statistics, test reports, usability testing Additional subjects according to participant interests

62443:
Name English: Data Communication
Danish Title: Datakommunikation
General Course Objectives: To establish an in depth understanding of the internet and LANs network principles and to learn methods for protocol analyses and establishment of communication between machines and applications. The course gives the foundation for further studies/courses related to computer networks.
Content: Overview: Computer networks and the Internet Application Layer: Protocols for commonly used applications, such as WWW, email, DNS, etc. and the socket paradigm Transport Layer: TCP and UDP, service attributes Network Layer: IPv4, IPv6, ICMP, NAT, Routers and Routing Algorithms Data Link Layer: Ethernet, Switches, error detection and correction Wireless: WiFi, Cellular Security: Encryption principles, firewalls Sustainability (energy consumption)
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Define concepts like protocol, protocolstack, congestion and flow control, fragmentation, addressing forms and multiplexing /de-multiplexing - Describe mainstream network components like routers, switches, acces point, firewalls and their use - Describe services provided by the key protocols and explain the connection to protocol / protocol header as well as relate to adjacent protocol layer services - Describe Wireless networks such as WiFi and Cellular - Use FSM-diagrams and sequence diagrams to analyse a protocol - Describe the most important types of encryption for data communication security - Use tools like wireshark etc. for network traffic analysis - Use fundamental socket-programming - Discus and evaluate the use of a) addressing forms, b) forward error correction versus error detection, c) stability of routing algorithms, d) explicit and implicit congestion control, e) available standards for local area networks (wired as wireless), f) implications on higher protocol layers of the NAT protocol, g)IP4 versus IP6 and h) Push versus Pull technologies
62444:
Name English: Data visualization and analysis - project
Danish Title: Data visualisering og analyse - projekt
General Course Objectives: The course objective is the application of open source data acquisition and analysis tools on a given problem and demonstrate and document a practical application per project group. Examples on problem areas might be analysis of dataflow from social media, from sensor measurements e.g. captured via Arduino processor, off-line analysis of data, etc. At the first course session, with all project participants, project groups are formed where each group is focusing on a specific problem. The set of problems addressed is selected at the first course session with all participants. During the 3-weeks projekt period the groups present project status at project seminars. The course is finalized with a seminar where the project group projects are presented and the handed in. The tools typically applied are R, RStudio, RStudioCloud, Python, Google CoLab, LaTeX and Beamer (LaTeX tool for presentations) in a laptop or cloud environment. The project seminars will be using Beamer and the final project documentation will be carried out using LaTeX.
Content: Identify problem area, which apply data visualization and/or analysis tools. Identify datatypes. Identify visualization/analysis tools. Specify, design, implement and validate solution. Identify processes, required by a system in normal operation. Documentation of system in LaTeX and present the system using LaTeX Beamer.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify a problem area which uses open source data visualization and/or analysis tools using at least a data clustering or classifications tool. - Identify, understand, and explain one scientific paper, on a clustering or classification method of relevance to the problem at hand. - Identify at least three relevant visualization/analysis models for the problem at hand, and compare their expected properties in relation to the problem at hand, including their required computational and storage resources. - Identify the necessary visualization/analysis tools of relevance to the problem at hand. - Specify and design a visualization/analysis system using one of the models identified. - Implement the visualization/analysis system solution preferably targeting the R language and/or Python in a laptop or cloud environment. - Verify and demonstrate the visualization/analysis system. - Identify and describe the processes needed for a visualization/analysis system applied in routine operation for the problem at hand. - Document the system in a report using LaTeX and prepare and present the report at the concluding seminar using laTeX Beamer.
62445:
Name English: Advanced Internet Technology
Danish Title: Avanceret Internetteknologi
General Course Objectives: The course Advanced Internet Technology works with implementation of .NET services on the Internet. The course teaches the latest technologies in the field of active .NET solutions on the Internet with the use of databases and the like. The course introduces to advanced graphic user interfaces, sessions and general state management. Also covered is advanced Caching principles. Content: Contents: • .NET based Internet Solutions • The application of databases in .NET based Internet solutions • Handling of security vulnerabilities in .NET based web solutions • WCF Web Services
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - set up .NET based web servers - implement advanced graphical user interfaces - build secure web solutions - create WCF Web Services - implement .NET based web application with database - perform a security test on a web application - test a .NET based application and issue a test report - develop a larger web application using databases - document the functionality and security of a .NET based application based on tests
62450:
Name English: Information technology 2
Danish Title: Informationsteknologi 2
General Course Objectives: The course aims to provide students with foundational competencies in object-oriented software development, including database integration, concurrency, graphical user interfaces, and basic user-centered design and evaluation.
Content: Object-Oriented Programming: - Object-oriented principles: encapsulation, inheritance, polymorphism, abstraction - Class design and responsibility assignment - UML class diagrams and object relationships - Introduction to error handling and exceptions Databases: - Introduction to relational databases and basic database design - Use of SQL (CRUD operations, simple joins) - Integration of databases into object-oriented applications Concurrency: - Introduction to threads - Communication and synchronization between threads - Typical use cases in application development Graphical User Interfaces: - Development of graphical user interfaces (GUI) - Event-driven programming - Separation of UI logic and application logic User-Centered Design & Evaluation - Introduction to usability and user experience (UX) - Basic principles of user interface design - User-centered design process - Introduction to evaluation methods

62452:
Name English: Bio-medical electronics 2
Danish Title: Medicoteknik 2
General Course Objectives: The overall objectives are to provide the students with an introduction to issues regarding transformation of physiological parameters to detectable and usable electrical measurements and signals.
Content: • Capacitors and inductors • Frequency analysis and filters • Operational amplifiers • Biopotential amplifier • Medical measurement techniques • The physiological interface • Metrological specifications • Metrological sources of error • Measurable physiological parameters • Electrical safety
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use correct terminology - Analyse resistive circuits - Explain and analyse circuits with capacitors and inductors - Calculate the transfer function of simple dynamic circuits - Describe the ideal operational amplifier - Analyse circuits with ideal operational amplifiers - Build an electronic circuit for measuring a physiological parameter - Establish electrical equivalency circuits for simple physiological parameters
62453:
Name English: Semester Project 2 Healthcare technology
Danish Title: Semesterprojekt 2 Sundhedsteknologi
General Course Objectives: The overall course objective is to provide students with practical experience in: • Analysing a biological organ as electrophysical measuring object • Analysing, design, development, test and use of an electronic measuring system for measuring a biological signal • Collecting, analysing and presenting measurement data from a patient simulator and test subject
Content: The project begins with an analysis of the heart as an electrophysiological measurement object, including ECG signal generation, voltage levels in given derivations and frequency content. Further, the most common sources of noise when recording an ECG are studied. The ECG signal as a tool for the diagnosis of heart diseases is then studied with examples. Working with a ECG measurement system comprising: electrodes, amplifier, filter, A/D conversion and transmission of data from a microcontroller to a PC. PC software for obtaining, analysing, and presenting the recorded ECG data, is developed. Measure ECG signals recorded from subjects and conduct preliminary analysis of these signals e.g. calculate heart rate, timings etc.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain cardiac physiology - Account for heart disease that can be diagnosed using ECG data - Analyse the heart as an electrophysiological measurement object - Explain the function of a biopotential amplifier - Perform verification measurements on a biopotential amplifier - Explain the advantages and disadvantages of patient (ECG) simulator - Explain a measurement system for measuring ECG signals - Collect, analyse and present ECG data using software developed in the course
62454:
Name English: Healthcare Science 2
Danish Title: Sundhedsvidenskab 2
General Course Objectives: To give the student knowledge and understanding of human anatomy, physiology, pathology, pathophysiology and pharmacology
Content: Anatomy and Physiology Basic understanding of the body • Renal structure and function • Digestive organs including Hepar / Pancreas (enzymes) • craniums anatomy • CNS/PNS • Endocrinology Pathology, Pathophysiology and Pharmacology Pathology • Diseases of digestive organs, including Hepar/Pancreas • Renal and urinary disorders • Disorders of locomotor apparatus • Ischemic heart disease including hypertension • Oncology • Diabetes types 1 and 2 Pharmacology • General pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and pharmacodynamics • Special Pharmacology relating to the above exemplary diseases
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the theory of biochemical processes at the cellular and systemic level - Explain selected parts of the human body's anatomy, structure, and function - Explain the theory of physiological processes in the healthy human - Explain selected problems associated with normal loads and selected disease states with knowledge of biochemistry, anatomy, and physiology - Explain the general pathophysiological mechanisms - Describe selected diseases and describe subjective and objective symptoms - Explain selected measurable anatomical and physiological parameters' relevance and importance - Explain the general pharmacology
62484:
Name English: Semester project 3 Healthcare technology
Danish Title: Semesterprojekt 3 Sundhedsteknologi
General Course Objectives: The project is divided into the following three objectives: 1. To plan the development of and user guides for a prototype for a healthcare IT system. 2. To construct a prototype of a monitoring system with the aim of providing an overview of physiological parameters estimated from patient data. 3. To argue for the healthcare aspects of the design, development and evaluation of the IT system and the patient monitor. The course contributes to the green transition by enabling the students to make software systems, that may contribute to optimizing resources and reducing waste.
Content: The project is documented in a report.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - develop a protocol for exchanging information between IT systems for healthcare use. - design and develop a monitoring system which analyses data from a patient. - verify the correct operation of the monitoring system using simulated patient data. - apply signal processing methods to analyze and process a biomedical signal and estimate physiological parameters - develop user guides for a healthcare IT system for all involved user groups - apply and argue for healthcare considerations in relation to the design, development and evaluation of a healthcare IT system - apply target group analysis for optimization of development, design, implementation and evaluation of healthcare technology - identify psychological aspects affecting the use of healthcare technology - formulate and consider relevant ethical aspects of development of new health care technology
62501:
Name English: Linux Server and Network
Danish Title: Linux server og netværk
General Course Objectives: To give the student sufficient theoretical and practical understanding and knowledge to design and implement a local network, including a server of own choice, connected to the Internet using PCs and VM's running Linux as the platform for both workstations and servers. Also cloud administation and operation is discussed.
Content: Workstation installation - turn your laptop into a working Linux computer Linux usage: Users; file systems and file system structure; essential commands. Graphical desktops. Networks: Linux in a networking environment: Structure and configuration of the networking software. Build your own system: Install packages: From source code (tar, ./configure, make, make install) or package managers: dpkg, RPM etc. Basic security: threats, prevention, detection. 62505:
Name English: Introduction to embedded systems
Danish Title: Introduktion til indlejrede systemer
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is introduce the student to the construction of embedded systems focusing on microcontrollers, the function and programming of microcontrollersi and the connection of microcontrollers with input/output devices
Content: - Microcontrollers and I/O devices - Principles for communicating with peripheral devices via serial protocols or analog signals. - Interrupts and their use within program control. - Programming languages for embedded systems - Tools for program development and debugging.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Program and troubleshoot programs for microcontrollers - Understand how different types of inputs and outputs for an embedded system work and how to connect them to a microcontroller - Use multimeters and/or oscilloscopes to troubleshoot electrical circuits - Explain the principles of using digital controllers for reading analog and digital inputs and for controlling actuators - Design and implement embedded microprocessor programs - Apply the interrupt system as a mechanism for synchronization of hardware and software events - Use protocols to communicate with other computers or periperal devices - Use the hardware components of a microcontroller for programming - Use relevant development tools, simulators, and debuggers - Analyse, divide, and implement a larger hardware project within a group of 2 – 3 students
62512:
Name English: Telemedicine 1
Danish Title: Telemedicin 1
General Course Objectives: Telemedicine systems use IT technology for communication of measurements, analysis of patient physiological data, and communication between health care professionals and patients. The course aims to introduce students to a telemedicine system used in clinical practice including the technologies that are needed to set up the system and enable the student to plan a telemedicine system that connects a patient, for example at home, with a remote medical facility.
Content: - Telemedicine applications for monitoring and treatment of chronic diseases. - National and international experience with telemedicine, e.g. "The Whole Demonstrator Project" in Britain. - Measuring the physiological parameters for clinical monitoring and treatment of patients having chronic diseases, e.g. COPD patients, diabetic patients and patients with heart failure: respiration, lung function, oxygen saturation, temperature etc. - Introduction to clinical decision support systems. - Wireless communication networks, antennas, modulation, communication channel, detection, bit-error rate, link budget. - Ad hoc short-range communication networks, minimizing energy consumption of communication networks, methods for harvesting energy, power levels in a variety of methods for energy harvesting. - Use of wireless WAN (Wide Area Networks), LAN (Local Area Networks), PAN (Personal area Networks) and BAN (Body Area Networks) for telemedicine and health technology. The course contributes to the green transition by enabling the students to develop solutions that reduce transportation and resource use.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the basic organisational and administrative principles of the Danish health-care system. - Explain the medical/physiological principles for establishing a telemedicine system for a given patient group. - Analyse the organizational and economic aspects of establishing a telemedicine system for a given patient group having a chronic disease. - Design and prototype a telemedicine system for a given patient group. - Describe the principles of algorithms for the processing of clinical data which can be monitored by the patient. - Explain the function blocks in a digital wireless communication network, radio wave propagation, antenna principles, modulation and coding methods, including calculating a link budget for a given digital communication link. - Explain protocols for wireless communication and use examples of protocols for wireless communication, including wireless network cell structure. - Explain the principles of a short-range ad hoc communication network with minimal energy consumption. - Explain the principles of energy harvesting and the importance of minimising energy consumption. - Explain and apply the above principles when planning a telemedicine system, including identification of the system's personal safety-critical elements.
62514:
Name English: Object-oriented programming
Danish Title: Objektorienteret programmering
General Course Objectives: To learn the fundamental concepts and techniques in an object-oriented programming language used in industry (currently Java). The course has the main goal to enable students to design, implement, and test small applications. Requirements, analysis, design, testing, versioning, and quality control is used as an integrated part of the development process.
Content: The course covers - Fundamental programming concepts and techniques for the systematic development of simple programs. - Data types, classes, objects, lists, encapsulation, methods, parameters, constructors, file handling, inheritance, and polymorphism. - Object orientation: modeling, class structure, library classes, and interfaces. - Systematic development of simple programs: modularization, step refinement, incremental development, and test.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Define and describe commonly occurring concepts and mechanisms in an object oriented programming language. - Use the Java object-oriented programming language and associated class library to write programs. - Understand and use data structures and class definitions. - Read, understand, and modify small programs. - Use object-oriented analysis, design, and implementation to solve practical programming problems. - Apply a software development process, including requirement, analysis/design, implementation, and testing. - Test a software solution. - Explain the application of object oriented concepts in software solutions. - Discuss and assess the quality of solutions through consideration of issues such as encapsulation, cohesion, and coupling. - Use version control systems
62517:
Name English: Medical Imaging Systems
Danish Title: Billeddannende modaliteter
General Course Objectives: To provide the student with knowledge and understanding of clinical systems for medical imaging, as well as to assess the sources of error associated with imaging systems.
Content: Physical principles of clinical imaging systems; practical applications of imaging systems for clinical use, assessment of the causes of error in imaging systems for clinical use. Associating the above to X-ray, magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan, computer tomography (CT) scan, positron emission tomography (PET) scans, and ultrasound.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understanding the physical principles underlying the clinical imaging systems. - Understanding progress in the practical application of an imaging system for clinical use. - Assess sources of error in imaging systems for clinical use. - Link the principles of image formation, practical use, and evaluation of sources of error for X-ray images. - Link the principles of image formation, practical use, and evaluation of error sources of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). - Link the principles of image formation, practical use, and evaluation of error sources of the computer tomography (CT). - Link the principles of image formation, practical use, and evaluation of error sources of positron emission tomography (PET). - Link the principles of image formation, practical use, and evaluation of error sources of ultrasound.
62518:
Name English: Applied medical  statistics
Danish Title: Anvendt medicinsk statistik

Content: The course aims to enable students after implementation has achieved an understanding of and experience with the use of probability distributions, including binomial, Poisson and normal distribution; methods of sampling and statistical modeling of clinical data; methods for parameter estimation in the above probability distributions; methods of regression and correlation analysis; parametric and non parametric modeling of clinical data; probability distributions Chi-squared, F-distribution and t-distribution; significance level of 1 - and 2-side tests; principles for the establishment and application of the test in clinical data; open source software for statistical analysis of clinical data.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand probability distributions, including binomial, Poisson,. and normal distribution. - Understand and apply methods of sampling and statistical modelling of clinical data. - Understand and apply methods for parameter estimation in the above probability distributions. - Understand and apply methods for regression and correlation analysis. - Understand and apply parametric and non parametric modeling of clinical data - Understand probability distributions Chi-squared, F-distribution, and t-distribution. - Understand and apply significance level and 1 - and 2-side tests. - Understand and apply principles for the establishment and application of the test in clinical data. - Use open source software for statistical analysis of clinical data.
62521:
Name English: Design-build project
Danish Title: Design-build projekt
General Course Objectives: In Design-build project students will design and develop their own medical device concept based on the needs of the patient and the market situation. A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to analyse, evaluate, and specify requirements for a medical device following the standards and regulations of medical device development. In addition, they will learn how to make mock-ups, minimal viable products, and apply different brainstorming techniques. Finally, students will work in groups to implement the project and will be able to plan, implement, and operate the services required for having a medical device on the market.
Content: In Design-build project students will design and develop their own medical device concept based on the needs of the patient and the market situation. The course span the 13- and 3-week period. In the 13-week period students will follow lectures and develop their own medical device concept. In the 3-week period students will implement a prototype of the medical device concept alongside writing a report which describes the concept, the theory behind it, and “sells” it.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - analyse and assess the need for product, process, or system in health care - specify a product, process, or system in health care - specify a product, process, or system in health care, taking into account the standards in the health care sector - specify a product, process, or system in health care, taking sustainability into account - specify a product, process, or system, taking the economic constraints into account - plan the design of a product, the implementation of a product or system, taking into account work done in a project group with several participants - perform the design of a product, the implementation of a product or system, using project management tools - analyse, specify, and implement a plan for the operation of the product, process, or system, taking into account financial, sustainability, and standards in the health care sector - demonstrate an overall project process that allows the transfer of product, process, or system
62523:

62524:

Danish Title: Signalbehandling

62527:
Name English: Big Data
Danish Title: Big data
General Course Objectives: Systematic collection, purification, storage and analysis of data, and reporting and the ability to respond and act on them - have the potential to transform the business in many companies. Classic disciplines such as data mining and data warehousing based on pre-defined data formats and database schemas that do not extend when data volumes are very large, heterogeneous, inconsistent and varying information. Here you have to go beyond relational databases. Big Data is typically stored distributed and replicated in a cluster of machines controlled by Hadoop in the cloud or on their own servers.
Content: Data sets in multidimensional spaces; data outliers and data classification; applying R/Python for data visualization, analysis, clusteranalysis, classification and machine learning. Handling large amounts of data and calculations on them; scaling, Spark and Map-Reduce application in a big data environmernt.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understanding multidimensional datasets - Understanding of outliers and classification - Using R/Python for data processing and analysis - Data visualization with R/Python - Apply data classification and machine learning - Understand the data and command structure of and configure a Big Data environment - Use the necessary management tools in a Unix environment - Apply the Map-Reduce algorithm and associated tools
62530:
Name English: Network Security
Danish Title: Netværkssikkerhed

Network Security Applications: Authentication Applications, Electronic Mail Security, VPN/IPsec, Web-security, cloud security, wireless security. System Security: Intruders, Malicious Software, Firewalls, Intrusion Detection Systems, Security Policies.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the various threats, vulnerabilities, and attack methods as covered during the course - Describe the various classes of cryptographic algorithms and explain their relative properties - Explain the methods for authentication of people, network traffic, and systems in the covered security protocols and applications - Explain the application and interplay of the algorithms in the covered network security applications and protocols - Describe the function and application of network components and applications used for countering threats - Explain the interplay of network components, protocols and applications for countering threats and vulnerabilities to security - Describe the typical content and best practices in a company’s security policy - Design, realize and document a security solution in a network - Apply tools for analyzing and generating network traffic to study security protocols and to test, verify, and document the implemented solution
62531:
Name English: Development Methods for IT Systems
Danish Title: Udviklingsmetoder til IT-systemer

62532:

62547:

Danish Title: Indlejrede C/C++ smarte applikationer

62550:

Danish Title: Sikkerhed i indlejrede systemer
General Course Objectives: To provide a basic understanding of theory and practice in the construction of secure communication and integrity in embedded systems.
Content: Fundamental characteristics of secure communications in embedded systems: - Cryptographic Algorithms and Protocols (including Key Management and Lightweight Cryptography) - Important Safety Properties (including Confidentiality, Integrity, Availability, Authenticity and Privacy) - Authentication Mechanisms and Protocols - "Trusted Computing" (including concepts such as Trusted Platform Modules and Trust Zones) - Signed Software (including Signature Validation and Public Key Infrastructures) - Physical Security and Distribution of Elements in an Embedded System - Data Security (including Secure Data Storage - locally and in the Cloud - as well as Secure Data Reporting) - Sustainability (including a focus on minimal resource consumption)
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand how the architecture of an embedded system consisting of several components influences the determination of the security demands the system. - Describe important characteristics of cryptographic algorithms and protocols and their use when communicating between embedded systems. - Describe the fundamental safety characteristics: Confidentiality, Integrity and Availability, as well as the importance of these when communicating between embedded systems. - Catagorize different classes of mechanisms and protocols to authenticate communication between elements in an embedded system. - Explain the possible uses of "Trusted Computing" techniques and technologies in the construction of secure embedded systems. - Explain the importance of physical security in a given embedded system in order to identify the impact of physical distribution of the system's elements. - Analyzing an embedded system consisting of several components, in order to identify risks, threat models and attack models. - Choose an appropriate implementation paradigm to satisfy given design requirements for data security in an embedded system. - Develop an overall design of a security architecture for an embedded system based on the interfaces and communication protocols of selected elements. - Develop a partial implementation of the security architecture of an embedded system based on an informal description of the function and purpose of the system.
62577:
Name English: Data Communication
Danish Title: Datakommunikation
General Course Objectives: The Purpose of the course is to: - Understand fundamental principles of communication in computer networks - Understand the structure of the Internet and its protocols and make use of it - Establish communication between two hosts on a computer network - Understand security aspect in Intra- and Internet
Content: - The structure of the Internet and its protocol stack - Standards for Local Area Networks (LANs), advantages and disadvantages of different types of networks - Detection and correction of transmission errors - Network topologies and the solution of routing problems in already existing networks - Introduction to Socket Programming - Encryption principles, firewalls - Sustainabillity (energy consumption)
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe the 5 layers of the internet-protocol stack and describe which services they offer - Describe commonly used internet protocols with applications such as web, mail and DNS - Apply socket-interfaces in a practical setting - Describe the protocols on the netvwork layer, this includes IP-addressing and netmasks (CIDR) - Describe when unicast, multicast and broadcast is used - Establish and maintain a communication over the internet - Explain the differences between error-detection and error-correction - and which implementations/layers that use these - Describe the most important types of encryption (based on symmetric keys ad public/private keys) - Explain different usage scenarios for data networks, e.g., LAN, WAN, VPN - Describe relevant components of data networks, e.g., router, switch, firewall, and explain their functionality - Based on a requirements description for a data network choose and configure the right components to establish a data network and argue for the choice - Design and implement communication protocols for example TCP, UDP, FTP
62581:
Name English: IT and Computer Communication
Danish Title: IT og kommunikation
General Course Objectives: To provide the student with skills to analyse, develop, and configure multilayer - including network based - IT systems. Furthermore, the course provide the knowledge required for independent study of topics related to computer networks, data security, and distributed systems.
Content: - Introduction to IT Security. - Software architecture and design patterns. - Introduction to distributed systems. - Introduction to "markup" language, primarily HTML and XML. - Introduction to system maintenance and system configuration. - UML: Sequence and state diagrams. - Introduction to project management. - Basic architectures: Computer Networks and the Internet. - Application Layer: Relevant protocols, and socket programming. - Transport Layer: TCP and UDP. - Network Layer: IP, NAT, Routing Algorithms, and Routers. - Data Link layer: Ethernet, Bridges, Switches, and Hubs. The course contributes to the green transition by enabling the students to optimize a development process, reducing resource waste.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - apply the subject terminology correctly. - describe and explain relevant, commonly used software architectures. - describe and explain the most commonly used distribution techniques as well as the layer-separation and abstraction principles in a protocol stack. - describe and explain state diagrams and sequence diagrams and apply these for the definition of a protocol. - describe and explain data exchange using primarily text based marchalling methods and apply these for exchanging data using a programming language. - describe and explain installation and configuration of a system as well as commonly occurring security issues in connection with computer systems and computer networks. - describe and explain network components and the communication between computers over the Internet. - describe and explain methods and protocols in the Internet protocol stack, addressing on IP-based networks, and the use by a program of protocols in the application and transport layers. - apply the essential tools and methods for analysis of network traffic and problems. - develop configurable, layered applications that use files and communicates over a network. - compare methods and services used in the protocols in the TCP/IP protocol stack and assess the applicability of protocols for a specific purpose. - participate in a professional discussion in the subject area.
62582:
Name English: Complex Systems and Devops
Danish Title: Komplekse systemer og Devops
General Course Objectives: This course builds on, and extends version control and test methods (02315/62532) and either advanced programming (02324) or backend development / distributed systemes (62597/62596) and frontend web technology (02363). In the course you will learn to develop, integrate, deploy and maintain the various components in a larger IT-solution. As part of the course we will develop and deploy a turnkey web system. The course provides prerequisites to participate in a development team that uses the principles of DevOps and establish an infrastructure for a complete web based it-system. The course contributes to the green transition by enabling the students to develop and operate IT-solutions in an efficient manner, reducing waste of resources.
Content: Development of single page applications using a frontend framework. Progressive web-apps as an alternative to mobile applications. Handling frontend application-state with a state manager. Backend security using hashing, salting og tokens. Use of package managers til for versioning and integration. Use of build automation and containers for control of Continuous Integration and Development. Web-based Continuous Integration and Delivery. Embedded og Standalone Web Servers. Containerization systems as support for CI/CD DevOps. Optionally realtime web applications using publish-subscribe architecture.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Apply selected frameworks for frontend and backend development. - Explain and implement 'Application state' using a state manager. - Setup fundamental backend security and token based security. - Apply frameworks for development of complex systems. - Apply package managers - Setup continuous integration, test and delivery (CI/CD) - Apply containerization and setup build servers, PaaS and IIaaS - Understand DevOps and be able to engage effectively in a DevOps organisation
62583:
Name English: Programmering af embedded wireless systems and sensors
Danish Title: Programmering af Indlejrede trådløse systemer og sensorer
General Course Objectives: Students will be able to analyse, design and implement low-energy wireless sensor-networks connected to a cloud service on the internet. In focus is the Internet of Things (IOT) used for supporting one or more af the FN sustainable development goals. After participating, you should have got an understanding for - and can develop a wireless system on a modern operating system for real-time handling of microcontrollers with sensors
Content: Various network protocols for monitoring and controlling, for example. intelligent buildings and cities. Protocols like. ZigBee, Z-Wave, LoRa, Bluetooth low energy, Wifi Programming embedded system with Linux operating system and RTOS by using relevant programming languages ​​eg. C and C ++, Java scripts on node.js and / or Python. Embedded systems client servers by http or MQTT of Internet protocols for REST webservice. Programming of Wireless sensors that can measure physical data REST Web services and cloud services, for example. thingspeak.com
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe and apply one or more low power networking protocols (ex.Zigbee, Bluetooth low energy og Z-wave) used in e.g. intelligent homes, smart homes/buildings for monitoring and control - Analyse and design a given embedded system and suggest how it can be configured / programmed to run in low-energy mode. - Analyze, design, and implement a Linux embedded client server system on a given microcontroller using libraries for communicating with wireless sensors - Configure and apply a development system to modern parallelized systems including gaining experience in synchronizing parallel tasks - Configure an embedded linux operation system and install linux drivers/libraries - Program an embedded Linux system using the primary programming language C and C++ as evt. Java scripts on Node.js and Python - Program a linux embedded system with MQTT protocol for communication to a REST cloud server - Use or make a REST servise on a server as well request data for showing them on a web user interface - Participate in a discussion about security in computer systems - Document a system
62588:
Name English: Operating systems
Danish Title: Operativsystemer
General Course Objectives: The purpose of this course is to provide the background and the context for understanding the principles behind operating system design as well as a working knowledge and hands-on experience of how these principles are put into practice in current operating systems. The goal is that students will be able to write programs for current and future operating systems. The course also introduces to virtualization, multiprocessor systems and real-time operating systems.
Content: The course consists of a theoretical and an experimental component. The theoretical component consists of: - Operating system architecture - Processes, threads, IPC, and scheduling - Virtual memory – focusing on paged memory - Functionality and implementation aspects of file systems - I/O devices - Drivers - Virtualization - Multiprocessors and multicomputers The practical component consists of exercises and laboratory experiments designed to give the student a deeper practical knowledge of modern operating systems.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - explain the role of the operating system and how computer programs are executed. - explain the concept of layered software architectures and describe the internal structure of an operating system as a hierarchy of abstraction layers. - explain basic operating system concepts such as processes, threads, and scheduling and describe how the use of interrupts, dispatching, and context switching ('process dispatching') supports concurrency in an operating system. - describe and apply basic system commands and explain the role of a command interpreter (shell). - compare and contrast common algorithms for preemptive as well as non-preemptive scheduling and especially discuss such scheduling algorithms that are applicable for real-time purposes. - explain the concept of virtual memory and how it is realized in hardware and software. - explain the concept of I/O devices and the difference between using I/O instructions and memory mapped I/O for communicating with I/O devices. - compare and contrast different approaches to file system implementations, recognizing the strengths and weaknesses of each. - explain the functionality and application of virtual machines. - evaluate the suitability of an operating system for a specific computer system. - develop programs for various operating systems and perform simple extensions, such as device drivers of existing operating systems.
62589:
Name English: Business Intelligence
Danish Title: Business Intelligence
General Course Objectives: The increasing demand for information to create competitive advantages and optimize business processes has stimulated an increased use of Business Intelligence (BI), Analytics and Big Data. The goal of the course is to give students professional competences to identify information deliverables in a strategic context to innovate business processes, a basic understanding of the technology in use, and skills to develop a BI solution by using a spreadsheet (e.g. MS Excel) or other generally available BI-tool, e.g. Power BI or Tableau.
Content: The relationship between business strategies and use of information and maturity models. Business requirement specification and business case. How to create an information wheel and develop an information strategy. Overview of Business Intelligence and typical risk factors (pitfalls). Productions of information at the functional organizational level (lead and lag information). The competences and role of the analyst and reporting system. The main components of an information system. The difference between data, information and knowledge. Quantitative analytics, data mining and reporting. Data warehouse, ETL, data marts. The businesses acquisition of source data. Business Intelligence Competence Center (BICC). The BI software vendors and practical BI solutions. Case based project work and presentation. Developing your own BI solution by using Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or another BI tool.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand Business Intelligence as a holistic discipline with relationships from business strategy and source data. - Have basic knowledge of strategy and business development. - Explain the main elements in the process of a business requirements specification and business case methodology. - Demonstrate basic knowledge of relational databases and their purposes. - Explain typical architecture and IT infrastructure components in Business Intelligence solutions. - Explain the purpose of the architectural components in a data warehouse, data marts and typical data creating source systems in the business’s immediate environment. - Explain various analytical techniques that generate and deliver information for decision support and process improvement. - Develop an information strategy based on a company strategy at the cooperate or department level and identify relevant information deliverables to improve upon processes or start new business processes. - Identify and explain the most significant risk factors associated with information projects. - Develop and explain the plan and requirements specification for a business intelligence project. - Develop a Business Intelligence solution with Power BI, Tableau, Excel, or other BI tool, based on case material.
62597:
Name English: Backend development, operations and distributed Systems
Danish Title: Backendudvikling, drift og distribuerede systemer
General Course Objectives: To design, build, deploy and operate a modern backend for an app or website. To understand of theory and good practice in the construction of distributed systems.
Content: Architectures and design of modern backends as part of a distributed systems, such as client-server, Service oriented architectures (SOA), and web services, such as SOAP, JSON REST and GraphQL. Richardson's maturity model for a REST service. Architectures in web application development (HTML, Javascript, serverside and client side languages and their interaction) Best practices in modern backend development Managing concurrency issues in a backend The course is project-oriented and includes development of a distributed system of your choice, typically a backend and communication with a web page and an app. Client/server systems are often a primary technology driver in the context of sustainable systems, where these contribute to the logistics management of sustainable resources in a social, an economic and an environmental dimension. This sustainability angle is included implicitly in the learning objectives of the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - distinguish between different architectures in modern backends - use resource oriented protocols (such as REST) as client and server - understand method oriented protocols (such as SOAP) - understand transactions and transaction isolation in a distributed system - understand security aspects in a distributed system - develop an implementation of a distributed system - select and configure a suitable deployment platform and deploy a backend - distinguise between different container-based virtualization technologies, such as Docker, and modern server management - use operational monitoring on a distributed syste, - assess and integrate various backends as a service (BaaS) as part of a distributed system - assess the sustainability when choosing deployment platform backend
62598:
Name English: Artificial intelligence in computer games
Danish Title: Kunstig intelligens i computerspil
General Course Objectives: Strategic games are games with well defined rules for the course of the game, and a strategy for applying these rules with the purpose of winning. Examples are tic-tac-toe, checkers, and chess witch are so called perfect-information games, and games with chance ex. back-gammon. Strategic games serves as models for problem solving methods in computer science. Methods that are applied in engineering-tasks such as VLSI design, robot-navigation, jobshop-planning etc.
Content: Introduction to Artificial Intelligence. Problem solving by statespace search: We will analyse and implement algorithms to find a route through a maze, the shortest paths between cities, planning problems etc. Design and implementation of a game: We will learn how a computer plays chess, and we will implement our own chess-program or another game of your own choise. Game theory, algorithm analysis, data structures.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - - use and explain relevant fields of Artificial Intelligence: Game-theory, Heuristic search. - - evaluate the usability of these methods in a given problem. - - design and implement complex recursive algorithms. - - analyse performance and complexity. - - tune algorithms. - - document his work in writing. - - discuss his work in a debate. - - work in team-based projects.
62601:
Name English: Thermodynamics and Mechanics for Electrical Engineers
Danish Title: Termodynamik og Mekanik for elektroingeniører
General Course Objectives: To provide the students with knowledge of thermodynamics and mechanics and thus contribute to the building of the students basic knowledge, so that they can understand and participate with solutions of technical problems in the areas mentioned.
Content: Thermodynamics: • Basic thermodynamic systems • Thermodynamic states and parameters, heat and work • First law of thermodynamics for closed systems • First law of thermodynamics for open systems • Internal energy and enthalpy • Phase changes and phase change enthalpy • Selected circular processes, e.g., heat pumps, cooling plants and thermal power plants • Heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation Mechanics: • Motions, moments and moments of inertia for rotating bodies • Material stretching and tension calculation • Extension of materials
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the first law of thermodynamics for open and closed systems. - Understand the phase change of substances. - Be able to calculate various selected thermal processes such as heat pumps, cooling systems and thermal power plants. - Understand and being able to calculate the efficiency of individual processes, including thermal and Carnot efficiency. - Understand and being able to calculate heat transmission, convection in general and in connection with cooling of electrical applications. - Understand and being able to calculate motions, moments and moments of inertia of rotating masses in connection with electric machines. - Have an understanding of materials stretching and applied mechanical stresses. - Understand the length extension of materials by heat or friction.
62603:
Name English: Thermodynamics with project
Danish Title: Termodynamik med projekt
General Course Objectives: The course shall give a basic understanding of thermodynamics, including initial heat transfer. This knowledge shall be applied on both individual components and systems.
Content: Thermodynamic: • basic thermodynamic systems • thermodynamic states and parameters, heat and work • 1st law of thermodynamics for closed systems • energy balance for open and closed systems • enthalpy, equations of state and specific heat capacity • 1st law of thermodynamics for open systems, including volume work • 2nd law of thermodynamics, cycle processes, reversible and irreversible processes • entropy, T-s/P-v/P-h diagrams, isentropic processes, technical work, isentropic efficiency and the Carnot process • phase diagrams, phase shift, cycle processes and cycle processes with phase shift • introduktion to theory for pressure loss, gas mixtures, combustion and moist air Initial heat transfer: • conduction, convection and radiation • one-dimensional heat transfer for plane and circular geometries • basic formulars for heat transfer based on given data for heat transfer Components: • turbines, piston engines, pumps, compressors, heat exchangers, nozzles and diffusors Systems: • heat/work engines (Otto, Diesel and Brayton) • steam power systems without feed water preheating • one-step heat pumps and refrigeration systems Project: • During the course, students will prepare a project which is made as a group work ending in a written report based on academic principle, and containing main elements from the CDIO concept, such as definition/description of system(s) and its boundaries, design based on relevant technical calculations, commissioning and operation. Choice of system is to have relevance to the systems presented during the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - understand and apply states and processes by thermodynamic parameters - understand and apply different models, expressed by equations (ideal gas equation), tables and diagrams - understand and apply determination of a systems exchange of work and heat with the sourroundings - understand and apply different catagories of energy - understand and apply simplifications for a system, and thereby allow for thermodynamic calculations - understand and apply principples of mass and energy conservation - carry out simple experiments, interpretate results and display these in a comprehensive way - measure pressure, temperature or flow in a system, and on the basis thereof undrstand to calculate other thermodynamic parameters - understand and apply determination of key charateristics for a system e.g. efficiency - understand and apply different efficiencies - understand and apply principles for gas mixtures, combustion and moist air
62606:
Name English: Mechatronics, applied discrete control
Danish Title: Mekatronik, anvendt diskret reguleringsteknik
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to give the students a professional competence to apply methods for analysis, design and implementation of mechatronic systems used in industrial equipment and energy systems, including being able to perform quality control of the designed control systems and manage the development process from requirement specification to delivery and commissioning. The course provides an understanding of applied discrete control techniques, including the basic concepts and methods so that the student can analyze, design, simulate and implement digital software algorithms for control systems using industrial computer PLC & graphical panels HMI as well as practical process systems.
Content: Sampling frequency, folding and aliasing. Discrete 1st order filter and Kalman filtering. FUZZY control and self-organizing FUZZY control. Discrete PID controller and implementation on PLC. Advanced control methods and their application. Quality control and management of the development process. Practical exercises with simulator, PLC & HMI.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Be able to use real-time industrial software for programming PID control algorithms on industrial computers PLC and microcomputer equipment Be able to design, build and use a smaller SCADA system. - Understand interfacing of transmitters and actuators. - Have an understanding of FUZZY control and be able to apply a self-organizing FUZZY controller to a process plant. - Have knowledge of digital filtering methods, including lowpass and Kalman filtering. - Understand and be able to apply the principles of feedforward, cascade and splitrange regulation to an industrial computer PLC. - Understand sampled systems, sampling frequency, folding and aliasing. Analog to digital conversion ADC and DAC and conversion solution LSB. - Be able to design and implement discrete noise filtering and discrete PID controller algorithms in the form of software for an industrial computer PLC. - Have hands-on practical lab work with control systems and process models.
62607:
Name English: Applied industrial robotics
Danish Title: Anvendt industrirobot teknik
General Course Objectives: The course aims to provide students with professional competence to be able to word with sensor input for robot applications, simulating robot paths and develop software for controlling an industrial robot system. Get an understanding of methods of analysis, design and implementation of a control on an electromechanical robot plant Get an understanding of the interaction between mechanics, control, software and electronics. Understand safety risk for people around the operation of autonomous robot systems.
Content: Industrial robot Sensor technology Robot programming Robot simulation program Practical exercises robot lab.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Be able to use python script language for robotics - Be able to use 3D simulation software for robot path planning simulation. - Be able to generate specific robot language in 3D simulation software. - Be able to use software to interface an industrial robot - Understand and be able to use sensor technology for robot applications - Understand the basic mathematics in robot kinematics. - Understand the electrical and mechanical structure of industrial robots and the meaning of encoder and motor on the robot. - Understanding of redundant safety circuits for emergency stop systems if. current rules for robot systems. - Have knowledge of personal safety on autonomous robotic systems
62614:
Name English: Advanced Engineering Dynamics
Danish Title: Advanced Engineering Dynamics
General Course Objectives: To provide the students with a theoretical and practical foundation for understanding, formulating, and solving complex dynamic problems by using analytical methods and simulation software within dynamics and analytical mechanics. The problems are real world problems from the fields: design, machines, vehicles, mechanisms, robotic and space technology.
Content: Newtons second law in rectangular and polar coordinates. Keplers three laws. Central forces and orbit mechanics. Newtons law of gravitation. Hohmann-orbits. Rocket equation.
