Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Apply concepts, theory and methods within the electromagnetic area such as: magnetostatic field quantities, Biot-Savart's law, Gauss' law, magnetic fields around conductors, and the corresponding boundary conditions (corresponding to sub-elemeters in course 30035) - Apply concepts, theory, and methods within the digital signal processing area such as: necessary sampling rate, anti-aliasing filter, discrete Fourier transformation, and design of digital filters (corresponding to sub-elements of course 62743) - Define, describe, develop and apply models for the methods and components used within the course. - Specify, design, implement, test and document digital signal processing ppograms and applications - Specify, design, calculate, analyze, model, simulate, construct, test and document the hardware - Cooperation in groups to address common tasks - Planning, specifying, collaborating, documenting and applying relevant engineering terminology. - Relate the specifications, calculations, simulations and measurements and draw clear and relevant conclusions - Explain the causes and differences between the calculated, simulated and measured results. - Discuss the differences to relevant theory, simulations and tests. - Communicate group planning process and objectives achieved
34764:
Name English: Robotics and Automation in Pharmaceutical Manufacturing
Danish Title: Robotteknologi og Automation i Farmaceutisk Produktion
General Course Objectives: This course aims to provide participants with fundamental understanding and skills required to design and implement integrated robotics and automation solutions in a pharmaceutical manufacturing environment. The students will learn about automation, robotics, perception and safety and will need to synthesize these topics within an integrated working system. By developing a solution to a real-life problem, participants will be able to identify the necessary components, communication strategies and safety measures specific to the pharmaceutical manufacturing domain. The course offers participants an opportunity to work on a use-case in pharma manufacturing to directly apply the lessons learned.
Content: The course introduces various devices, components and communication protocols used in industrial automation and how to choose the appropriate one for the specific application. The course focuses on how the automated systems interact in a real production environment. It gives an insight into various aspects and regulations that need to be considered when designing an automation system, and the additional requirements specific to pharma manufacturing. The content of the course is built around a concrete, real-life task where the learnings can be directly applied and aimed to give practical skills in programming PLCs, HMIs, industrial robots and vision systems. The structure of the course will combine selected lectures at DTU on topics such as industrial robot arms, PLC programming, and robot vision, each followed by hands-on development in the premises of NNE (Novo Nordisk Engineering) in Virum.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify various devices and components used in industrial automation - Use PLC and robot programming languages to develop code for pharmaceutical manufacturing applications - Argue about the choice of an appropriate controller, way of communication and safety components - Design and program a safety system based on basic risk assessment - Explain and reason various regulatory requirements in pharma manufacturing - Design and implement interfaces and interlocks between different systems within pharmaceutical manufacturing such as e,g, robot, PLC, vision system. - Analyze a problem of integrating an industrial automation system and formulate specifications and success criteria - Explain and communicate the concept and solution to an industrial automation system integration problem - Work in a team to solve a complex task
38112:
Name English: Entrepreneurial Marketing
Danish Title: Marketing i iværksætteri
General Course Objectives: The course will enable students to understand the interplay between products and services and the market, and to develop their skills in entrepreneurial marketing by following a customer development process.
Content: The students will be asked to develop a marketing planning with respect to a specific product/service, following a customer development process. The course will enable the students to think strategically about developing customers through various approaches in entrepreneurial marketing. The course is based on a combination of empirical examples, theories and concepts about market, business design, strategy and marketing.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Design a viable business solutions for a particular product/service, using Design Thinking principles - List the various conceptualizations of the market and describe the qualification of a product on the market - Understand the interplay among value, behavioral change and business model - Understand and follow customer development process (customer discovery, customer validation, customer creation and customer building) - Analyze how organizations use the marketing mix to market products/services to their target customers - Explain fundamental concepts of business strategy - Explain and use fundamental concepts of branding and advertising techniques - Apply strategic pricing to a product/service - Conduct market analysis for a particular product/service - Understand and apply digital marketing tools to a particular product/service - Analyse the relation between a product and its market using the theoretical perspectives of the course curriculum
38113:
Name English: Applied AI for Entrepreneurs
Danish Title: Anvendt AI for Entreprenører
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to introduce students to generative AI technologies for creating scalable startups leveraging the potential of agents and models, by utilizing high level application frameworks to design prototype concepts, and assess business potential as well as societal impact.
Content: The course focuses on prototyping generative AI concepts, combined with business modeling tools for identifying and optimizing market value. Lectures will introduce high level frameworks for designing multimodal transformer based applications. Combined with short videos that explain the Python code examples, the lectures will introduce business modeling tools for translating AI functionalities into novel products combining reasoning models with agents and structured memory.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify trustworthy AI core abilities to address user needs - Compare AI approaches to optimize market value - Combine AI functionalities into products for potential market segments - Apply AI technologies to prototype concepts as cloud solutions or integrated with hardware - Evaluate AI concepts using different types of metrics - Assess AI potential value versus implementation challenges - Optimize market value for implementing AI prototype - Define agile strategy to maximize outcome of AI solution
38888:
Name English: Journal club in entrepreneurship and innovation research
Danish Title: Journal club for entreprenørskab og innovationsforskning
General Course Objectives: The course aims at giving the students a critical approach to the existing literature, building knowledge about new literature within their research areas, and to practice scientific communication skills and discussions as well as assess ethical aspects.
Content: The course consists of presentations of scientific papers from high-profile journals by the PhD-students in the topics of entrepreneurship and innovation research. The purpose of the paper, results, and conclusions must be presented, and a critical discussion of the methods and the results should also be included. The student should also emphasize what the new issues in the paper are, and how these can contribute to his/hers PhD project. Each presentation must result in a short summary with the most important results and conclusions. These summaries are collected for the course, such that a relevant database is constructed during the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Conduct a systematic and scientific information search. - Apply various search methods on the internet (e.g. WebOfScience and DTIC). - Select relevant scientific publications. - Explain results and conclusions from publications. - Critique and defend the applied methods. - Relate conclusions to own research projects. - Communicate methods, results, and conclusions to other PhD students. - Argue scientifically in a discussion. - Critique and defend coherence between the research questions asked and the research design applied
41046:
Name English: Materials and mechanics
Danish Title: Materialer og mekanik
General Course Objectives: To obtain an understanding of the connection between materials selection, mechanical requirements and geometrical constraints in product design. The course covers the characteristics of a number of materials classes with emphasis on understanding of the atomic structure and associated possibilities to tailor the materials properties by e.g. thermal treatment. The participants will learn to analyse simple mechanical product requirements and based on that select suitable materials.
Content: Metals, polymers and ceramics differ in properties because of their chemical bonds and internal structure. Materials for specific products must therefore be selected with a view to the functionality of the material. The course gives an understanding of the structure of different materials classes, how this affects the properties and how the properties may be tailored by changes to the internal structure of the material, e.g. through thermal treatment. The course further focuses on the interplay between mechanical requirement and the properties of materials. You will lean to determine the correct geometrical dimensions for product components while considering mechanical loads and materials properties.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - determine stress and strain in simple, linear elastic design elements using Hooke’s law for a unixial stress state - calculate member forces in statically determined plane trusses using the method of sections and the method of joints - determine stresses and deformations in simple, plane beams subjected to bending - perform dimensioning with respect to initiation of plastic yielding - identify the main classes of materials and recognize principal types of bonding for different materials classes, including crystal lattices - differentiate between elastic, plastic and viscoelastic behavior of metals, ceramics and polymers - apply phase diagrams to interpret and predict microstructures in metals - classify strengthening mechanisms and processes in materials - propose appropriate materials for everyday products based on materials properties
41793:
Name English: Precision Manufacturing
Danish Title: Præcisionsfremstilling
General Course Objectives: The PhD course on Precision Manufacturing is dedicated to PhD students with a background in manufacturing engineering. The aim of this course is to enable the students to exploit the capabilities of Precision Manufacturing processes in order to design Precision Engineering products with outstanding performance. The course centres on developing a comprehensive understanding of the necessary conditions, tools and methods of Precision Manufacturing and introducing the basics of Zero Defect Digital Manufacturing. Following this course the students will develop a deep understanding of: 1) precision engineering and precision manufacturing principles, 2) conditions to achieve high precision in manufacturing, 3) advanced manufacturing technologies, 4) tools and methods to implement precision, improve process performance and reduce defects in production. The focus of the course is on tools and methods, while selected processes are discussed to support their presentation and application in practice.
Content: The course takes its starting point from the knowledge of basic manufacturing processes. After introducing the relationships between product functionality and process properties and performance, the boundaries of Precision Manufacturing are defined and the requirements for the implementation of Precision Manufacturing are presented. The two necessary conditions for implementation of Precision Manufacturing are described and validated through a number of examples. The four groups of tools and methods for implementation of Precision Manufacturing, namely: 1) Anticipated Process Knowledge (including modelling and simulation, DOE, experimental optimization); 2) Process monitoring, control and feedback, compensation, in situ metrology; 3) high accuracy hardware (machine tools, tools and fixtures); 4) Controlled manufacturing environment will be described and practical implementation to selected processes will be demonstrated. The concept of Concurrent Engineering is introduced in the context of Precision Manufacturing, explaining the need of manufacturing awareness early in the product design process. Precision Manufacturing processes will be introduced with the aid of a suitable framework for their classification and selection. In depth presentation will be given for selected processes, including both theoretical description as well as practical application of the tools and methods for advanced process simulation, optimization and monitoring.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the conditions to achieve high precision manufacturing - Analyze functional requirements and translate them into design specifications with focus on precision requirements - Select (apply) suitable advanced manufacturing processes matching the product specifications - Identify (evaluate) critical issues hindering manufacturing accuracy - Apply the tools and methods taught to improve manufacturing accuracy - Perform (apply) theoretical calculations to support decisions concerning process selection and choice of process parameters - Select (apply) suitable measurement methods for verification of product compliance with design specifications - Create a strategy for improving manufacturing accuracy in manufacturing scenarios (processes and or components) different from those presented in class - Apply systematic methods to create a coherent sequence of actions leading to production of precision products
41815:
Name English: Introduction to Finite Element Analysis
Danish Title: Introduktion til Finite Element Analyse
General Course Objectives: The Finite Element Method is one of the most widely used numerical methods for designing and optimizing components and processes in traditional machine industry, production, devices for medical and biomechanical applications (Life-sciences) as well as civil infrastructure. It is an essential tool with significant societal contributions to areas such as the green transition, the healthcare sector, and Industry 4.0. Students of this course will get a fundamental understanding of the theoretical background of the finite element method and its application to industrial problems. Using commercial finite element software, students will be able to conduct thermal and structural analyses in 2D and 3D. By means of both theory and numerical experiments, the students will be able to grasp the breadth of its capabilities, but importantly also its limits. Particular emphasis is put on concepts of numerical modeling philosophy, such as understanding, evaluating and controlling the different sources of analysis errors.
Content: The course is based on theoretical lectures, computer exercises and project work. Initially, the stiffness method is introduced as a practical approach to the finite element method for simple elements. Subsequently, the general theory of finite element is presented by covering the concepts of virtual work, shape functions and numerical integration. The most common element types found in finite element software are discussed and tested. Moreover, simple and more advanced boundary conditions are explained in detail. A series of practical aspects are also covered such as import of CAD geometries, meshing techniques, file formats and post-processing. The basic theory behind different analysis types are also presented as well as the most common types of linear solvers employed in finite element analysis. In the first group project the students program a very simple finite element model using the stiffness method. During the three weeks period in January a larger project work is performed using commercial software.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Perform structural and heat transfer modeling using available finite element software. - Explain the theory behind the most common options provided in the graphical user interface of commercial finite element software. - Recall the most common types of finite element analyses and choose appropriately for a given problem. - Describe the different meshing strategies and techniques, and apply them appropriately in order to create accurate and efficient finite element models. - Choose one or more suitable finite element types for a specific analysis. - Describe input and output file formats used by finite element software, and modify finite element models by editing of such files. - Explain how imported CAD model descriptions can affect the generated finite element mesh, identify and fix issues with imported CAD geometries. - Perform system simplifications in terms of geometry, loads and boundary conditions in a finite element model to achieve the required accuracy while minimizing computation time. - Verify a model and evaluate its accuracy, based on simple hand calculations, finite element theory, and mesh convergence studies. - Explain the logistics behind the implementation of the finite element method for numbering of degrees of freedom and connection of elements. - Post-process and report finite element analysis results in a structured, clear, concise and informative manner.
41833:
Name English: Introduction to Experimental Dynamics
Danish Title: Introduktion til Eksperimentel Dynamik
General Course Objectives: The aim of this course is to introduce the basic concepts of theoretical and experimental dynamics, sensing technology and vibrations to students with no prior background in these subject areas. To achieve this goal, the course focuses on hands-on exercises and experimental activities to facilitate the understanding and application of the lectured theoretical content. The students will develop the necessary skills to plan and devise test setups, carry out vibration tests, process the measured vibration data, extract the dynamic properties, and subsequently, use the extracted information to analyze and assess the structural and dynamic performance of the tested structures.
Content: - Introduction to basic principles for evaluating the dynamic behavior of structural systems - Techniques and instrumentation (sensing technology) for dynamic/vibration measurements - Vibration/dynamic testing of scaled structural systems and vibration response measurements with appropriate sensing technology - Introduction to techniques and methods to process measured vibration data - Introduction to techniques and methods to extract dynamic properties from measured vibration data - Experimental estimation of material properties from vibration tests - Comparison between theoretical and experimental dynamic properties (estimated from data acquired in vibration/dynamic tests) - Assess the dynamic performance of the tested structural systems
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Devise an experimental methodology and conduct dynamic testing to measure and infer about material and structural performance. - Apply and process measured data from experimental work to test and validate numerical models as well as to estimate structural and dynamic properties - List and explain experimental methods and procedures for determining the dynamic properties of structural systems. - Compare experimental and theoretical dynamic properties and explain how the structure's parameters (such as mass, stiffness and boundary conditions) is related its dynamic performance. - Use the relevant sensing technology to measure the vibration responses (e.g., accelerations) of scaled structural models induced by dynamic loads. - Apply signal processing methods and tools to process and convert the vibration responses measured in accelerations into displacements, by exploiting basic mathematics and signal processing theory. - Apply the experimental modal analysis framework to estimate the modal properties of the scaled structural models, i.e., the natural frequencies, the mode shapes and the damping ratios. - Estimate basic material properties by applying modal analysis techniques to the measured vibration responses. - Analyze and assess the dynamic performance and the tested structural systems.
41864:
Name English: Process technology
Danish Title: Procesteknik
General Course Objectives: The overall aim of the course is to provide the students an understanding of thermodynamics, fluid mechanics and continuum mechanics of thermal and mechanical materials processing. The students are acquainted with fundamental theoretical methods of analysis in order to carry out simple estimates as well as a bit more detailed calculations.
Content: Theoretical basis for calculating thermal material processes: Heat transfer mechanisms, Heat balances. The heat conduction equation in 1D. Lumped analysis. Application to heat treatment. Calculation of solidification times in casting, Chvorinov's rule, simple analysis of cooling of melt in a gating system. Simple heat transfer analysis in welding. Solutions to the heat conduction equation for moving heat sources. Short presentation of basis for calculating mechanical material processes: yield criteria, flow rule and strain hardening. Short presentation of methods of metal forming analysis. Application of the calculation methods on processes like forging, rolling, extrusion, deep drawing and stamping. Examples on modern production methods for processesing of components ranging from tons to micro grams will be shown.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - describe the basic heat transfer mechanisms - set up simple heat balances - calculate solidification times for simple geometries - evaluate the abovementioned methods of analysis with respect to simple calculations of temperature development in casting, heat tratment and welding - describe logarithmic strains, yield criteria and the flow rule - apply analytical methods, including informed/derived results from the work method and the slab method, for analysis of simple metal forming operations - apply the above mentioned analytical methods for calculating the influence of basic material and process parameters on resulting strain, hardness, process forces and tool loads in simple metal forming operations - select among the abovementioned methods for simple process planning tasks in metal forming
41940:
Name English: Advanced Digital Technologies in Construction Projects
Danish Title: Avancerede digitale teknologier i byggeprojekter
General Course Objectives: This course focuses on the use of remote sensing and data processing techniques in construction projects and the development of digital building models, as carriers of project information for data extraction, exchange, and communication in applications ranging from automated progress reporting to automation and robotics in construction.
Content: This course will focus on advances in digital technologies in construction. The themes to be covered are development, instrument configuration, and application of various remote sensing technologies as radio frequency identification, global navigation satellite system; 3D point cloud data capturing from ground and airborne instruments such as laser scanning, light detection and ranging, unmanned aerial vehicles, and photo-and videogrammetry. After the data collection the students will use methods in signal processing and data analysis such as filtering, noise reduction, and feature extraction for topic-relevant applications or use cases. These include construction site progress monitoring with real-time resource location sensing and tracking; as-built modeling from range point-clouds; right-time proactive construction safety, health, and wellbeing; automated or human-machine guidance and interaction; general automation and robotics applications in construction. Theoretical aspects of the harsh work environment and the complex and dynamic nature of construction site characteristics, often relevant to the success or failure of remote sensing, will also be covered. Course activities in and outside the laboratory will explore three major areas that create challenges for embedding advanced technologies in construction projects: • Complexity, with a particular focus on the relationship of technical vs. organizational complexity. • Investment, with a focus on identifying and mitigating key risks from a business and process point of view. • Human acceptance, addressing the social and organizational intricacies caused by automation, personal rights, and intra-organizational factors.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - identify sensors to measure parameters related to construction sites - evaluate the current and the different levels of automation and robotics in construction - analyze and assess potentials and barriers in implementing remote sensing in building information modeling (BIM) and virtual design in construction (VDC) - independently find relevant and supplementary information for remote sensing techniques - develop a measurement plan using remote sensing for construction applications - interpret and analyze captured data - create as-built 3D models from point cloud data - apply and explore remote sensing techniques for observing construction site progress
41950:
Name English: Timber Structures
Danish Title: Trækonstruktioner
General Course Objectives: The course provides a fundamental understanding of the mechanical properties of wood such as strength, stiffness, load duration and moisture, and how the material wood is used as basic beam and column elements for structural design. The course also covers basic connection design using dowel type fasteners such as nails, dowels and bolts.
Content: The course cover mechanical properties of wood and wood-based products, statical calculation models of straight timber members /beams and columns) in the Ultimate (ULS) and Serviceability Limit States (SLS), duration dependent loads on wood structures, influence of moisture on design of timber structures, construction wood-based elements (structural timber, glued laminated timber, and other Engineered Wood Products (EWP)), fasteners and joint design using dowels, bolts and nails, as well as local instability problems, i.e., flexural and lateral torsional buckling. The course consists of lectures and solving assignments throughout the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain how the characteristics of the material wood effect its use as a construction material - Define relevant material properties of wood for use in structural design. - Evaluate different timber products and their application in basic structural systems. - Use relevant standards and literature in design of basic wood structures. - Define and handle duration dependent loads on wood structures. - Assess the tensile, compressive, shear and flexural strength of straight wood-based elements. - Evaluate the instantaneous and permanent deformations of straight wood-based elements. - Evaluate the impact of local instability (buckling and lateral torsional buckling) on the strength of timber elements. - Calculate the dowel effect of nails, bolts, and dowels and design connections in timber structures composed of multiple fasteners.
41959:
Name English: Computational Structural Modelling: Linear Finite Element Method
Danish Title: Bærende Konstruktioners Numeriske Modellering: Lineær elementmetode
General Course Objectives: The Finite Element Method (FEM) is a widely used tool among Civil Engineers (and Engineers in general) due to its generality and flexibility in a large number of engineering problems. Although most practitioners use commercial programs, an understanding of the underlying theory is a necessity for performing reasonable, realistic and reliable analyzes using FEM. This course focuses on the fundamentals behind the method and provides the theoretical basis for further studies, as well as the use of FEM as a design tool. The course is oriented towards constructions and the structural mechanics area.
Content: The main subject is the Finite Element Method for structural design purposes. Emphasis is on a systematic development of the Finite Element Method based on the principle of virtual work, starting with panels. Shape functions are introduced for interpolation of the primary variables from which the generalized strains and stresses can be determined. Numerical integration and the isoparameter method are introduced and applied. In connection with the use of commercial Finite Element Method programs, the general structure is introduced. A commercial program is used and based on a theoretical insight into the Finite Element Method, a critical assessment of results can be made. It is shown how Maxwell-Betti's theorem can be used to optimize structures in a Finite Element Method context. The course is structured around lectures and exercises that cover both analytical derivations, programming of the Finite Element Method and use of commercial software.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Introduced and apply influence lines in Finite Element formulations. - Establish the Finite Element Method equations for panels and shells based on the principle of virtual work. - Explain and apply the isoparametric method for the development of elements. - Apply Maxwell-Betti's theorem for optimization of structures using the Finite Element Method. - Explain different structural element types. - Apply and evaluate the results obtained using different structural element types. - Apply a commercial FEM program and perform critical assessment of the results - Program and modify linear Finite Element programs. - Perform an analysis of beams subjected to torsion using the Finite Element Method.
41971:
Name English: Advanced Timber Structures
Danish Title: Videregående trækonstruktioner
General Course Objectives: The course builds on the basic understanding of design of wood-based element and connections, by introducing orthotropic mechanical properties of wood and how these properties influence the design of elements with varying cross-sections and curved shapes. The course covers advanced topics such as finite element modelling, built-up elements, fire design, moisture deformations, and moment- and screwed connections.
Content: The course includes an introduction to specific material properties of wood such as its orthotropic structure, its behavior under moisture, fire and load duration. Topics covered are instability problems, displacements, transverse tension/compression, geometries with varying cross-sections, curved geometries, moisture-related stresses and deformations, reinforcement of brittle failure modes, design of moment-resistant and screwed connections, determination of connection slip and rotational slip modulus, and composite structures. The course will be a combination of short lectures, independent study and design work. The design project includes the determination of loads and calculation of structures based on relevant standards and literature.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze the performance of advanced wooden structures by taking into account its specific behavior in terms of anisotropy, strength, rigidity, humidity, load duration, and fire properties. - Analyze and calculate timber structural elements with varying cross-sections and curved shapes. - Analyze, and devise relevant measures, for the bracing of large timber frame structures. - Define and evaluate the impact of serviceability criteria on the performance of large timber buildings and building components. - Define and handle time and moisture dependent effects and loads on timber structures. - Analyze complex structures in both solid timber, glulam and Engineered Wood Products (EWP) using Finite Element software. - Assess and calculate mechanical connections that are able to resist large forces and moments. - Use relevant standards and literature in the design of advanced wood structures. - Take part of a design team working with wood structures.
41991:
Name English: CASMaT International Summer School on Advanced Structural and Material Testing
Danish Title: CASMaT International Sommerskole om Avanceret Konstruktions- og Materialeprøvning
General Course Objectives: To introduce the theory and concepts behind advanced multiscale testing of structures and materials – with a focus on composites materials and structures – and to allow the students to get hands on experience with the most important, advanced measuring techniques and methodologies.
Content: Introductory lecture on the concepts of multi-scale testing. The main body of the course consists of 4 modules with a combination of lectures and hands-on experimental work: • Data acquisition and instrumentation. • The coupon scale: Advanced materials testing. • The subcomponent scale: Hybrid testing. • Full scale testing: Digital twinning. On the last day the physical presence on campus is concluded by assignment work and course evaluation. The course is supplemented by guest lectures on selected topics from international experts.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe the purpose and importance of experimental mechanics investigations - Describe the basic principles of integrated testing and modeling - Describe the basic principles and benefits of virtual testing - Explain the basic principles of sensors (including strain gauges, accelerometers, fiber optical sensors) and measurement techniques (including acoustic emissions, thermography, digital image correlation) and implement these appropriately at different length scales - Classify and implement different materials characterization methods for composite systems (including SN curves, constant life diagram, damage development and accumulation) - Explain how to link experimental measurements with numerical simulations to apply hybrid testing techniques to a structural component test - Explain how to link experimental measurements with numerical simulations, to create a digital twin - Define a relevant multiscale test approach to evaluate the performance of a structure made of a specific material - Make predictions from one scale to another based on experimental data and modelling - Evaluate the behavior/performance of a full-scale wind turbine blade when exposed to mechanical loading
41992:
Name English: Design-Oriented Numerical Modelling of Reinforced Concrete Structures
Danish Title: Design-orienteret numerisk modellering af armerede betonkonstruktioner
General Course Objectives: The scope is to present relevant state-of-the-art research and best practices within the field of structural concrete, with the aim that students develop sound and refined design and assessment capabilities. The course covers several topics ranging from the main principles in conceptual design of reinforced concrete to advanced numerical modelling.
Content: The course is structured around lectures and practical exercises covering both analytical and numerical approaches. In the exercises, students will work with analytical models, MATLAB code and existing software programs, focusing on the design and assessment of practical cases. The lectures will cover topics such as: • Concepts of limit state design and safety. • The theory of plasticity and the fundamental theoretical basis for the formulation of numerical modelling of concrete structures. • Convex optimization methods and description of the corresponding FEM formulation to optimize the collapse load. • Energy principles for elastic structures and description of the corresponding optimization-based FEM formulation for service limit state analysis • Non-linear fracture mechanics and behaviour of cracked structural concrete • Displacement-based FEM formulations and the application to fully cracked concrete structures. • Considerations on serviceability limit state and cracking of structures • Reliability concepts and application within the frame of limit analysis The lectures will be given by experts from DTU.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - A student who has met the objectives of the course will: Understand the concept of limit state design - Have an insight into the prerequisites for a safe and sound application of plasticity-based approaches to structural concrete - Understand the importance and implications of the deformation capacity of materials and structures - Understand and apply the concept of Finite Element Limit Analysis (FELA) to design, analysis and verification of concrete structures - Understand the extremum theorems and the duality in weak upper- and lower-bound solutions with respect to FELA - Understand and apply the concept of Finite Element Serviceability Analysis (FESA) to analyze and to evaluate the serviceability behaviour of reinforced concrete structures - Understand and apply the concept of Elastic-Plastic Stress Fields (EPSF) for design and assessment of structures - Understand and be capable of applying the limit state safety format in a numerical modelling context
41B3A:
Name English: Management of Sustainable Construction 1 - the Project
Danish Title: Ledelse af Bæredygtigt Byggeri 1 - Projektet
General Course Objectives: The course focuses on management of sustainability in the construction project, from the first design sketches through detailed planning to execution, and on where in the process choices are made of decisive importance for the sustainability of a construction project. The course gives the students an overview of the value chain for choosing solutions and decisions. How are the best choices made, which skills and methods are necessary, who makes which decisions at which level, and how project groups are led in processes with a focus on sustainability. What barriers might there be in relation to the implementation and realization of the desired decisions and choices, and how can these barriers be handled.
Content: Theoretical overview of projects, programs and portfolios and their context, management, organization and work division. Stakeholder analyses. Introduction to different project management models. Dilemmas/​perspectives/​challenges about management, leadership, companionship. Establishing ownership across the organization. Methods and tools, including service descriptions, requirements specifications, etc. Risks, effects and consequences. Risk matrix.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify essential characteristics of sustainable construction projects throughout the process. - Analyze the process in relation to the desired sustainability goals. - Identify critical decision points and determine important milestones in the process. - Assess and apply relevant project management tools. - Assess and mitigate risks in sustainable projects. - Analyse and mitigate possible barriers to the implementation and realization of sustainable choices and solutions in projects, programs and portfolios. - Lead discussion and considerations regarding sustainable choices and solutions. - Based on this, will be able to design an optimized project management model. - Plan and manage the project from design to realization. - Control the process and defend the choices made to achieve a construction project that is as sustainable as possible.
41B3B:
Name English: Management of Sustainable Construction 2 - the Company
Danish Title: Ledelse af Bæredygtigt Byggeri 2 - Virksomheden
General Course Objectives: The sustainable restructuring of construction requires the adoption of solutions, processes and business models across the organisation's value chain. This applies both to companies' internal behavior and strategy, as well as externally in relation to product and market. The aim of the course is to give the students the knowledge and skills to participate in this process. The course deals with models for company strategy and business development, as well as methods and tools to promote the process around sustainable construction, including how a company can position itself to be able to contribute to a sustainable transition.
Content: Business types, market types, responsibilities. Management of companies versus projects. Ownership across the organization. Models for strategy and business development; value chain analysis; business strategic analysis; circular business models. Documentation and reporting; ESG, CSR. B-corp certification. Green accounts, total cost of ownership. The EU's taxonomy and the UN's Program for Responsible Investments. The students will meet companies where sustainability is a significant part of the company's identity and services.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify essential characteristics of an organization with a sustainable business strategy. - Characterize different types of organization in relation to their primary products and markets. - Analyze and identify potentials and risks of a sustainable company strategy and business model. - Identify and solve critical decision points and set important milestones in the process. - Identify, assess and apply relevant management methods and tools. - Analyse, discover and mitigate possible barriers to the implementation and realization of a sustainable corporate strategy and business plan. - Develop and design a sustainable and/or circular corporate strategy and business model. - Plan, lead and implement the design of a sustainable and/or circular company strategy and business model. - Control the process and defend the strategic choices, both internally and externally.
41B3C:
Name English: Management of Sustainable Construction 3 - Change Processes
Danish Title: Ledelse af Bæredygtigt Byggeri 3 - Forandringsprocesser
General Course Objectives: The student acquire knowledge and competence to participate in the innovative change processes that are a necessity for the green transition, including: selected theories and models for innovation and change management at both company and sector/societal level; selected models for product development and innovation; methods and tools to promote sustainable construction.
Content: Transition theory and Strategic Niche Management as an approach to systemic change in the construction sector. Product development, including stage/gate model and Open Innovation. Organizational development, including Kotter's 8 step change model. Pilot and demonstration projects – what can they do and what can't they? Certification schemes and circular economy as driving forces. Methods and tools, e.g. transformative projects and MCDA methods. The students will meet companies with a clear strategy for innovation management as part of a green transition. The students must relate the course content and learning objectives to a specific project, which must be analyzed in relation to this. The students collaborate on the project in small groups.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze and identify development and change potentials in relation to sustainability. - Analyze and assess technological maturity and market potential for sustainable innovations. - Evaluate and apply theories, models, methods and tools for innovation. - Plan and lead innovation and change processes in projects and companies. - Identify and assess critical barriers and driving forces in the innovation process - Formulate milestones and deliverables and set milestones in the innovation process. - Identify, analyze and mitigate possible risks in innovation projects. - Assess the importance of external systemic framework conditions and incentive structures for innovation in projects and companies.
41B4A:
Name English: Master of Sustainable Construction - master thesis
Danish Title: Master i Bæredygtigt Byggeri - masterprojekt
General Course Objectives: The master thesis completes the Master of Sustainable Construction. The thesis must be based on one or more of the topics that have been dealt with in the previous courses in the master programme, and must demonstrate the student's ability to work independently with sustainability in construction.
Content: The students will by themselves formulate the master's thesis; the academic focal point of which must be one or more of the subjects included in the master's programme. The project is to be based on a concrete project or a challenge, primarily taken from one of the students' companies. It can be a concrete construction project, a method or a process (e.g. management or change process). The students receive supervision, primarily from one of the lecturers associated with the programme. The supervisor is agreed with the person concerned and with the head of studies.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Work independently with sustainable construction, based on evidence and research. - Be familiar with evidence and research through available scientific literature. - Define and explain a wide range of the factors that determine sustainability. - Describe and analyze issues and dilemmas in connection with sustainability. - Describe and choose the competencies that are necessary in a given organization in relation to making a given project more sustainable. - Set up scenarios for development in a given project or a given organisation, under different conditions. - Design new solutions or solution models that point in the direction of more sustainability. - Define different solution models, analyze advantages and disadvantages and discuss them. - Combine interdisciplinary knowledge and use it to develop new solutions or models that point in the direction of more sustainability. - Combine interdisciplinary and holistic knowledge of sustainable construction and discuss this in the master thesis. - Give a perspective to the interdisciplinary knowledge and defend a given conclusion.
42189:
Name English: Transport System Analysis
Danish Title: Analyse af transportsystemer
General Course Objectives: This course is about understanding and being able to analyse transport systems. Students will gain knowledge on key mathematical methods used to model travel demand and supply in complex mobility systems. Applications encompass a wide range of traditional and emerging modes of transport, covering both private and public perspectives.
Content: The course covers quantitative methods that can be used to solve problems within transport modelling, and is built around 3 interconnected modules: demand (D), supply (S) and DS interactions. Related to demand modelling, the course focuses on statistical and mathematical methods, especially regression, discrete choice models, iterative proportional fitting in matrix estimation, and gravitation models. Related to supply we focus on the performance of transport networks, traffic flow theory, network modelling and queueing. Finally, within demand-supply interactions we will focus on equilibrium analysis and traffic assignment. In addition to introducing the underlying fundamentals, the course will include numerous case-studies from different transportation settings. The classes are taught in an interactive manner, with theoretical parts combined with hands-on exercises using an interactive notebook environment. Knowledge of coding is not a must, although some exercises will be presented in Python.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe fundamental techniques and aggregation levels for modelling transport systems - Formulate and apply models for generation and distribution of travel - Analyse travel mode choice using logit and nested logit models - Apply and validate a demand model for transport analysis - Apply and assess different models to evaluate the performance of transport systems - Implement, analyse and argue the strengths and weaknesses of different modelling and solution methods to solve traffic assignment problems - Explain the structure of transport models and discuss feedback mechanisms - Formulate and apply a combined transport model to evaluate the impacts of potential policies - Use mathematical software for the analysis of transport systems and network performance - Present focused and concise transport system analyses in writing
42403:
Name English: Advanced Operations Management for Production and Service Systems
Danish Title: Avanceret Operations Management til produktions- og servicesystemer
General Course Objectives: In the era of digitalization, the importance of operations management is tremendous for sustainable economic growth. The effectiveness and efficiency of various production and service systems can be improved by analytics. Optimization methodologies and simulation techniques offer many opportunities for better decision-making and planning in volatile environments. This course aims to teach advanced operations management problem-solving technologies like modeling, optimization, and simulation with application to production and service operations management. Students should be able to make sound decisions and lead critical discussions in the context of operations management. The course promotes abstract thinking and develops abstract problem-solving competencies.
Content: This course will acquaint students with advanced concepts in operations management, emphasizing the impact of digitalization. Modern planning problems from production and service operations management will be analyzed, modeled, and solved using mathematical programming and simulation. The focus is on increasing effectiveness and efficiency in current business operations. The students will work on case studies, applying the theoretical knowledge to real-world decision-making problems. Critical thinking and abstract problem-solving capabilities are taught throughout the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the fields of production and service operations and can differentiate between them - Explain examples of advanced planning problems and models in production and service operations - Assess the applicability of different analytical tools in advanced operations management - Analyze case studies in advanced operations management - Model advanced production and service operations problems and solve these models with appropriate mathematical methods - Analyze production and service operations problems and make sound decisions in the field of advanced operations management - Discuss and reflect upon important managerial insights in the context of advanced operations management - Apply and transfer the knowledge to any operations management problem
42S11:
Name English: Sustainable Leadership Foundations
Danish Title: Sustainable Leadership Foundations
General Course Objectives: The course builds a comprehensive understanding of sustainability and leadership, focusing on the strategic drivers and challenges organizations and humans face when committing to sustainability. Participants will explore critical factors influencing sustainability from a systemic and business perspective, learning how to lead initiatives that foster long-term, impactful change.
Content: This course applies your leadership framework and lays out the foundations of sustainable leadership and sets the starting point for the programme Master in Sustainable Leadership. By taking a holistic perspective, we unpack sustainability definitions, trends, and interlinkages. The course will consist of lectures, case studies, practical workshops, and group discussions to equip participants with both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the core principles, theories, and practices of sustainable leadership. - Analyze sustainability definitions, trends, and their interconnections from a holistic viewpoint. - Test and apply your leadership frameworks, such as change management, situational leadership, human behavior and ethical leadership. - Utilize systemic thinking and recognize planetary and human boundaries in decision-making. - Incorporate risk and resilience into sustainable business strategies. - Set effective sustainability goals and create strategic roadmaps. - Identify and engage with key stakeholders for successful sustainability initiatives - Integrate sustainability drivers into value chains and business operations.
42S12:
Name English: Complex Problem Framing
Danish Title: Complex Problem Framing
General Course Objectives: The definition of sustainability tries to encompass complex interlinks between social, economic and environmental aspects of a society. The objective of this course is to break down these complex sustainability challenges and design solutions to these challenges.
Content: To create positive societal impact, it is essential to understand and address complex systems in which sustainability challenges sit, as well as the trade-offs that are associated with sustainability. This course tackles this challenge and unpacks complex problem framing in sustainability solutions across a value chain. By adopting the approaches of human-centered design, design thinking, and inclusive innovation, participants will practice analyzing and synthesizing complex problems into manageable problems that account for the problems’ root causes and surrounding ecosystems and actors. Participants will practice facilitating and design of complex, non-linear processes.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand basic concepts related to complex problem framing, such as root cause analysis, and system mapping - Synthesize complex problems into manageable problems - Map and analyze the systems and stakeholders surrounding problems - Align critical problems and motivations across agendas and actors - Navigate complexity in practice through real-life case work - Design, prototype, and test solution concepts - Apply appropriate facilitation leadership styles in connection with complex problems - Understand human-centered design, design thinking, and inclusive innovation
42S13:
Name English: Business Models for Sustainability
Danish Title: Business Models for Sustainability
General Course Objectives: Business models are changing with the major transition of our societies, due to decarbonization, sustainability and digitalization. This course provides participants with a modern toolset to analyze, evaluate, improve, and create business models that address major sustainability challenges.
Content: The main goal of this course is to provide participants with tools and frameworks to analyze, evaluate, improve, and create business models that address major sustainability challenges. We will revisit and critique modern sustainability thinking in business, analyze business model innovation through a sustainability lens, and examine how “fundamental” frameworks in strategy and operations can be adapted to build innovative sustainability initiatives. We will then dive deeper into emerging sustainability topics such as Regeneration, Industry Self-Regulation, AI and Society, and Decarbonization. We will engage in various case discussions, simulations, and group exercises throughout the course. Importantly, many of the course’s activities allow participants to apply course concepts to design an innovative business model in the context of their choice. At the end of the course, participants will propose a business model innovation that addresses a social or environmental need (either within an existing company or as a start-up idea).
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe and critique the limitations of modern business and operations strategies in addressing major sustainability challenges - Evaluate the benefits, risks, and costs of recent innovative sustainable business models - Translate and extend modern sustainable operations strategies to a particular organizational context. - Apply modern business model innovation and operations strategy tools to create new solutions to sustainability challenges - Evaluate and apply various risk shifting and mitigation strategies when designing and deploying new sustainability initiatives. Also, appraise how risk mitigation strategies act as a driver for business model innovation - Engage with sustainability through as an entrepreneur (or intrapreneur) - Approach sustainability as an avenue for value creation and through a “systems designer” lens - Confidently communicate at the “senior executive level” the broader objectives of a sustainability initiatives to relevant stakeholders
42S14:
Name English: Sustainability-Driven Innovation & Design
Danish Title: Sustainability-Driven Innovation & Design
General Course Objectives: This course focuses on the relationship between creativity and innovation, and how design thinking and user involvement can be used to develop socially sustainable solutions through empathy building, use of dialogue tools and design methods. There will be an active focus on the SDG pledge of Leaving No One Behind, where course participants will be introduced to universal design and inclusion. The course introduces a consultancy case process which will also cover later courses.
Content: There will be an active focus on the SDG pledge of Leaving No One Behind, where course participants will be introduced to universal design and inclusion. We focus on a general introduction to creativity, design thinking, and inclusion. The first part of the course will finish with culminate in an assignment facilitated by the lecturers where the students utilize tools designed to enable a different focus when developing user understanding to develop a more inclusive solution. The second part will focus more specifically on co-creation, user-involvement and facilitation of innovation processes and will culminate in an innovation sprint, where the course participants will deploy their knowledge and actively try out different methods and facilitation. The course introduces the start of the consultancy project, that runs throughout the whole semester. The consultancy project with a company can involve collaborating to identify and implement strategies that improve the company’s environmental, social, and economic performance. The goal is to create long-term value for the company by helping to adopt practices that are environmentally friendly, socially responsible, and economically viable, aligning with global sustainability standards and enhancing the company's brand reputation.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze and reflect on the advantages and disadvantages of involving stakeholders in the design processes - Understand the significance of stakeholders in and for the involvement of different types of design process participants - Explain the advantages and disadvantages of using universal design to promote interdisciplinary collaboration - Apply appropriate facilitation style in in an innovation sprint - Reflect on the use of workshop co-creation techniques in the design process - Design and facilitate an innovation sprint with the support of the acquired learning material - Debate the importance of inclusion and universal design in innovation processes - Provide peer feedback on sustainability driven innovation solutions
42S15:
Name English: Sustainable Organizations and Partnerships
Danish Title: Sustainable Organizations and Partnerships
General Course Objectives: Part 1: The objective of this course is to harness organizational forms that are best positioned to cater to positive societal and organizational impact. This course equips participants to design, lead, and engage sustainable organizations and cross-sector partnerships. It covers leadership, organizational culture, strategy, and governance across global and local contexts. Participants learn to assess effectiveness, engage stakeholders, and foster collaboration to drive measurable sustainability impact. Learning objectives 1-6 Part 2: The second part of the course focuses on addressing complex strategic challenges in sustainable leadership, and how executive consultancy and co-creation approaches can generate actionable, high-impact solutions. The course introduces a consultancy project process covering research, concept development, solution synthesis, evaluation, and presentation, integrating interdisciplinary knowledge and prior learning from the programme. The course runs throughout the full semester. Learning objectives 6-12
Content: This course examines the organizational forms most suitable for achieving sustainable societal and corporate impact. It covers corporations, social enterprises, nonprofits, and advocacy organizations, exploring their roles and limitations. The course begins with a macro-level perspective on global governance, international agreements, voluntary codes of conduct, and sector-specific initiatives. Participants analyze organizational culture, leadership styles, and strategic, operational, and tactical layers that shape sustainable transformation. Practical exercises focus on facilitating collaboration across diverse mindsets, value systems, and institutional contexts - a critical skill in forming effective cross-sector partnerships. Case studies and discussions emphasize how global strategies translate to local impact, equipping participants to navigate multi-level governance and organizational challenges while creating tangible sustainability outcomes. The second part addresses complex strategic sustainability challenges in real organizational contexts. Participants apply research, co-creation, and innovation methods to frame challenges, synthesize solutions, and design actionable strategies that balance environmental, social, and economic considerations. The project develops skills in stakeholder engagement, facilitation, and inclusive collaboration, culminating in a written report and oral presentation to senior management. Solutions aim to create long-term organizational value, align with global sustainability standards, and demonstrate professional consultancy and strategic leadership capabilities.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify and analyze organizational forms that enable sustainable impact and compare sustainability cultures across organizational types and sectors. - Apply leadership approaches to enhance organizational sustainability and reflect on and consolidate a personal approach to leading sustainable organizations and partnerships - Evaluate conditions that influence effectiveness of different organizational forms - Identify, assess, and engage with strategic stakeholders for sustainability initiatives and analyze how partnerships and collaborations support sustainable outcomes. - Examine regulatory and institutional frameworks that influence organizational sustainability. - Design strategies for cross-sector collaboration at global and local levels, and integrate organizational, cultural, and leadership insights into actionable plans. - Analyze a complex organizational sustainability challenge and delimit it within a strategic context - Collect and structure relevant empirical and theoretical data to inform the defined problem and evaluate the collected information and formulate a clear and measurable project objective - Develop alternative solution concepts using relevant theories, methods, and tools and synthesize the solution space and identify coherent cross-disciplinary solution options - Design an integrated solution addressing strategic, organizational, and sustainability considerations - Assess the strategic relevance and organizational feasibility of the integrated solutions and evaluate the sustainability impact, risks, and value creation of the proposed solutions - Assess project progress and outcomes against the defined project plan and objectives and reflect on team collaboration and the student’s role as consultant and innovation facilitator
42S16:
Name English: Sustainability Data
Danish Title: Sustainability Data
General Course Objectives: This course focuses on data-based decision making from the perspective of sustainability. The aim is to have knowledge of the most prevalent sustainability data types and sources, and to be able to interpret and leverage data for sustainability strategy and reporting.
Content: This course provides a view on sustainability-focused data management, emphasizing the design of relevant metrics and reporting structures essential for informed decision-making. Participants will learn to classify key sustainability data, understand LCA models and carbon credits, and critically assess data to support strategy. Through exploring reporting implications and designing sustainability metrics, the course equips learners to align data with strategic goals and regulatory requirements.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify and classify most relevant and prominent sustainability databases - Understand the language of LCA life cycle assessment models - Understand how the carbon credits market functions - Identify lates developments related to biodiversity indicators and associate legislation - Master data-based management language - Design sustainability metrics for strategic purposes - Ability to critically access data in different formats - Understand and design for sustainability reporting requirements
42S17:
Name English: Change Management for Sustainability
Danish Title: Change Management for Sustainability
General Course Objectives: The aim of the 1. part of the change management course is to learn how to best empower yourself and others to realize and execute sustainable change in an international context. Learning objectives 1-5. The 2. part of the course develops participants’ personal leadership practice in general by integrating leadership theory with professional experience. Leadership is addressed as a values-based, ethically grounded, and behaviorally enacted discipline rooted in self-awareness. Through structured reflection, 360-degree feedback, and small-scale leadership experiments, participants strengthen individual leadership capabilities and formulate a focused development trajectory. The course introduces a coherent leadership development framework that supports continued growth across the programme. Learning objectives 6-10
Content: In the 1. Part of the course, we explore how sustainability is perceived, and sustainable leadership is practiced across cultures and sectors, and how these different approaches have implications for global sustainability transformations. We analyze organizational strategies as well as community-level implementations to sustainable change. We reflect on how to increase our sphere of influence to lead to more globally relevant and impactful sustainable transformations. 2. part of the course integrates theory, reflection, and practice to develop personal leadership. Participants work within a structured leadership framework supported by a 360-degree feedback process. Personal development goals are defined and tested through leadership experiments, supported by peer coaching circles that ensure reflection and accountability.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain key theories of sustainability, leadership, and change management across cultures and sectors. - Analyze how cultural differences influence sustainable leadership and global sustainability transformations. - Evaluate organizational strategies, plans, and business cases addressing multi-dimensional and cross-sector sustainability challenges. - Apply appropriate facilitation and leadership methods to engage stakeholders and communities in sustainability-driven change. - Develop and articulate a personal sustainable leadership identity grounded in theory and practice. - Analyze personal leadership behavior using established leadership theories and structured feedback. - Evaluate strengths, development needs, and ethical implications of their leadership practice. - Formulate a focused personal leadership development goal grounded in evidence. - Design and apply leadership experiments aligned with personal values and organizational context - Synthesize and assess insights into a coherent personal leadership model and development plan
42S18:
Name English: Financing and Sustainability
Danish Title: Financing and Sustainability
General Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to understand the foundations of sustainable financing and how to decarbonate society through finance. We look at transition risks and climate risks and which financial instruments are used to encourage the development of green projects on macro and micro level in organizations and in society.
Content: The goal of this course is to give a solid understanding of sustainable financing, covering regulations, debt mechanisms, and investments that support green projects across industries. The course will explore key financial tools related to impact finance like green bonds, EU taxonomy, impact investing, and venture capital while analyzing global trends and regulatory changes that influence sustainable finance. The course addresses the social, ecological, and economic impacts of regulations, as well as the risks and returns of sustainability investments. At the same time the course considers economic rebound mechanisms and behavioral rebound mechanisms. By course end, participants will be ready to integrate sustainability into corporate financial strategies and drive organizational change considering human behavior.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explore global trends on impact investment approaches to promote sustainability. - Understand how regulatory changes affect loans, debt, and investments (e.g., EU taxonomy, green bonds, standards etc.) - Ability to measure non-financial performances (various ESG standards, CO2 emissions and its scopes, external verification) - Analyze the social, ecological, and economic impacts of global regulations and impact finance. - Create legitimate sustainability claims based on legal frameworks. - Examine how regulations shape sustainable financing and green project development. - Evaluate financial risks and returns of sustainability-focused investments. - Know how to lead sustainable change as an intrapreneur (micro-level) and entrepreneur (macro level) through financial strategies, impact investments and behavior economics.
42S19:
Name English: Communicating Sustainability
Danish Title: Communicating Sustainability
General Course Objectives: The objective of this course is to be able to translate, create and communicate sustainability solutions to a wider audience and build the capacity to be a sustainability thought leader.
Content: The goal of this course is to build leadership skills and competencies necessary to understand and successfully execute communication of sustainability. Participants will learn the most relevant concepts and tools related to sustainability communication, including stakeholder engagement, EU-taxonomy, sustainability reporting, data visualization and Science Based Targets. The course builds on practical case exercises, including a crisis communication simulation game. The results of the communication strategy will be presented to an expert panel during the course. Through a practical social media exercise, participants will learn how to debate the most challenging sustainability topics with critical stakeholders.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the main theoretical concepts and tools related to sustainability communication - Understand behavior design and storytelling - Know about visual infographics and data visualization. - Understand how the changing regulatory environment influences sustainability communication - Understand how greenwashing is practiced. - Know about crisis communication, marketing and stakeholder engagement - Create and present an operable crisis communication plan under time pressure - Ability to create, communicate and debate a sustainability agenda/strategy as a thought leader
42S20:
Name English: Master Project
Danish Title: Master Project
General Course Objectives: The Master Project should demonstrate the author’s breadth of view regarding the ability to arrive at well-grounded proposals for management actions concerning cross-disciplinary and cross-organizational sustainability problems. The master projects should demonstrate the ability to reach and present well-grounded proposals that should lead to implementable solutions.
Content: The master project course involves identifying a complex sustainability-related problem within an organization and addressing it using multidisciplinary scientific methodologies and cutting-edge international research. Participants are expected to take a holistic and systemic approach to the problem, developing models, systems, and processes that offer practical solutions. The thesis requires both written and oral communication of research-based knowledge and demonstrates the ability to work independently while reflecting on personal academic development and specialization in sustainability.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify a complex sustainability-related organizational problem. - Apply elements of current research at an international level to develop ideas and solve problems. - Apply multidisciplinary scientific methodologies, theories, and tools within sustainability. - Develop the ability to take a holistic and systemic view of a sustainability problem. - Develop relevant models, systems, technologies, and processes aimed at solving sustainability-related organizational problems. - Discuss research-based knowledge both orally and in writing. - Understand how to seek out leading international research within multidisciplinary sustainability. - Develop the ability to work independently and reflect on your own learning, academic development and specialization.
46120:
Name English: Scientific Programming for Wind Energy
Danish Title: Videnskabelig Programmering for Vindenergi
General Course Objectives: Writing code to solve complex scientific and engineering problems has become an essential skill for scientists and engineers. This course helps students to develop this skill through: learning core principles and best practices for programming; practicing usage of fundamental software development tools and techniques such as version control, packaging and architecture design; leveraging scientific computation tools commonly used in scientific Python, like numpy, matplotlib and scipy; developing, evaluating and communicating Python libraries for wind-energy applications through hands-on group projects, peer code reviews and code presentations. Through this course, a student’s material, cognitive, and social computational literacy will be largely improved, together with the ability to formulate computational problems in wind energy and solve them with programming.
Content: The content of this course is tailored to students who have average to little previous experience in programming and want to take other courses at DTU Wind. The course uses the Python programming language. During the course, students work in small groups on in-class exercises, weekly assignments, and two projects. Students must pass the first project to submit the second project. The final grade is evaluated based on the second project. Consistent practice in communication about scientific code is ensured by weekly group-to-group presentations of their solutions to the week’s assignment. In the first part of the course, students learn how to collaborate in groups on code using the version-control software git/GitHub, which is used throughout the semester. After that, students use the foundational packages for scientific Python programming (numpy, matplotlib, scipy) to practice basic skills such as numeric array manipulation, loading/​saving/​visualizing data, and writing/importing functions. These skills are cemented in the first project, in which groups calculate the time-marching response of a simple wind turbine model for different turbulent wind conditions and visualize the resulting statistics. After the first project is handed in, more advanced topics are presented. This includes more abstract concepts from general programming—such as object-oriented practices, designing package architectures, and linting—as well as more wind-specific topics—e.g., packages and data formats that are commonly used in wind energy. The course ends with the final project, in which students work individually or in groups to publish a Python package for wind energy, complete with tests and documentation. A list of pre-defined final projects is provided, but students may submit a request for a different project if they have an idea they would like to pursue.
