Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Utilize Python packages common to wind energy, such as numpy, matplotlib, scipy, PyWake, TOPFARM, xarray, pandas, etc. - Manipulate data stored in the most common wind-energy formats, demonstrating skills such as loading from/saving to file, performing computations, and visualizing results. - Design and publish a Python package for a wind-energy application with tests and documentation. - Collaborate with a team on a code base hosted on GitLab, demonstrating basic git skills such as adding, committing, pushing, and branching. - Develop, debug, and lint code using VS Code and related extensions. - Communicate code orally and also in writing, via diagrams, comments, commit messages, and documentation. - Critically analyze code for good coding practices such as modularity, maintainability, adherence to stylistic conventions, etc. - Write tests for scientific code. - Execute code on a computing cluster.
46711:
Name English: Stability and control in electric power systems
Danish Title: Stabilitet og kontrol i elforsyningssystemer
General Course Objectives: Give students the necessary background and competences for assessing stability in electric power systems.
Content: After a general introduction to the stability problems in electric power systems, the main categories of stability problems are treated, including the mechanisms of instability, countermeasures and theory for analysis. The lectures are complemented by exercise sessions with Python, where study cases are modelled, simulated, and analysed.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the principal causes of voltage, frequency, and rotor angle stability problems in electric power systems - Describe the different representations of the synchronous machines used for stability studies in electric power systems - Analyse voltage stability problems in electric power systems using PV curves - Explain the key concepts for frequency control in electric power systems - Analyse rotor angle small-signal stability problems in electric power systems and describe means to prevent them - Describe how the stability problems in electric power systems are affected by grid-related power transfer limitations and generator-related power injection limitations - Analyse rotor angle transient stability problems and describe means to protect the system against them - Analyse and explain analytical and simulation results
46W43:
Name English: Wind Turbines Components
Danish Title: Vindmøllers komponenter
General Course Objectives: Wind turbines consist of various components that work together to harness the energy of the wind and convert it into electrical power. Some of the key components include blades, tower, nacelle and drivetrain, sub-support structures. This course on wind turbine components aims to provide students with a comprehensive and basic understanding of the aforementioned components on their functions, design, materials, manufacturing, measurement, digital tools, and end of life. Please note that blades and sub-support structures are not covered in this course because they are well-explained in other classes (for instance, 46W11 and 46W34)
Content: The course consists of 13 modules covering the following content/topics: - General introduction of wind turbine mechanical, electrical and structural components - Conceptual design and sizing, introducing design standards IEC 61400 - Drivetrain topology, analytic loads calculations - Materials usage and recycling (including rare-earth material) - Tower design and manufacturing technologies - Condition monitoring and sensing - Life cycle analysis of selected components Each module will be structured with specific learning objectives and tasks. Usually, a typical module consists of one or two video lectures, relevant research problems or publications, and some calculation exercises.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe the function of major components and how they work together to produce electricity, including materials used and manufacturing technologies - Compare the different types of wind turbine drivetrains, including geared, medium-speed, and direct drive machines and understand the design tradeoffs - Describe different manufacturing technologies (welded and additive manufactured) for wind turbine towers (steel and concrete) and present pros and cons - Explain the measurement and sensing technologies on various components with the focus on condition monitoring - Summarize the maintenance and repair procedures for wind turbine components, including safety protocols and troubleshooting techniques - Use mathematical and engineering principles to design and size wind turbine components such as the shaft, gearbox, generator and supporting structures - Perform simple analysis on health monitoring data of selected components using turbine measurement data from public domain - Assess the environmental impact of turbine components throughout its entire life cycle, from the extraction of raw materials to manufacturing, transportation, installation, operation, maintenance, and finally, decommissioning and disposal.
47216:
Name English: AI-orchestrated self-driving labs (Online)
Danish Title: AI-orkestrerede selvkørende laboratorier (Online)
General Course Objectives: The students will obtain hands-on experience with self-driving experiments and machine learning-based orchestration and optimization software. The students will implement software capable of turning a custom Arduino-based setup equipped with pumps and colour sensors into an autonomous laboratory that is able to mix liquids toward targeted optical properties. The students will also get insight into computational tools and approaches to accelerate the discovery of clean energy materials, e.g. batteries, nano-catalysts, fuel cells, and photovoltaics. Moreover, the students will acquire expertise in working with open-source databases, data API, and FAIR-principles.
Content: A 3-week course focusing on learning the methods and tools necessary for AI-orchestrated self-driving labs consists of several components: lectures on theory, a guest lecture from industry, performing computer exercises and orchestrate experiments. Three main scientific areas are involved in this course: 1) Data-driven materials discovery (lectures and exercises) Database and API tools, FAIR data, high-throughput screening approaches 2) Machine/deep learning techniques for autonomous materials discovery (lectures, examples and exercises) Supervised/unsupervised methods, fingerprinting, Bayesian methods (generative algorithms) 3) Autonomous experiments (theory, simulations, and experiments) Introduction to the required software and hardware Orchestrate and direct a custom Arduino-based hardware based on data from experimental and theoretical databases. On-the-fly analysis of the output
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand and apply machine and deep learning approaches to analyze materials data and guide materials discovery - Understand and analyze computational and experimental databases for materials discovery - Apply Bayesian optimization and other machine learning techniques to optimize target materials properties - Implement software for running autonomous robotic experiments - Apply relevant software tools to analyze, interpret and evaluate experimental results - Understand how to work with open-source databases, data API, and FAIR-principles. - Understand the presence of noise in the experimental data and strategies to account for them - Present results in a concise oral presentation to an expert audience
47217:
Name English: Introduction to Electrochemistry (online)
Danish Title: Introduktion til elektrokemi (online)
General Course Objectives: In the near future, electrochemical energy storage and conversion devices are expected to become an integral part of our energy system, targeting to reduce the need for carbon-intensive processes and de-fossilize industries (Power-to-X). This course aims to provide a fundamental understanding of electrochemical reactions and the necessary concepts to describe electrochemical processes, enabling students to explain the working principles of selected electrochemical applications. The material of this course is equally suited for chemistry, material science, and physics students with previous knowledge of thermodynamics, kinetics, mixtures, and chemical reactions. The objectives of this course are to develop an understanding of electrochemistry and its specific concepts and to grasp the various conceptual approaches to describe cells, reactions, and their limitations.
Content: Historical overview and societal use of electrochemical processes, redox reactions, equilibrium electrochemistry, chemical thermodynamics, half-cell reactions, electrodes and interfaces, electrolytes, transport phenomena, industrial electrochemistry, energy conversion and storage, overview of electroanalytical methods, corrosion and corrosion protection
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Give an overview of modern electrochemical terms and concepts - Explain the key principles of electrochemistry, e.g. redox reactions - Describe the fundamentals of an electrochemical cell, such as the role of the anode/​cathode/​electrolyte - Evaluate a cell’s potential and predict the effect of concentration and temperature on an electrochemical reaction using the Nernst equation - Explain the basics of kinetics and mass transport of species in an electrochemical cell - Explain the principles (thermodynamics, kinetics, mass transport) governing an electrochemical reaction - Organize and execute project work based on the knowledge obtained - Communicate project work results orally and in writing - Evaluate a scientific presentation and give constructive feedback to peers
47341:
Name English: AI4Materials: Artificial Intelligence for Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery
Danish Title: AI4Materials
General Course Objectives: Machine Learning (ML) techniques in materials science are being used to accelerate the discovery and design of new materials and systems. This course will cover the fundamentals of ML methods tailored to materials science applications. The overall strategies for data-driven accelerated materials science, including data infrastructure, will be discussed. It will provide insight into key research methods, such as multi-scale simulations, automated materials synthesis with experiment planning, materials characterization techniques, and system-level testing that can benefit from AI acceleration for time and cost savings. We will cover ML for accelerating experimental and computational methods employed in materials research at multiple length and time scales, from atomic scale to system level. With project-driven learning objectives, students will gain hands-on experience of how ML methods can be used to accelerate all stages of materials discovery for computational methods and experimental techniques. 4-week group project where students work collaboratively to apply ML techniques to a specific materials science method. The project outcome is a written report and presentation.
Content: Principles of applied data science, datasets, FAIR data, exploratory analysis of materials data, surrogate models for accelerated simulations, reverse design with generative models, AI integrated materials design workflows, design of experiments, machine learning in accelerated materials synthesis process characterization and testing Literature references Book chapters, review articles, collected online learning resources will be provided
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the data-driven strategies to accelerate materials discovery, including essential data science infrastructure and best practices for managing large multi-fidelity datasets. - Summarize key ML techniques and their applications to materials science, including supervised and unsupervised learning, reinforcement learning, and generative models. - Identify the materials science methods used in materials discovery within computational simulation, synthesis, and characterization techniques that will benefit from acceleration with machine learning modeling. - Apply feature engineering, data preprocessing, and exploratory analysis on materials science dataset. - Create ML surrogate models to accelerate physics-based materials simulations at one of the scales - molecular dynamics, or phase field simulation, or finite element simulation. - Implement ML tool and workflow for materials synthesis planning, or design of experiments, or accelerated testing and characterization. - Critically analyze the performance of ML models within the context of projects in accelerating simulations or material characterization by collaborating in teams. - Prepare a written report describing the project's objectives, methods, results, and insights gained, and make a research presentation.
62010:
Name English: Product understanding
Danish Title: Produktforståelse
General Course Objectives: The course is a mandatory course for engineering students on the Process and Innovation study line. The aim of the course is that the students, who follow the course, gain basic knowledge about the design of a physical product by the applied materials and their manufacturing methods, as well as training in choosing materials for specific products. Applied materials, in this context, are the metals and polymers used in modern, industrial production. The student obtains insight in choosing materials both from points of view regarding application, durability, sustainability and environmental considerations. Furthermore, working with CAD is used as a supplement to the students' fundamental understanding of manufacturing.
Content: - The Granta Edu Pack program, structure and use. The program can be installed on the student's computer. - Introduction to the terms stress and strain as well as the analysis of a strain tension graph. - Introduction to the atomic structure of materials, crystallographic and amorphous structures. - Introduction to and use of phase diagrams. - The structure of metals and polymers and their applications and properties. - The sustainability of polymers. - Analysis of the materials in a given component and suggestions for selecting materials to a component. - Training in the presentation of an academic material subject. - Fundamental CAD and technical drawing.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Gain insight into the structure of a product (design and materials usage) by taking apart a domestic product (e.g. hair dryer or angle grinder). - Describe the mechanical properties and application of the materials often found in domestic products (metals and polymers). - Select metals and polymers for a given application. - Gain fundamental knowledge of the newer polymer types, e.g. bio-polymers, in relation to the sustainability challenges of polymers. - Conduct introductory laboratory investigations of the composition of materials and their material parameters, e.g. tensile test. - Describe the concepts of stress and tension and analyse a tensile graph and apply the data that comes from the analysis of a tensile test. - Conduct an information search within manufacturing methods. - Gain knowledge for the basic manufacturing methods used for products made from metals and polymers. - Use the term "material index" and use the material database program CES to select the optimal material for a given application. - Describe and apply simple phase diagrams, including TTT diagrams in connection with heat treatments. - Apply CAD and technical drawing at beginner's level, but still with such a routine, that the student will be able to seek help in future courses.
62090:
Name English: Technology and Manufacturing
Danish Title: Teknologi og Produktion
General Course Objectives: The course's overall goal is to impart knowledge to the students about - central parts of classical physics, especially statics and thermodynamics - scientific reasoning and methodology. The course thus aims at supporting their ability to understand technical and industrial problems, and contribute to the solution -- including energy conversion in relation to FN's Sustainable Development Goals. - The student will gain knowledge about practical production through excercises in Design Build Lab.
Content: Simple mechanical, structural and thermodynamic calculations. Being able to relate, apply and evaluate these in relation to industrial processes, especially Stirlingmotors. Practical exercises in Design Build Lab.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Calculate simple static problems - Calculate simple thermodynamic problems - Solve simple tasks from industry in statics and thermodynamics - Relate and identify industrial problems in statics and thermodynamics - Select an appropriate solution approach in industrial problems in statics and thermodynamics - Understand the difference between Otto-, Diesel- and Stirlingmotor based on their pV-diagrams - Relate the calculations and measurements done on the Stirlingmotor to the Stirlingmotor built by the students - Validate physical calculations and their results with respect to the course content - Present problem solving with regard to scientific thinking and methodology. - Gain knowledge of mechanical manufacturing methods through demonstrations and practical exercises.
62112:
Name English: Industry 4.0 in practice
Danish Title: Industri 4.0 i praksis
General Course Objectives: Industry 4.0 (The Fourth Industrial Revolution) is the ongoing automation of traditional manufacturing and industrial practices, using modern smart technology. Large-scale machine-to-machine communication (M2M) and the internet of things (IoT) are integrated for increased automation, improved communication and self-monitoring, and production of smart machines that can analyze and diagnose issues without the need for human intervention. This course is a hands-on and technical introduction on selected technologies in Industry 4.0 among others cooperation robots (cobots), mobile robots (AMR), vision system and Augmented Reality. In addition a hands-on Industry 4.0 is used.
Content: The course is running in a laboratorie in small groups and contains: · Introduction projects on programming cobots, AMR, vision system and doing 3D printing. · Project in use of cobots, AMR and visionsystem for solving a task with pick up, sorting, assembly and quality control. · Project in use of AR technology and 3D scanning in order to complete an Industry 4.0 related task. · Project in data and Industry 4.0 handled in a Industry 4.0 learnin facility. · Classes will be held in hands-on subjects related to the course. · Classes with theory will be held.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have insight into selected technologies and systems related automating and digitization of production systems and processes in relation to Industry 4.0 - Learn how to program robots with 6 axes who cooperates, mobile robots (AMR) and vision systems for use in solutions on simple automation tasks and explain how these technologies play a role in Industry 4.0 - Learn to use the Augmented technology, perform simple 3D scanning and use the software Blender to built guides and instructions for equipment in an AR space - Learn to retrieve data from a database and relate the data to a physical system - Learn to problem solve technical problems in different tasks and projects by finding the relevant material/documentation. - Lear to use engineering skills in project work in order to execute the efficient. - Gain knowledge on how a MES (Manufacturing Executing System) works and which role it plays in Industry 4.0 - Learn how you can organize and optimize a material flow in a Industry 4.0 system. - Gain knowledge on different censor technologies and understand how data is created in a production system and learn how this can be used in connection with Industry 4.0 - Explain how Industri 4.0 contributes to a higher sustanability
62121:
Name English: Manufacturing development and digitalisation (project no. 4)
Danish Title: Produktionsudvikling og digitalisering (projekt 4)
General Course Objectives: To give the students a solid knowledge of methods used in solving manufacturing engineering problems, and to give them practical experience in using such methods in a specific project in a company. The project build upon the skills and competences gained from the projects in 1-3. semester, and all mandatory courses in the production engineering education. The use of these skills and competences are integrated in a problem based context. In relation to methods this project forms the basis for a later final project in a company. The course contains several elements of Industry 4.0.
Content: The project om 4th semester will have production engineering improvement in a company as the overall theme. The project will include problem formulation, analysis and diagnosis and formulation of possible suggestions to solve the problems and possibly also ways to implement these suggestions. In the course, the students will asses the relevance of Industry 4.0 technologies. It is important that the problems in the project are both complex and interdisciplinary. Analysis and solutions must include aspects from more than one discipline regarding Operations Management, Technology, Economy, and Information Technology.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the importance of a process oriented approach, and ability to describe and analyse business processes including both technical and administrative aspects. - Basic knowledge of methods to handle complex production engineering problems where all phases including problem formulation, analysis, diagnosis, specification of possible solutions and possibly implementation are involved. - Ability to make appointment with a company concerning a specific problem area and on the basis of this specify a project. - Ability to develop a comprehensive problem formulation for a project - Ability to design and perform comprehensive analysis in relation a specific production engineering problem. This will include collection and analysing of both quantitative and qualitative data. - Ability to formulate comprehensive solutions to specific production engineering problems in a company based on the analysis and diagnosis performed. - Ability to specify which possible solutions to production engineering problems a company should choose in a specific situation and how they should be implemented. - Ability to evaluate the implementation of specific solutions to production engineering problems in a company from a strategic perspective - Have insight into selected technologies and systems related to digitization of value chains production systems, and processes as well as Industry 4.0 - Understand the importance of digitizing and Industry 4.0 in relation to the company's strategy and the company's development of value chains, production systems and processes - Understand how digitalisation and Industry 4.0 affects the company's ability to optimize processes and flow - Understand how the company's supply chain as well as production planning and management tasks are affected by digitalisation and Industry 4.0
62143:
Name English: Mechanical product documentation and analysis
Danish Title: Mekanisk produktdokumentation og -analyse
General Course Objectives: Whether designing a full product or a single component, understanding the fundamental challenges of engineering is essential. Beyond analyzing the physical loads acting on a component, students must master the conventions of technical documentation. This course introduces students to the engineering profession through the application of core technical competencies and group dynamics. Students will gain a foundational understanding of engineering problem-solving, including the acquisition of a professional technical vocabulary and proficiency in mechanics and CAD (Computer-Aided Design). Please note that a Windows-based laptop is required, as essential software is not compatible with macOS
Content: The course covers sketching techniques, fundamental projection rules, and standards for technical drawings of machine components. This includes dimensioning as well as specifying simple tolerances and surface roughness. A general introduction to graphical communication is provided, focusing on the presentation of results in technical journals. Furthermore, students will use CAD for product modeling, the creation of technical drawings, as well as illustrations and animations. Working in small groups, students will analyze a self-selected product (e.g., an electric screwdriver or a mini-robot) to identify its main components and functions. The product analysis is documented in a technical poster, focusing on production methods, material costs, durability, and functionality. Subsequently, students will develop a 3D-printed prototype of a simple mechanical system (e.g., a syringe pump) based on a given specification. The system will be based on a linear actuator controlled by a single-board computer and a stepper motor. The project concludes with systematic testing of the prototype and documentation of the results in a test report.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the characteristics of the projection (double-orthogonal and axonometric projection) and choose the most appropriate projection form for a given task. - Perform the drawing types, principles sketches and diagrams that describe machine construction and function and apply them to spatial visual drawings and sketches, mechanical engineering and design drawing. - Read a mechanical drawing and judge whether it is clear and unambiguous. - Produce a high-quality mechanical engineering drawing suitable for manufacture in an external workshop, including having demonstrated knowledge of relevant standards. - Model a product of multiple components in an advanced CAD system and apply the models as a basis for the production of simple machining drawings and Rapid Protyping of the models. - Use drawing (graphic modeling and communication) for problem solving, including proposition and presentation. - Demonstrate effective group collaboration, including clear communication, division of responsibility and constructive conflict management. - Systematically disassemble a mechanical product, identify main components and create bill of materials. - Identify components, materials, and analyze their properties in relation to function. - Document project work and results in technical reports, use technical terminology from a high professional level (objective, theory, methods, results, discussion and conclusion). - Visualize and present data using graphs, diagrams and tables.
62150:
Name English: Basic Mathematics
Danish Title: Grundlæggende matematik
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to provide the students with concepts, methods, and way of thinking in the areas of basic applied mathematics (primarily calculus). This especially involves the application of mathematical analysis in the study of mathematical models. Real-world problems, drawn from a wide variety of scientific, technological, and economic subjects, are central to the course.
Content: Elements of calculus and its applications.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Address and manipulate mathematical expressions (in the form of equations, functions, and parameterizations) - Handle trigonometric functions and the radian measure - Perform differentiation and apply derivatives, perform integration and apply antiderivatives and definite integrals - Apply elementary methods based on the manipulation of derivatives (Taylor’s formula of first and second order, Newton’s method in one variable) - Set up and manipulate simple infinitesimal models, solve elementary optimization problems - Analyze and characterize differential equations by means of fields of line elements and by studying the relationships between complete and partial solutions - Solve first order linear differential equations and first order differential equations with a separable right hand side by algebraic means - Solve second order linear differential equations with constant coefficients by algebraic means - Apply numerical methods for ordinary differential equations - Have elementary knowledge of vectors and vector functions in 2D and 3D - Set up and apply multivariable mathematical models, determine derivatives of multivariable functions - Have basic knowledge of the normal distribution
62283:
Name English: Digital Modeling and Technical Drawing Communication
Danish Title: Digital Modellering og Tegne-teknisk Formidling
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to give the students experience in using 3D modeling tools to generate design material in Revit and MagiCAD. The student must demonstrate skills in 3D modeling and prepare 2D design material based on a given case and give an estimate of dimensions (material, etc.) for each constructions and installations so that these dimensions can be incorporated into the technical communication (3D and 2D). The purpose is also for the student to be able to read and produce drawing material that is unambiguous and understandable for construction industry professionals at a level where they can build according to it. The students gain insight into: - to be able to use the industry's digital planning and communication tools with an emphasis on Revit and MagiCAD -develop working sketches by hand for reflective and projecting purposes - learn to read and draw plans, sections, elevations and technical drawings with specifications according to industry standards -be able to model several proposals competently - and assess design parameters in relation to the proposals - gain knowledge of the synthesis of buildings via digital modeling of: climate screen, static systems, installation and energy conditions, and draw these in 3D and 2D
Content: The purpose of the course is to give the student the opportunity to partly prepare a project proposal for a given building in the group and partly to delve into a part of a main project individually. Based on skills from courses 62319 and 62331 Key elements: -Sketching by hand - modeling in a digital environment - model iterations with a view to optimization - produce building design material in the form of graphic and digital communication
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use hand sketching as a tool for critical reflection in connection with solution selection and final design - Create technical drawing material in 3D in a digital environment - Create technical drawing material in 2D in a digital environment - Model building volume and constructions in a digital environment - Model mechanical installations in a digital environment - Model, visualize and set up alternative solution proposals, and analyze the advantages and disadvantages of the proposals, and based on this explain the choice of solution - Present plans, sections, elevations and technical drawings unambiguously and comprehensibly - Apply industry standards in technical drawing communication
62284:
Name English: Tender project
Danish Title: Udbudsprojekt
General Course Objectives: • that the student can prepare building details based on knowledge of structures, thermal insulation, moisture, etc. • that the student acquires knowledge and skills from subject courses in semesters 1-3 are included in the design work • that the student acquires knowledge about the documents that supplement drawings and calculations in connection with tenders for building or construction projects
Content: Plan and project in an interdisciplinary digital environment
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use knowledge and methods from the selected courses to carry out a complex engineering project - Describe, analyze and evaluate an acquired project that has reached the design phase - Complete a design project for a tender project, as well as prepare the necessary interdiciplinary detail drawings and documents so that the subject area can be sent to tender. - Know and assess contract forms and tendering law - Know, assess and prepare Tender Letter - Know, assess and prepare basic descriptions - Know, evaluate and prepare a list of offers - Plan and project in an interdisciplinary digital environment - Utilize knowledge about sustainability when choosing solutions and tenders - Account for the group work - Presentation of the project and chosen solutions - Detail design of interdiciplinary building details
62285:
Name English: BIP 4. Execution phase
Danish Title: BIP 4. Udførelsesprojekt
General Course Objectives: • the student acquires knowledge and skills from subject courses in the 3rd and 4th semesters and which are included in the project work • give the student the tools to turn a tender project into an execution project, with planning, construction site establishment and operation, as well as monitoring execution processes, within construction and construction.
Content: The course participants take a delivered project as their starting point, and which is converted from a tender project to a practical execution project. The project is based on the subject courses taught in the 3rd and 4th semester. The course includes establishing a construction site, operation and safety on construction site. As well as establishing of construction pits, assembly of building elements, assessment of construction methods.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use knowledge and methods from the selected courses to carry out a complex engineering project - Describe, analyze and evaluate a project proposal obtained - Convert the obtained tender project into practical execution - Construction site planning and construction site safety - Planning of construction pits - Assembly of building elements (concrete elements, shower cubicles, mechanical installations) - In situ production (walls, decks, bathrooms, mechanical installations) - Detailed execution timetable - Quality assurance and defect remediation - Account for the group work - Presentation of the project and chosen solutions
62286:
Name English: Operation and Maintenance of Road and Drainage Systems
Danish Title: Drift og vedligeholdelse af vej- og afløbssystemer
General Course Objectives: To give the student knowledge, tools and strategies for operation and maintenance of roads and drainage systems, with an emphasis on traditional economy and climate impact. Roads and drainage systems are both very important parts of society's infrastructure. Roads and drainage systems require large investments and with very long lifetimes, operation and maintenance are correspondingly costly for the economy and climate impact.
Content: Road structure and materials Operation and maintenance of roads and paths Operation and maintenance of permeable pavements Road maintenance strategy Road maintenance methods Registration and condition assessment, prioritization of efforts Operation and maintenance of signaling systems The main components of the drainage system. Operation and maintenance of the drainage system's structures and wells Data collection for existing capacity Adapting the drainage system's structures to climate change Operation and maintenance with a focus on operating energy optimization Operation and maintenance of LAR solutions Strategy for pipe renovation Methods of pipe renovation TV inspection and condition assessment and prioritization of renovation efforts Prevention of rat problems. LCA tools for roads and supply systems
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Acquire knowledge and tools for road operation and maintenance - Acquire knowledge and tools for operation and maintenance of drainage systems - Plan and design maintenance of road systems - Plan and design maintenance of drainage systems - Explain solution proposals for the maintenance of roads and drainage systems - Analyze and optimize energy consumption in the drainage system - Explain technologies for road maintenance - Explain technologies for pipe renovation - Analyze and recommend solutions assessed in relation to sustainability, supported by multi-criteria and LCA based methods - Explain the group's cooperation
62424:
Name English: Project work in practice
Danish Title: Projektarbejde i praksis
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide students with practical experience in planning, execution and documentation of group projects, including application of commonly used tools for execution and documentation of group projects, information search and performing a critical evaluation of information ad project results.
Content: Introduction to information search. Introduction to project planning. Execution, test and documentation of project work. Integration of experiences from different subject areas. Introduction to commonly used tools. Evaluation of the consequences of the application of commonly used tools. Evaluation of performed work.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Participate constructively in the execution of group projects. - Document the execution and results of group projects. - Implement, test and apply simple electronic circuits as part of group projects. - Implement, test and apply simple software programs as part of group projects. - Apply commonly used tools as part of the execution of group projects. - Apply commonly used tools as part of the documentation of group projects. - Apply commonly used tools for information search. - Critically evaluate the results of performed project work and information search. - Evaluate the sustainability of the application of commonly used tools.
62595:
Name English: Full Stack Development, Operations and Distributed Systems
Danish Title: Full stack udvikling, drift og distribuerede systemer
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to train the participants in developing web applications using some modern front-end technologies and to design, build, deploy and operate a modern backend for an app or website. To understand of theory and good practice in the construction of distributed systems.
Content: Architectures and design of modern backends as part of a distributed systems, such as client-server, Service oriented architectures (SOA), and web services, such as JSON, REST and GraphQL. Development of modern front- and back-end services. Richardson's maturity model for a REST service. Architectures in web application development (HTML, Javascript, serverside and client side languages and their interaction) Best practices in modern backend development. Managing concurrency issues in a backend. The course is project-oriented and includes development of a distributed system of your choice, typically a front- and back-end and communicatiing with a web page and/or an app.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the principles and architecture of web applications (front- and back-end) - Develop full-stack applications of a certain complexity - Document, implement, deploy and monitor a distributed system - Organize code according to the chosen architecture - Explain the principles of reactive programming - Use resource oriented protocols (such as REST) as client and server - Understand transactions and transaction isolation in a distributed system - Understand security aspects in a distributed system - Select and configure a suitable deployment platform and deploy a backend - Distinguise between different container-based virtualization technologies, such as Docker, and modern server management - Assess the sustainability when choosing deployment platform backend
62641:
Name English: Sustainability, mobility, and society
Danish Title: Bæredygtighed, mobilitet og samfund
General Course Objectives: The course is an introduction to the value creation and impact of transport on the environment, economic development, and society at large. The course covers the relationships between sutainability, mobility and society (e.g. commerce, manufacturing, quality of life, and culture).
Content: The course covers basic concepts of transportation systems and sustainability in transportation services. It examines various soft strategies for promoting sustainable modes, supplemented by real-world examples. In addition, students will learn basic techniques for analyzing travel demand and different types of transportation data. Emphasis is placed on developing the skills to evaluate real-world data and assess the impact of emerging public transportation options on both the transportation system and the sustainability of urban environments.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain different transport modes, their typical applications, technology development, and political issues. Explain basic concepts of urban development. - Define sustainability and measure the sustainability of transport services, especially in greenhouse gases (CO2). - Understand and explain different soft strategies to increase the use of more sustainable modes of transport. - Understand and explain the classic four-stage transport model: trip generation, distribution, modal split, and assignment. - Understand and explain basic concepts for analyzing transport demand such as trip, trip stages, transfer, commute, origin, destination, alternative route, volume, level of service, etc. - Understand the benefits and differences between origin-destination surveys and passive transport data. - Analyze a case study of real travel data. - Understand and explain the purpose and benefits of advanced traveller information systems. - Can write technical reports and present report results orally
62642:
Name English: Planning of infrastructure
Danish Title: Planlægning af infrastruktur
General Course Objectives: The objective of the course is to provide the students with the basic competences within the field of road traffic planning, as well as further develop their GIS skills to the level that is needed in the road sector.
Content: A road project in the Metropolitan area is coded, modelled and evaluated with respect to the traffic impacts. This includes specification of the project, overall need analysis, choice and coding of the alignment, estimating construction costs, calculation of route choice, induced traffic and other traffic impacts. The road project is evaluated by means of a cost-benefit analysis.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Carry out an overall need analysis for a road project and based on that to specify the project - Examine the alignment options and substantiate the final choice - Estimate the construction costs related to a road project - Understand the basic principles behind route choice assignment - Carry out a quality control of the results of the route choice assignments - Calculate induced traffic and interpret the results hereof - Calculate and analyze traffic impacts (e.g. accidents, noise, air pollution, travel time and driving costs) and be able to explain which initiatives will reduce the problems - Carry out a cost-benefit analysis of a road project and interpret the results hereof - Use GIS to produce simple maps to illustrate and analyze data and results - Write a technical report
62670:
Name English: Statistical Analysis and Data visualisation
Danish Title: Statistisk Analyse og Datavisualisering
General Course Objectives: To give the students a basic understanding of statistical, data-related concepts. To train the students in data visualization and the use of statistical analysis methods.
Content: - Basics of probability: random experiments, events, sample space, probabilities, rules for computation of probabilities, Bayes' theorem, independence and dependence. - Distributions: random variables- discrete and continuous, distribution functions, properties of distributions- mean and variance, quantiles. - Discrete distributions: Bernoulli, binomial, Poisson, and uniform distributions. - Continuous distributions: uniform, exponential, Poisson, normal, chi-squared, Student's t and F distributions. - Multidimensional random variables: joint, marginal, and conditional distributions. - Data analysis: descriptive statistics, measuring relationship using covariance and correlation. - The estimation problem: sample, population, confidence intervals, central limit theorem. - Statistical hypothesis testing: test statistic, level of significance, p value. - Linear regression: simple and multiple, fitting, prediction. - Time series analysis: additive and multiplicative models, trends and seasonality, forecasting. - R: analyzing and visualizing data using R, computing, performing hypothesis testing, fitting and prediction.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Apply the principles of probability theory to solve a given problem. - Create summaries and visualizations of a given dataset. - Estimate properties of a population and quantify the uncertainty of the estimate using confidence intervals. - Perform a one-sample Student's t test on a given dataset. - Perform Welch's test on a given dataset. - Perform estimation of single and multiple proportions. - Test for linear dependence of data using linear regression. - Apply Student's t test to a data in a multiple linear regression setting. - Perform analysis and prediction for time series data on a given dataset. - Perform statistical tests on data that do not have normality assumptions. - Compute the joint, marginal and conditional probabilities for a given problem.
62706:
Name English: Design of electrical installations 2
Danish Title: Projektering af elektriske installationer 2 (El-autorisation 2 hos Teknika)
General Course Objectives: The student obtains the theoretical basis for passing the electricity authorization test, which gives the right to approval as a professional responsible in an authorized electrical installation company when the requirements according to the Executive Order on the approval of professional responsible in the area of ​​electricity, plumbing and sewerage installation and in the gas area, etc. is fulfilled.
Content: Dimensioning of electrical systems and installations System earthing IT (TT and TN) Phase compensation Low voltage switchboards Selectivity Harmonic currents Surge current, short-time current and thermal average current LV trunking system Special areas (Construction and demolition sites, Agriculture and horticulture, Conductive rooms with limited freedom of movement, Camping sites,... )
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe and explain the construction of electrical systems and installations - Explain how electrotechnical concepts, calculation methods, legislation, orders and standards are used to design, install, commission and maintain electrical systems and installations in a safe and sound manner. - Use electrotechnical concepts, calculation methods, legislation, orders and standards to document, project, install, commission and maintain electrical systems and installations in a safe and sound manner - Identify and assess whether electrical panels and electrical machines can be installed legally - Analyze and assess electrotechnical operational and energy optimization issues in electrical systems and installations as well as develop, justify and select relevant solutions - Describe and explain, using electrotechnical documentation, practical and professional problems and solutions regarding electrical systems and installations to partners and users in Danish. - Engage in professional collaboration and assume responsibility for the group's results and individual members' learning regarding electrical systems and installations - Reflect on own and the group's learning needs and develop knowledge, skills and competences in relation to electrical systems and installations.
62712:
Name English: Basic C Programming
Danish Title: Grundlæggende C programmering
General Course Objectives: To develop foundational programming skills in C, enabling students to write, debug, and analyze basic programs using structured programming principles.
Content: - Introduction to the tools - Intro to C programming - Structured program development - Program control - Functions - Arrays - Pointers - Characters and strings - Formatted input/output - Structures, unions, bit manipulation and enumerations - File processing - Data structures - Computer-science thinking: Sorting Algorithms and Big O.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Install and configure a C programming development environment. - Identify and explain core C programming concepts, including syntax, data types, operators, and basic I/O. - Apply structured programming principles by designing modular programs using functions, loops, conditionals, and header files to separate interface from implementation and enhance code maintainability. - Interpret and create flowcharts to visualize and plan program logic. - Analyze and debug programs to resolve basic real-world programming problems. - Evaluate memory management techniques by implementing pointers, arrays, and dynamic allocation. - Create robust applications by integrating standard library functions and file I/O operations. - Implement and utilize fundamental data structures (e.g., arrays, linked lists) to organize and manage data. - Design, implement, and analyze common sorting algorithms while evaluating their efficiency using Big O notation.
62775:
Name English: Applied electrical engineering
Danish Title: Anvendt elteknik for Maskin
General Course Objectives: The purpose with the course is to give students a basic knowledge of electrical circuits, laws of electromagnetism, power transformers and electrical motors. To introduce and develop an understanding of electronic components, devices and circuits. This includes basic electrical properties (RLC), DC and AC circuits, basic laws and theories associated with circuit analysis, power transformer and principles of AC and DC motors. Lab activities of operating power transformers, AC and DC motors will be held with the students.
Content: Analyse of electrical systems, DC and AC circuits, power transformer, DC and AC motors, power and torque for motors. Control of simple motor set-ups. Small practical, relevant tests will be held with the students.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand active and passive components in electrical circuits. - Describe the characteristic curves for passive components like resistors, inductors and capacitors. - Be able to use Ohms law and Kirchhoffs Laws in simple electric Circuits. - Be able to use the mesh and node method in DC Circuits and calculate power in DC circuits. - Be able to use complex functions describing AC current, voltage, power, apparent power, reactive power and phase shift. - Understand basics of electrical power systems. - Understand basics of power transformer. - Understand the construction and function of the AC and the DC motors. - Understand power and torque for motors and gears for coupling of motors. - Understand the torque curves for DC motors - Understand the start-up/shut-down and direction reverse of AC motors. - Be able to use simulation software for simulation of smaller electrical circuits.
62804:
Name English: Semester project 4: Mechatronics og innovation
Danish Title: Semesterprojekt 4: Mekatronik og innovation
General Course Objectives: To give the students training in the implementation of an innovation process based on the development of a mechatronic product. Mechatronic products are mechanical products that contain electronic components such as sensors, actuators, and motors to control and monitor the products. Mechatronic products are thus central to the development of e.g. automated production facilities or robotics. Throughout the course, students will learn about the typical components of this type of product as well as typical control strategies. Essential aspects of the course include; Insight and understanding of innovation processes as well as exercises in carrying out a development project in a group where the group participants may have different professional interests. In addition, the course will train cooperation across areas of interest with the creation of common goals in the group, time planning, division of work, etc.
Content: The course is project-oriented and starts with the implementation of an innovation process with a focus on mechatronic products. In the first half of the course, the students will complete a mechatronics exercise which will give the students practical experience with the design and operation of a mechatronic product. In the second half of the course, the students will use this experience to complete an innovation process. As key elements of an innovation process, work will be done in these areas: Problem identification, idea generation, collection and assessment of quantitative and qualitative information, prototyping, and testing and testing of ideas, prototypes, and concepts. Throughout the course, the students will have to use the competencies they have acquired in 62807, 62694, and 62809. It is therefore recommended that the students take these courses alongside this one.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Apply programming, including conditional code execution, loops and functions to model a mechatronic product. - Design and implement combinational and sequential control logic on platforms such as microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino). - Design, build, and demonstrate self-developed functional mechatronic systems with at least one degree of freedom for real-world applications. - Write technical reports with clear structure, graphics, and well-documented source code. - Organize and design an innovation process to solve a concrete innovation challenge as well as explain and evaluate the chosen process and method on the basis of theory. - Analyze, assess and describe possible solutions to an innovation challenge from a business, technological, organizational and user perspective. - Select and argue for a chosen innovation solution and describe the solution's implementation, business potential and budget. - Communicate a proposed solution as a written presentation that includes a documented prototype as well as analyzes and considerations about business, user, sustainability, organizational, and technological conditions and also relates to the implementation of the proposed solution. - Evaluate and reflect on collaboration in a team, including own and others' roles in the innovation process to understand how the team communicates, plans, decides, solves problems, handles disagreements, and handles professional and personal differences, as well as the use of own and others' skills in solving a specific task.
62808:
Name English: Dynamics
Danish Title: Dynamik
General Course Objectives: To provide the student with a fundamental understanding of phenomena related to dynamics of rigid bodies and mechanical vibrations.
Content: 1D impact. Vector description of rigid body kinematics. Kinetic energy, linear and angular momentum for rigid bodies and systems of particles. General equations of motion. Work and power. Work-energy relations. Conservation principles for linear and angular momentum and energy. Vibrations of systems with one degree-of-freedom; undamped and damped free vibrations; forced vibrations, frequency response and resonance; energy methods.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Draw free-body and kinetic diagrams for plane motion of rigid bodies. - Apply vector-description for plane motion of rigid bodies in inertial and non-inertial coordinate systems. - State the general plane equations of motion for rigid bodies and systems of rigid bodies and determine linear and angular accelerations. - Find center of gravity and mass moment of inertia for simple bodies. - Use the principle of linear momentum conservation to solve simple 1D impact problems. - Apply the principle of linear momentum conservation for rigid bodies and systems of particles. - Apply the principle of angular momentum conservation for rigid bodies and systems of particles. - Determine the natural frequency and damping ratio for systems with one degree-of-freedom. - Find the response of damped and undamped systems with one degree-of-freedom subjected to a harmonic load. - Determine work and power of external forces and couples. - Apply work-energy relations for plane motion of rigid bodies. - Use the energy method to set up the general equations of motion for particles and rigid bodies.
62809:
Name English: Modeling and Programming
Danish Title: Modellering og Programmering
General Course Objectives: This course aims to provide a basic level of proficiency in MATLAB programming and the application of physical laws to formulate mathematical models within the field of mechanical and control engineering.
Content: Fundamental Matlab programming: Conditions, loops, functions, arrays, plots, handles, and file input/output. Classical laws of physics: for example Newton's 2nd law, Fourier's heat law, Kirchhoff's current law. Numerical solution of initial value problems: Euler's method, midpoint rule, ODE45, and Simulink. State-space formulation. Linearization of differential equation.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Write programs in Matlab using conditional code execution, loops, functions, and arrays. - Solve a set of differential equations in the time domain with ODE45. - Solve a differential equation in the time domain with Simulink. - Apply the Matlab Symbolic Math Toolbox for manipulation of and solving equations. - Describe the governing equations for various problems in the field of mechanical and control engineering. - Rewrite higher order differential equations as a set of first order differential equations. - Determine whether a system is linear or not, and perform the linearization of nonlinear systems. - Apply file handling (read and write) as well as plotting to handle data.
62810:
Name English: Geometric Operations in Plane and Space
Danish Title: Geometriske operationer i plan og rum
General Course Objectives: The course aims to strengthen the understanding of geometry in the plane and in space. The understanding is improved by defining and calculating geometric quantities, e.g. arc lengths or volumes. Vectors and matrices are used as a common tool, and are also used to emphasize the importance of the chosen coordinate system.
Content: Vectors in plane and space. Dot product, Cross product and scalar triple product. Cartesian, polar and spherical coordinates. Homogeneous coordinates. Coordinate transformation. Parametric curves, surfaces and solids. Implicitly given curves (in the plane) and surfaces (in space). Arc length parametrization of curves. Frenet-Serret basis, curvature and torsion. Normal of a surface. Translation, rotation, scaling, shearing, reflection and projection of a geometric object. Center of mass, moment of inertia. Composite motion.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Apply vector calculus in plane and space. Dot product (scalar product), calculation of lengths and angles, cross product, plane product, space product. - Apply Cartesian coordinates, polar coordinates, and spherical coordinates - Perform a kinematic analysis of a trajectory curve which is given by a parameterization - Find parametric representations of implicitly defined curves and surfaces - Apply 2x2, 3x3 and 4x4 matrices for description and analysis of 2-dimensional and 3-dimensional geometry and motion - Calculate arc length, area and volume for general curves, surfaces and solids - Calculate the center of mass and moment of inertia of selected geometries - Construct geometries by Cosserat-sweeping
62C22:
Name English: Railway technology, operations and capacity
Danish Title: Jernbaneteknologi, -drift og -kapacitet
General Course Objectives: This course offers technical knowledge of railways that is useful in the planning and management of railway operations. The course provides theoretical and practical knowledge including mathematical methods and industry-specific computer applications typical for the planning of rail traffic.
Content: Particular conditions for railways - including an introduction to train control on railways, infrastructure elements, signalling systems and timetabling as well as evaluation of the capacity and regularity of timetables.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the technical components and operating characteristics of railways, such as track, signals, and trains - Describe current important concerns and trends in railway management, and organization of government agencies and private operators - Explain digital technologies and Industry 4.0 in railways, including signal technologies such as ERTMS and train tracking - Calculate train motion and minimum train separation (headways) - Calculate the punctuality of railway lines from historic data or simulation - Operate a model of a railway infrastructure and analyze this using relevant computer software - Create a timetable for a railway service and explain the parameters and decisions required - Evaluate the capacity of a railway line and explain how capacity and timetable influence punctuality - Reflect on trends in transport demand and produce a rail network plan for the future

62L95:
Name English: Management with Data
Danish Title: Ledelse med Data
General Course Objectives: The purpose for the student is to acquire knowledge, skills and competencies to use data and documentation to create a basis for managerial decision-making processes and work systematically with quality development of the organization's core task.

Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have gained knowledge of and understanding of data as a basis for creating empirical knowledge and documentation. - Assess different data types in relation to managing the organization's development. - Plan collection of relevant data as documentation of management efforts and can analyze data, as well as plan management efforts on the basis of collected and processed data. - Work systematically with quality development of the organization's core task using a data-informed management practice. - - - - - - - -
62P05:
Name English: Project Management - Methodologies and Tools

Content: Learning Objectives (continued): Skills: • Perspect and discuss applied theories and methods in relation to own practice, including involving relevant actors • Discuss the unpredictable and complex context of the project and draw consequences from this Contents: The main content is: • Project organization • Project management as an interdisciplinary way of working • Project types and models • Project establishment, planning, estimation, management, evaluation and follow-up • Project economics and stakeholder analysis • Project evaluation forms and methods
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have knowledge of project management's applied theory, method and practice and be able to use correct subject terminology (Knowledge and understanding) - Have knowledge of and be able to reflect on relevant theories and methods in a scientific theoretical perspective (Knowledge and understanding in the project management field - Have an understanding of and be able to reflect on the use of the presented tools in practice (Knowledge and understanding) - Apply project management methods and tools to gather and analyze information, and will master the skills associated with project management (Skills) - Evaluate theoretical and practice-related project management issues and justify the actions and solutions chosen (Skills) - Communicate practical and professional project management issues and solutions to partners and management in both written and oral form in a professional manner. (Skills) - Apply methods and tools for analyzing, structuring, planning, managing, documenting and evaluating projects (Skills) - Reason for choosing and deselecting relevant theories, methods and tools in project management (Skills) - Handle complex and development-oriented project management situations in working relationships (Skills) - Independently enter into professional and interdisciplinary project collaboration and assume responsibility within the framework of professional ethics (Competences) - Develop own practice in relation to the project management area (Competences) - Bringing the subject's skills to use in your own organization (Competences)
63853:
Name English: Sustainable Business in the pharmaceutical industry on emerging markets and developing countries - Access to health care
Danish Title: Bæredygtig forretningsudvikling i medicinalindustrien på vækstmarkeder og udviklingslande - adgang til sundhedsydelser
General Course Objectives: This course will try to understand, analyze and evaluate cases on the strategic and organizational challenges and dilemmas facing pharmaceutical companies when they roll out activities in developing countries. In particular, the focus will be on how pharmaceutical companies try to reach the poorest and most vulnerable segments in developing countries and what specific challenges they face in this regard. During the course we will try to understand and analyze how pharmaceutical companies measure and communicate on their impact in developing countries, including social return on investment (SROI), ESG reporting and the SDG´s. We will analyze which partnership models work most effectively in developing countries and how contextual factors influence on the economic, social and environmental effectiveness of different partnership models. As access to care increasingly rely on digital solutions and IA, and on the use of technology in facilitating access to products and services, the course will zoom in on the kinds of technologies that support sustainable business models and philanthropic activities best, The course takes point of departure in literature on International Business, Sustainable Business Models, impact investment and finance, technology and corporate philanthropy as well as research undertaken by faculty during 2022/2023. The course will provide insights from a number of pharmaceutical companies operating in developing countries. In particular, cases and evidence from the Novo Nordisk-Roche partnerhip on Changing Diabetes in Children (CDiC) will be used extensively, and practitioners from Novo Nordisk and Roche will participate in the course. The course is an innovative collaboration between DTU, CBS and Novo Nordisk under the EuroTeq framework, with guest lecturers from Novo Nordisk being actively involved and allowing students from different backgrounds coming together and benefiting from diverse perspectives.
Content: Social Return on Investments Creating Shared Value Impact investments Corporate Social Responsibility Sustainability Environment, Social, Governance, ESG Sustainable Development Goals, SDG Pharmaceutical industry Emerging Markets and Developing Countries Technology and AI Digital technologies International Business
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understanding the empirical field of corporate philanthropy and sustainable business in the pharmaceutical industry in developing countries - Understanding, applying and critically assessing theories and frameworks related to sustainable business and corporate philanthropy in the pharmaceutical industry in developing countries - Understanding, applying and critically assessing methodologies for calculating the social, environmental and financial impacts and efficiency of corporate philanthropy and sustainable business models in the pharmaceutical industry in developing countries - Understanding and critically assessing the various financing models that can be brought to bear - Understanding and critically assessing the role of digital solutions and AI to sustainable business and corporate philanthropy challenges in the pharmaceutical industry in developing countries - Understanding and critically assessing the balance between global integration versus local adaption - Evaluating models for corporate social responsibility for the pharmaceutical industry in low and middle income countries - Understand and analyze global business and CSR in the pharmaceutical industry
