General Course Objectives: The student should learn to describe and use modelling of battery materials and devices at different lengths and time scales.
Content: • Introduction to the modelling and simulation of rechargeable batteries. • Porous electrode theories, materials, structure, function, and operation. • Density Functional Theory approaches. • Cluster expansion. • Kinetic Monte Carlo approaches. • Molecular Dynamics approaches. • Continuum modelling. • Multi-scale modelling. • Machine Learning methods. • Application to lithium and sodium chemistries (-ion, air, and sulfur) and redox flow batteries: intercalation and conversion materials, electrolytes, transport, electrochemical processes, ageing, and fabrication processes. • Access to specific software (freeware and in-house) will be provided.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Describe the fundamental theory behind different modelling methods - Understand uses and limitations of various models - Be able to choose the appropriate method to tackle different problems and aspects of a battery - Perform calculations using the codes provided during the course (ASE/GPAW, LAMMPS, Matlab and Python scripts, COMSOL Multiphysics, CLEASE) - Explain limitations in battery technologies - Explain how to link materials scales - Engage with battery modelling experts - Present your results in a concise report
62236:
Name English: Industrial Programming
Danish Title: Industriel Programmering
General Course Objectives: To develop foundational programming skills, enabling students to understand and communicate industrial automation requirements, particularly in scenarios involving databases and robot automation.
Content: • .NET framework • Visual Studio development environment • Basic C# syntax, console application structure, variables, expressions • Boolean logic, branching, looping • Type conversion, complex variable types, string manipulation • Functions, variable scope • Debugging in Visual Studio, error handline • Object-oriented programming (OOP), OOP techniques such as inheritance, polymorphism, UML • Collections, comparisons, conversions • LINQ, using databases • User interface programming using WPF • Robot arm programming using an Universal Robot cobot
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Install and configure a programming development environment. - Identify and explain core programming concepts, including syntax, data types, operators, and basic I/O, to understand software functionality. - Apply decision-making structures (e.g., if, switch) and loops (e.g., for, while) to analyze and control automation logic. - Understand and describe object-oriented principles such as encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism to support structured software design. - Document classes and their relationships using UML to communicate system architecture. - Explain the role of exception handling (try-catch) in improving program stability. - Use debugging tools to analyze and troubleshoot errors in industrial software. - Understand and describe database integration to store and retrieve industrial process data. - Apply basic programming to create simple automation solutions using predefined tools and libraries (e.g., database operations, robot control). - Implement a basic control program to interface with an industrial robot and predefined libraries or APIs. - Apply Industry 4.0 and 5.0 aspects like human-centric automation, cybersecurity, and mass personalization in an industrial software context.
62278:
Name English: Sustainable water treatment and groundwater protection
Danish Title: Bæredygtig vandbehandling og grundvandsbeskyttelse
General Course Objectives: The natural drainage system, e.g. streams, lakes and fjords, affects the quality of groundwater, which is the basis for drinking water treatment. At the same time, groundwater recharge is affected by climate change and the way, we handle rainwater and rainwater runoff. The course aims to support a sustainable urban water management by outlining the interactions among stormwater and groundwater in water supply systems. The main objective of this course is to develop students competences in terms of quantitative and qualitative aspects related to water supply, mainly focusing on groundwater protection and water treatment technologies. This includes how environmental legislation leads to action plans and remediation to protect our groundwater resources.
Content: Denmark's drinking water supply is covered by groundwater. Throughout the country, there is focus on developing new methods for securing good water quality for the water supply. In this course you will learn about the design of water treatment plants. In the course you will also learn how to protect the groundwater resource in the context of the The 17 Global Goals for Sustainable Development, the whole water cycle and in relation to legislation on water planning. Processes at the water treatment plants, the interior design and technologies. The influence of climate change and rainwater handling on the groundwater resource and water balance. Groundwater protection and action plans Water abstraction, chemistry and water quality as well as water treatment to ensure drinking water quality. Legislation and plans that support the protection of groundwater: the EU Water Framework Directive and related Danish legislations.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Gain an overview of essential elements of groundwater recharge, based on climate change and new ways of handling rainwater and drainage, among others - Initial design, calculation and documentation of a water plant, and presentation here off - Explain the overall water balance equation for an area with focus on the connection with the natural drainage system - Carry out water characterization and quality criteria - Explain water treatment technologies, including the chemical processes that occur on a water treatment plant - Explain threats to groundwater quality - Explain groundwater protection and action plans and knowing the most relevant legislation within soil, groundwater and water supply - Analyze and recommend solutions assessed in relation to sustainability, supported by multicriteria and LCA based methods - Reflecting on and justify choice of solutions - Reflecting on the group's cooperation with particular focus on interaction with possibly exchange students
62287:
Name English: Building Renewal - structures
Danish Title: Bygningsfornyelse - konstruktioner
General Course Objectives: Throughout the course, the student must acquire knowledge about Sustainable Building Renewal. The student design the necessary changes to the building's structures so that the building's interior design and expected resource consumption meet current and future requirements for sustainable construction.
Content: Buildings use up to 40% of Denmark's total energy consumption. To meet the government's and the EU's goal of reducing the energy consumption of existing buildings by at least 50% by 2050, it requires massive investment in renovation projects. At the same time, the buildings must be rebuilt to meet future requirements for Sustainable Construction. A project proposal will be made for the proposed changes to an older building with the following topics: • Analysis of possible sustainable measures • Registration and evaluation of building structures. • Economic assessment of costs of rebuilding, maintenance and improvements. A tender project is prepared for selected subject areas, for example: • Design of necessary structural changes caused by new interior design and transformation. • Design of repair due to fungus damages. • Design of necessary reinforcement of foundations.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Assess and analyze an old building with a focus on the preparation of an action plan for how the building can be renovated/transformed to meet future functional requirements , energy requirements and sustainability requirements. - Proposal for a more contemporary space division or transformation of the use of the building. - Proposal for an energy renovation of the building. - Proposal for the establishment of a recreational area on the roof or on terrain and new balconies with a focus on energy optimization, energy production and retention of rainwater. - Assess the fire technical conditions. - Design of necessary structural changes caused by new interior design. - Design of repair due to fungus damages. - Design of necessary reinforcement of foundations. - Explain for the cooperation of the group.
62288:
Name English: Building renovation registration and design proposals
Danish Title: Bygningsfornyelse registrering, ide og design
General Course Objectives: The course will provide the student with knowledge of Danish building traditions throughout history. Based on this knowledge, a design proposal will be prepared so that the building will meet current and future requirements for interior design, energy consumption, indoor climate and sustainability. The design proposal will require renewal of mechanical installations as well as necessary structural changes to the supporting structures in the building.
Content: Buildings use up to 40% of Denmark's total energy consumption. In order to meet the government's and the EU's goal of reducing the energy consumption of the existing building stock by at least 50% by 2050, massive investments in renovation projects are required. At the same time, the requirements for the design and use of our buildings are changing. The students prepare a registrant with associated design proposals for building renovation, with the following means: • Analysis and assessment of building condition • Registration and assessment of mechanical installations and building structures. • Design proposals for changes to the interior, including a new bathroom • Design proposals for changes to the climate shield, with an assessment of minimizing energy consumption. • Design proposals for water, drainage, heating and ventilation conditions for a contemporary comfort level and minimizing future resource consumption • Design proposals for necessary structural changes • Sustainability assessment of the design proposals • Economic assessment of the costs of the proposed solutions.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Evaluate and analyze an older building, with a focus on preparing an action plan for how the building can be renovated to meet future functional, energy requirements and sustainability requirements. - Prepare proposals for a more contemporary space division with special emphasis on establishing wet rooms. - Prepare proposals for energy renovation of the building. - Prepare proposals for establishing a recreational area on the roof, or on terrain, and establish new balconies, with a focus on energy optimization, retention of rainwater and energy production. - Evaluate the fire engineering conditions. - An Energy Label is prepared for the building - Design of new heating and ventilation installations for contemporary energy and comfort requirements. - Design of new drainage and water installations for contemporary energy and comfort requirements. - Explain for the cooperation of the group.
62289:
Name English: Building renovation energy and installations
Danish Title: Bygningsfornyelse energi og installationer
General Course Objectives: Through the course, the student will acquire knowledge about Danish building tradition through the ages. Based on a prepared design proposal, the students will work on the project further, so that it becomes a Tender Project and Execution Project according to FRI's service description.
Content: Buildings use up to 40% of Denmark's total energy consumption. In order to meet the government's and the EU's goal of reducing the energy consumption of the existing building stock by at least 50% by the year 2050, massive investments in renovation projects are required. At the same time, the requirements for the design and use of our buildings are changing. The students prepare a Tender Project and Execution Project for a building renovation, with the following objectives: • Analysis of the submitted Design Proposal • Design necessary changes to building structures to make it possible to carry out the Design Proposal • Design a new bathroom • Design changes to the climate shield proposed in the Energy Label. • Design new water, drainage, heating and ventilation installations • Design and document the Sustainability Proposals listed in the Design Proposals • Economic assessment of the costs of the proposed solutions.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Assess and analyze an older building, with a focus on analyzing a design proposal for building renovation of an existing building so that it meets future functional, energy and sustainability requirements. - Design new wet rooms. - Design energy renovation of the building. - Design recreational areas on roofs or on the ground, as well as new balconies with a focus on energy optimization, rainwater retention and energy production. - Design fire protection for existing buildings. - Project proposals in Energy Label - Design new heating and ventilation installations for modern energy and comfort requirements. - Designing new drainage and water installations for modern energy and comfort requirements. - Explain for the cooperation of the group.
62326:
Name English: Urban Water and Road Infrastructure
Danish Title: Byers vand- og vejinfrastruktur
General Course Objectives: The course aims to introduce the student to the infrastructure of a local area, understood as roads, paths and parking, as well as wastewater supply and rainwater drainage, also based on soil conditions. In this course you will learn to analyze, plan and design good, up-to-date and thus sustainable road and supply systems. The students must: - be able to familiarize themselves with the statement and regulations of a local plan, - acquire basic skills in the design of road and traffic facilities as well as drainage systems and rainwater management. - be able to use the profession's digital tools for fcommunication - and acquire tools to constructively participate in and contribute to the group's collaboration.
Content: This course focuses on being able to design parts of infrastructure facilities. Traffic and Roads: - Road users. - Content of the plans on roads, paths and parking. - Traffic safety and traffic engineering - Design of roads and paths. - CAD Water and Environment: - The content of the plans on environmental and supply conditions. - Planning and design of waste water supply. - Planning and design of rainwater drainage on surface and under terrain - Dimensioning of piped systems - Initial dimensioning of detention basins
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify and locate traffic problems. - Develop solutions to traffic problems. - Design selected elements of road construction in urban areas. - Carry out an overall planning and prepare a proposal/project proposal for a local area's wastewater and rainwater supply. - Plan and design elements for surface solutions for rainwater. - Plan and design elements for drainage piping systems using manual calculation methods. - Communicate and argue for the assignment in writing and orally, with focus on digital tools. - Explain team cooperation and developments.
62360:
Name English: Cast-in-place concrete structures
Danish Title: Pladsstøbte betonbygværker
General Course Objectives: The student must gain sufficient knowledge and understand the behavior of cast-in-place concrete structures. The student must gain skills in design of cast-in-place concrete structures.
Content: Overview of course subjects, where the students can delimit and plan the project work: Mandatory: Determinations of loads, statically models, statically determined and undetermined disc structures. Internal forces in cast-in-place concrete structures: Elasticity theory and plasticity theory Structures carrying capacity: concrete slabs, concrete beams, concrete columns and concrete walls Joints: design and carrying capacity The project work must be done according to the subjects above and approved by the professors
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze structural and statically model for cast-in-place concrete structures - Evaluate possible load combinations - Calculate internal forces in cast-in-place concrete structures by using elasticity theory and plasticity theory - Design and dimension plates and beams - Design and dimension walls and columns - Design and dimension joints in and between structural elements - Reflect on and motivate chosen solutions - Present and explain the group cooperation
62361:
Name English: Hgh-Rise Buildings - Structures
Danish Title: Højhusbyggeri - Konstruktioner
General Course Objectives: The student must gain sufficient knowledge and understand the behavior of structures in high-rise buildings. The student must gain skills in design of high-rise buildings constructed by using prefabricated structural elements
Content: Overview of course subjects, where the students can delimit and plan the project work: Obligatory: Determinations of loads, statically models, statically determined and undetermined disc structures. Internal forces in high-rise buildings: Elasticity theory and plasticity theory Structures carrying capacity: slabs, beams, columns and walls. Joints: design and carrying capacity The project work must be done according to the subjects above and approved by the professors
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Analyze structural and statically model for a high-rise building - Evaluate possible load combinations - Calculate internal forces in high-rise buildings by using elasticity theory and plasticity theory - Design and dimension plates and beams in elements - Design and dimension walls and columns in elements - Design and dimension joints in and between structural elements - Reflect on and motivate chosen solutions - Present and explain the group cooperation
62370:
Name English: Building installations and indoor climate
Danish Title: Bygningsinstallationer og indeklima
General Course Objectives: Through the teaching and self-study, the student will acquire knowledge about the choice of installation principles and management strategy for ventialtion, cooling and heating in complex buildings.
Content: Mechanical installations are necessary for us to provide a good indoor climate and to ensure comfort in all buildings. The course includes project proposals, for these installations for a complicated building, with evaluating different designs of these. Procurement / export project is carried out for heating, cooling, ventilation and associated automation.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Evaluate and analyze forms of energysupply forventilation, cooling and heating - Assess and design advanced heating and ventilation as well as cooling systems for a larger building. - Prepare a main project for integrated heating cooling and ventilation - Use BIM as a design and dimensioning tool for mechanical installations. - Compile selected HVAC parts of preliminary and main projects for BMS, including functional descriptions and principle diagrams for selected plants - Use of indoor climate simulation for planning heating, cooling and ventilation systems - Documents, argues and communicates the chosen solutions in writing and orally - Explain for the cooperation of the group.
62602:
Name English: Mechanics and Thermodynamics for Electrical Engineers
Danish Title: Mekanik og termodynamik for elektroingeniører
General Course Objectives: To provide students with a basic knowledge of mechanics and thermodynamics that is necessary for the design and analysis of modern engines and sustainable power systems.
Content: Mechanics: • Motions, moments and moments of inertia for rotating bodies • Work-energy-principle • Stresses and strains in materials under axial, torsional, and bending loads. • Thermal expansion of solids Thermodynamics: • Basic thermodynamic systems • Thermodynamic states and parameters, heat and work • First law of thermodynamics for open and closed systems • Selected circular processes, e.g., heat pumps, cooling plants and thermal power plants • Heat transfer: conduction, convection and radiation
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand and being able to calculate motions, moments and moments of inertia of rotating masses in connection with electric machines. - Apply the work-energy-principle to simple, mechanical systems, and realize the analogies to the calculation of electric components such as resistors and capacitors. - Have an understanding of materials' strain and stresses under applied mechanical loading. - Have an understanding of friction, and the length expansion of materials by exposure to heat. - Conduct experimental verification of e.g. the correlation between mass moment of inertia and angular acceleration for an electrical machine and/or the efficiency of a heat engine. - Understand the phase change of substances. - State and explain the first law of thermodynamics for open and closed systems. - Identify heat transfer mechanisms and calculate the corresponding thermal resistance. - Be able to calculate various selected thermal processes such as heat pumps, cooling systems or thermal power plants. - Understand and being able to calculate the efficiency of individual processes, including thermal and Carnot efficiency. - Brainstorm on the design of new sustainable power systems.
62638:
Name English: Road Engineering Materials
Danish Title: Road Engineering Materials
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is that students can acquire knowledge and skills in road engineering materials as well as relevant laboratory and field test methods on both micro and macro levels. The course introduces both traditional road materials with relevant calculation methods of optimum materials content, and “greener” solutions in modern road pavement (e.g., recycled waste materials, innovative surface materials, sustainable construction techniques, smart pavement…). In addition, the students are able to design and calculate the road drainage system, as well as evaluating methods for the possible treatment of rainwater. Permeable pavement, including the mixture design method, sustainability analysis, and the main properties are presented as an example to show how the road structure can contribute to rainwater control.
Content: This course is designed to introduce the properties and compositions of road engineering materials, as well as relevant laboratory and field test methods including soil, aggregate, cement and cement concrete, bitumen and asphalt concrete. Students go through transport geotechnics and soil reinforcement techniques applied to different soil conditions for road construction. Students can draw and analyze different aggregate gradation curves, understand chemical reactions during the cement hydration process, calculate optimum bitumen content, learn mixture design methods and other sustainable and smart pavement technologies. In addition, the student can evaluate methods for the possible treatment of rainwater. The permeable pavement is also introduced as a method of drainage, which includes the design method, selection of construction materials, road performance evaluation, common road distress and maintenance methods.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Recognize the layout and components of the typical road structure - Understand basic knowledge of transport geotechnics and soil reinforcement methods - Evaluate the physical, mechanical properties of aggregates, as well as gradation curve - Identify the bitumen composition, mechanical properties and asphalt concrete mix design - Demonstrate the cement hydration process, mechanical properties and cement concrete mix design - Identify common road distress types and maintenance methods - Recognize "green solutions" on traditional pavement and smart pavement - Design and calculate the road drainage system - Implement the permeable road pavement design and main properties
62811:
Name English: Introduction to mechatronics and robotics systems
Danish Title: Introduktion til mekatronik og robotteknik
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to give the students a theoretical introduction to, and practical experience with mechatronics and robotics. The course encompasses the technical interaction between the fields of mechanics, electronics, and software development in industrial and robotic systems. The course equips the student with the competence to design and construct automatic control systems in the control, regulation, and monitoring of industrial and robotic systems. The course applies control engineering theories and methods used to manage, for instance, mechanical and thermal processes in practical systems, using sensors, actuators, and associated software development on controllers such as microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino and ESP32) or industrial controllers (e.g., PLCs), along with graphical user interfaces.
Content: Sensors, actuators, and electric circuits; rotary and linear motion sensing; motors; combinatorial and sequential control; control systems using microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, ESP32) or industrial controllers, HMI panels, GUI Interface.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Use sensors, analog signals, and actuators for robotic or industrial applications. - Select and implement appropriate interfaces for sensors and actuators in systems such as robotic systems or process plants. - Develop software and graphical user interfaces for control and monitoring applications. - Design and implement combinational and sequential control logic on platforms such as microcontrollers (e.g., Arduino, ESP32) or industrial controllers (e.g., PLCs). - Analyze and design control methods for dynamic processes such as robotic systems or process plants. - Apply and evaluate control methods to regulate systems such as mechanical, fluid, or thermal systems. - Implement real-time programming of PID algorithms to microcontrollers, including Arduino, ESP32, or industrial controllers. - Gain hands-on experience through laboratory and workshop activities involving systems such as 3-DOF robotic system. - Collaborate on hands-on projects in teams where students design, build, and demonstrate self-developed functional mechatronic systems with more than two degrees of freedom for real-world applications.
62G01:
Name English: Introduction to sustainability
Danish Title: Bæredygtighed – begreber og koncepter
General Course Objectives: To achieve a fundamental understanding of sustainability and the role of businesses in sustainable development, including planetary boundaries, 'doughnut economics,' and the UN Sustainable Development Goals. The ten themes of the EU's ESRS standards will be among the key topics covered in the course. These include climate, pollution, biodiversity, water and marine environments, resource use, corporate governance of sustainability, and social sustainability concerning employees, end-users, the value chain, and relevant local communities. With this fundamental understanding, participants will be able to advise their management and colleagues on the prioritization of sustainability initiatives.
Content: See learning goals
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Gain a fundamental understanding of sustainability, including definitions, dimensions, and the role of companies in sustainable development - Understand the planetary boundaries, doughnut economics, and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) - Understand the themes of the EU’s ESRS (European Sustainability Reporting Standards), including climate, biodiversity, water, resource consumption, and social sustainability - Understand the conceptual and legislative history of corporate sustainability - Gain general knowledge of relevant regulatory frameworks, including EU sustainability directives - Distinguish between "more sustainable", absolute sustainability, and regenerative/restorative practices - Operationalise the understanding of sustainability for application in company activities - Translate the understanding of sustainability into a foundation for sustainable business development - Identify connections between environmental sustainability, social sustainability, and their governance - Develop a holistic orientation towards sustainability and navigate its various branches - Identify interlinkages between environmental and social sustainability and integrate governance aspects into sustainability work across organisational levels - Advise management and decision-makers on sustainability priorities based on analysis of legislation, ESG standards, and the company’s specific context
62G02:
Name English: Life Cycle Assessment and Sustainability Impacts
Danish Title: Livscyklusanalyser og bæredygtighedspåvirkninger
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide an understanding of the environmental impacts of products from a life cycle perspective and experience in conducting a life cycle assessment using simplified methods. With these skills, the participant will be able to conduct relevant LCA screenings and thereby target the company's sustainability efforts, including priorities in general business development.
Content: See learning goals
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain environmental impacts according to different impact categories - Understand impacts on the environment, climate and nature, including options for converting quantities into emissions, waste volumes, energy, water and land requirements - Describe the life cycle phases and processes in the life cycle of a product system - Define goal and scope, a relevant functional unit, and system boundaries for an LCA of a product system - Develop a plan for data collection of process inputs and outputs - Calculate impacts on the environment, climate and nature, including conversions from quantities to emissions, waste volumes, energy, water and land requirements - Calculate environmental and climate impacts of raw material procurement, own production, distribution and disposal - Assessment of the environmental impacts throughout a product's life cycle (the module covers an LCA screening of a product) - Have linguistic and sustainability skills in LCA - Identify sustainability impacts, including on climate, of processes, such as production and transportation, in an organisational-LCA - Identification of points for development and with potential for it
62G03:
Name English: Developing and improving ESG performance
Danish Title: Udvikling og forbedring af ESG-performance
General Course Objectives: The course aims to provide an understanding of how ESG performance of an organisation can be improved, with the aid of relevant techniques, methodologies, and technologies.
Content: Additional learning goals: - Identify links between decisions in sustainable product development and their effects on business processes and the value chain - Navigate complex requirements from stakeholders, regulations, and the market Evaluate how resource efficiency, material selection, and circular economy principles can strengthen a company’s ESG performance
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand how both technological and nature-based solutions can be used to improve ESG performance - Understand principles of Design for Environment, Design for Disassembly, and the concept of material efficiency - Understand how social sustainability can be developed and improved within the company and across the value chain - Understand how to apply external validation mechanisms such as SBTi - Apply methods, models, and techniques to improve performance, including digitalisation and technologies for product disassembly - Apply principles of sustainable product development, including Design for Environment, Design for Disassembly, sustainable materials, and material efficiency - Integrate ESG principles into business processes and the value chain by applying technologies, models, and methods that improve environmental and social sustainability - Propose strategies for sustainable production, including recycling processes, reverse logistics, and maintenance - Conduct impact assessments of process improvements, new policies, and new technologies - Assess and implement external validation standards and certification of ESG performance - Apply portfolio management to coordinate multiple simultaneous initiatives - Evaluate how methods, models, and techniques for sustainable development of processes and products—including those in the value chain— can impact ESG performance
62G04:
Name English: ESG reporting
Danish Title: ESG-rapportering
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide an understanding of how to identify relevant standards and procedures and create a credible and valid ESG report for an organization. With this understanding, participants will be able to apply relevant EU directives (including ESRS standards for ESG reporting), conduct materiality analyses and data validation, prepare credible ESG reports, and manage data requests from the value chain.
Content: The ten thematic standards in ESRS (E1-5, S1-4 and G1) and their content are included in the module “Introduction to Sustainability”
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand the relevant EU directives that govern ESG reporting at the company, value chain, and industry level - Understand the general standards for sustainability reporting, including ESRS standards 1 and 2 on general requirements and disclosures, as well as the standard for small and medium-sized enterprises (VSME)* - Understand the role and use of software tools in ESG reporting - Conduct double materiality analysis (DMA), including stakeholder analysis, selection of metrics, and gap analyses - Independently apply and implement ESG reporting in compliance with applicable EU directives and ESRS standards to ensure transparent and credible sustainability communication - Assess the validity of data and information used in reliable ESG reporting - Prepare a sustainability statement for the annual report, including appropriate structure, use of graphs and illustrations, and carry out processes related to evaluation and potential auditing - Manage and assess data requests from larger companies within the value chain, including customers and suppliers - Avoid greenwashing and greenhushing, and ensure credibility in reporting - Contribute to ensuring that ESG performance measurement and documentation supports overall business development - Critically assess and validate ESG data and identify potential risks of misleading reporting with regard to stakeholders and legal requirements - Integrate ESG reporting into the company’s strategic decision-making processes and use measurements and documentation to improve ESG performance and the company’s market position
62G05:
Name English: Sustainable Business Development
Danish Title: Bæredygtig virksomhedsudvikling
General Course Objectives: The purpose of the course is to provide an understanding of potential strategies for the sustainable development of businesses, with a focus on their business models and value chains. The module covers both environmental and social sustainability. With this understanding, participants will be able to comprehend and analyze the integration of sustainability into corporate strategy and value chains, develop sustainable business models and strategies, assess the relevance of external validation standards, and facilitate sustainable transformation through value chain analysis, circular economy, and stakeholder engagement.
Content: Two additional learning goals: - Independently analyse and develop sustainable initiatives for companies by integrating environmental, social, and economic considerations into business models, operations, and value chains - Facilitate sustainable transformation in companies through value chain analysis, circular economy principles, and stakeholder engagement to potentially create long-term competitive advantages
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Understand and discuss the integration of sustainability into business strategy and objectives - Understand environmental management systems and explain their applications - Understand business models that support the circular economy, e.g. servitization and product-service systems - Understand how social sustainability can be incorporated into company strategy and objectives, as well as into the value chain - Formulate strategies for integrating circular economy principles into companies - Assess the potential for external validation through, for example, SBTi or EcoVadis - Analyse customers’ sustainability reports and priorities, including customer purchase criteria - Analyse the potential for sustainable development within a company’s own products and processes - Conduct value chain analysis, including customer understanding and supplier collaboration - Develop conceptual solutions, including proposals for new business models to support sustainable business development - Acquire the ability to identify how sustainability is embedded in a company’s goals and strategy - Develop a holistic understanding of how business decisions impact sustainability performance
62I20:
Name English: Organizational Psychology and Management
Danish Title: Organisationspsykologi og ledelse
General Course Objectives: The purpose is for the student to acquire knowledge, skills and competencies to develop their own leadership, management practices and organization through psychological perspectives.
Content: The course content may vary depending on the type of tender. Contact the course coordinator for further information.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have knowledge and understanding of theories, concepts and methods within selected organizational psychology research areas in relation to the development of one's own management practice and organization. - Reflect on the concepts and methods of selected organizational psychology schools in relation to one's own practice. - Assess, justify, select and apply relevant solution models for one's own organization based on an understanding of organizational psychology. - Develop your own leadership based on organizational psychology. - Identify your own and the organization's development needs as a basis for working on developing your own organization's practice based on organizational psychology. - - - - - -
62L28:
Name English: Strategic Management
Danish Title: Strategisk ledelse
General Course Objectives: It is the aim that the student acquires knowledge, skills and competencies to strategically develop his leadership tasks and justify strategical options in leadership practices.
Content: The course content may vary depending on the type of tender. Contact the course coordinator for further information.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have knowledge and understanding of theories, concepts and models regarding strategic management based on the organisational and so-cial perspectives - Have skill sets to be able to justify and select theories and models regarding strategic management for the analysis of organisational capabilities - Have skill sets to be able to collect, analyse empiricism and evaluate leadership practices based on a strategic perspective - Translate knowledge and skill sets for strategic management and actions in practice - Identify the need for competency development relating to strategic changes and development - - - - - -
62L96:
Name English: Management with Data
Danish Title: Ledelse med Data
General Course Objectives: The purpose for the student is to acquire knowledge, skills and competencies to use data and documentation to create a basis for managerial decision-making processes and work systematically with quality development of the organization's core task.
Content: Data-driven decision-making becomes particularly interesting for companies in the age of big data and artificial intelligence. The course will: • help understand how data can be used for managerial decisions to lead to business value for a company • provides insight into what is needed for a data-driven company from a managerial point of view • discuss challenges a manager needs to be aware of when relying on data analytics and AI for decision-making and show solution ideas • explain how a data-driven culture can be built in a company The course language will be English, but most of the teaching material is in Danish. The exam report can be written in Danish or English.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have gained knowledge of and understanding of data as a basis for creating empirical knowledge and documentation. - Assess different data types in relation to managing the organization's development. - Plan collection of relevant data as documentation of management efforts and can analyze data, as well as plan management efforts on the basis of collected and processed data. - Work systematically with quality development of the organization's core task using a data-informed management practice. - - - - - - - -
62P11:
Name English: Communication and Team Relations
Danish Title: Kommunikation og teamrelationer
General Course Objectives: The aim of the course is to heighten the students' understanding of their role as project managers and the added responsibility to make the cooperation and the communication between the project participants function in the best possible manner, such that you become co-players in regard to the project. The course gives the students insight into and training in the use of tools for communication, cooperation along with metods for analysing and dealing with challenges within communication and team cooperation.
Content: Preferences and motivation of individuals Team development Change management
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Have an understanding of methods and tools within communication, cooperation and project management, and must be able to reflect on their use in practise while using correct terminology. - In a theory of science perspective, be able to identify, understand and reflect on theories and methods within communication and cooperation. - Assess, choose and argue for the choice of theories, methods and tools which best support the development of the communication and cooperation in a concrete context. - Communicate practise based and academic problems and solutions within communication and team relations both orally and in writing in a professional manner. - Observe and collect empirical data in a relevant manner in relation to a chosen problem in cooperation - Initiate growth for one-self, the individual project participants, the project group and the organisation, within communication and teamrelations - Discuss, develop and adapt chosen theories and methods to own management practise, whithin communication and teamrelations. - .
63870:
Name English: Needfinding at the Hospital
Danish Title: Behovsafdækning på Hospitalet
General Course Objectives: The course establishes the foundation for innovation in the hospital ecosystem by introducing methodological context analysis and the identification of 'matters,' 'problems,' 'needs,' or 'challenges' (hereafter: 'needs'). Through fieldwork at hospital departments, as well as relevant theory, you will be able to analyze the context of innovation and your own role in the innovation process. Also, you will be introduced to methodologically identification of needs and the development of the knowledge base necessary to validate and refine these needs, thereby laying the groundwork for innovation and problem-solving in future projects, including a master's thesis if applicable.
Content: In this course, you will work in a team assigned to a specific hospital department, where agreements have been made in advance. Fieldwork within the department is a central part of the course. The teaching includes sessions introducing theory and methodology, as well as presentations from practitioners. The course concludes with an open seminar where the results are presented to partners form the hospitals. The platform innocloud.dk is applied for knowledgesharing and interaction with the wards. Teams have access to supervision, either online or through visits to the department. Process reflection and learning reflection—both individually and as a team—are an integral part of the course.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain and discuss the meaning and role of the 'need' in systemic innovation process models - Interact and communicate with healthcare professionals, patient relatives, and other relevant actors - Conduct a qualitative case study - Synthesize findings from a qualitative study into a context analysis by applying Actor-Network Theory, value frameworks, and theory about knowledge dynamics, including mapping relevant actors and considering economic, technological, and legislative factors - Methodologically discover areas of importance and 'needs' in the innovation ecosystem and apply qualitative methods and other relevant research methods to develop knowledge necessary to qualify and prioritize these - Disseminate, communicate and share knowledge about prioritized 'needs' to relevant actors in the ecosystem - Propose a future process for innovation and problem solving based on prioritized 'needs' - Estimate the potential gain for actors in the ecosystem, and discuss critical factors relevant to the further development of prioritized 'needs', incorporating feedback from the partner - Plan and organize a group’s teamwork for an organizational need finding process - Reflect upon a group's role and actance in the innovation ecosystem in relation to team roles and team dynamics
LY100:
Name English: Problem-Based Project Work and Research Methods
Danish Title: Metodelære og rapportskrivning
General Course Objectives: The course introduces students to working with problem-based project work (PBL) as an academic and learning method. The goal is for students to gain a fundamental understanding of the entire project process: from idea and problem formulation to method selection, data collection, and academic analysis. The focus is on developing practical skills in project writing, collaboration, and methodological awareness, which can be applied throughout the program and in practice.
Content: Problem-based project work (PBL), idea development, problem background, problem analysis, problem formulation and delimitation, literature search, theory selection and use of academic concepts, understanding of methods (qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods), scientific empirical data (measurements, log data, observations), humanistic empirical data (interviews, questionnaires), project planning and operationalization, academic analysis, discussion, conclusion, perspective, as well as presentation techniques and peer feedback. The above topics are addressed based on maritime issues. The working method is self-study, supported by ongoing guidance and peer-to-peer feedback. Students work with self-chosen or assigned problems and gradually develop their methodological awareness and project competencies.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the principles of problem-based learning (PBL) and describe how it is applied in maritime contexts. - Identify and formulate a practice-oriented problem and delimit it in terms of time, place, and relevance. - Analyze and explain a problem from relevant academic perspectives – including assessing causes and consequences. - Select and use relevant academic literature and explain how it contributes to understanding the project's problem. - Explain and apply relevant theories and concepts in the analysis of a specific problem. - Compare and choose between qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods in relation to the project's purpose and questions. - Use and combine different types of empirical data (measurements, observations, interviews, questionnaires) in working with practice-oriented data. - Plan and structure a small-scale project, including linking goals, methods, and empirical data into a coherent work process. - Actively participate in academic feedback and reflect on others' and one's own project components in peer-review situations. - Critically reflect on one's own methodological choices and work process and assess how these choices affect the project's quality and applicability.
LY200:
Name English: The maritime industry and key stakeholders
Danish Title: Maritim brancheforståelse
General Course Objectives: This course aims to provide students with a solid foundation for understanding the complexity of the maritime industry, its many stakeholders, and how they interact and influence each other within a global value chain, along with an initial introduction to key concepts. Throughout the course, students will develop the ability to identify, analyze, and discuss issues from an industry perspective. This includes gaining an understanding of, and being able to analyze, how external and internal stakeholders influence technical, strategic, and operational decisions in the maritime industry – and how, as a naval architect, one can navigate these influences.
Content: The global network, value chain, and stakeholders of the maritime industry; concepts, maritime infrastructures; direct and indirect influence on decisions, technology, and practice; ship types and their unique profiles; design, construction, and operation; business models, operational cultures; and the influence of key stakeholders on the industry and the maritime sector.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain what the maritime industry encompasses and how it differs from other industries. - Identify key stakeholders and their overall functions. - Describe how stakeholders are interconnected within a value chain. - Participate in professional dialogue about the structure of the industry. - Explain and apply relevant theories and concepts in the analysis of a specific problem. - Understand how value creation occurs in shipping and related sectors. - Understand how different operational models and ship types have unique profiles and distinguish between their business models. - Understand how design, construction, and operation are inextricably linked. - Understand how stakeholders – both direct and indirect – shape decisions, technology, and practices in the maritime sector. - Apply analytical methods to map stakeholder influence. - Reflect and use problem-solving in realistic, interdisciplinary scenarios.
LY300:
Name English: Ship Hydrostatics 1 – Intact and Damaged Stability
Danish Title: Skibshydrostatik 1 - intakt- og skadestabilitet
General Course Objectives: The course introduces the principles of ship stability with a focus on lines plans, hydrostatic curves, loading conditions, weight estimation, and sectional area curves. The methods are applied in a concept study of a selected vessel.
Content: - Stability in the concept study of a selected vessel - Types of stability and terminology - Sectional area curve - Lines plan - Weights and centers of gravity - Hydrostatic curves
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Identify stability concepts and their significance for a vessel’s performance - Explain the importance of accurate lines plans in ship design - Identify and apply relevant hydrostatic curves in the preliminary design phase - Explain loading conditions and their use in stability assessment - Apply calculation methods relevant to ship stability - Estimate weights and centers of gravity for a vessel - Prepare and use sectional area curves in design work - Assess a ship’s stability under different condition - Use computer‑based tools to support stability calculations - Identify and apply relevant standards and regulations related to ship stability - Use loading computers as a tool for solving intact stability tasks
MA100:
Name English: Problem-Based Project Work and Research Methods
Danish Title: Metodelære og rapportskrivning
General Course Objectives: The course introduces students to working with problem-based project work (PBL) as an academic and learning method. The goal is for students to gain a fundamental understanding of the entire project process: from idea and problem formulation to method selection, data collection, and academic analysis. The focus is on developing practical skills in project writing, collaboration, and methodological awareness, which can be applied throughout the program and in practice.
Content: Problem-based project work (PBL), idea development, problem background, problem analysis, problem formulation and delimitation, literature search, theory selection and use of academic concepts, understanding of methods (qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods), scientific empirical data (measurements, log data, observations), humanistic empirical data (interviews, questionnaires), project planning and operationalization, academic analysis, discussion, conclusion, perspective, as well as presentation techniques and peer feedback. The above topics are addressed based on maritime issues. The working method is self-study, supported by ongoing guidance and peer-to-peer feedback. Students work with self-chosen or assigned problems and gradually develop their methodological awareness and project competencies.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the principles of problem-based learning (PBL) and describe how it is applied in maritime contexts. - Identify and formulate a practice-oriented problem and delimit it in terms of time, place, and relevance. - Analyze and explain a problem from relevant academic perspectives – including assessing causes and consequences. - Select and use relevant academic literature and explain how it contributes to understanding the project's problem. - Explain and apply relevant theories and concepts in the analysis of a specific problem. - Compare and choose between qualitative, quantitative, and mixed methods in relation to the project's purpose and questions. - Use and combine different types of empirical data (measurements, observations, interviews, questionnaires) in working with practice-oriented data. - Plan and structure a small-scale project, including linking goals, methods, and empirical data into a coherent work process. - Actively participate in academic feedback and reflect on others' and one's own project components in peer-review situations. - Critically reflect on one's own methodological choices and work process and assess how these choices affect the project's quality and applicability.
MA143:
Name English: Mechanical product documentation and analysis
Danish Title: Mekanisk produktdokumentation og -analyse
General Course Objectives: Whether designing a full product or a single component, understanding the fundamental challenges of engineering is essential. Beyond analyzing the physical loads acting on a component, students must master the conventions of technical documentation. This course introduces students to the engineering profession through the application of core technical competencies and group dynamics. Students will gain a foundational understanding of engineering problem-solving, including the acquisition of a professional technical vocabulary and proficiency in mechanics and CAD (Computer-Aided Design). Please note that a Windows-based laptop is required, as essential software is not compatible with macOS
Content: Sketching techniques, basic projection rules and standards for performing drawings of machine components. Dimensioning, including indication of simple tolerances and surface roughness. General introduction to graphic communication, including presentation of results in technical journals. Use of CAD for product modeling, production of technical drawings as well as illustrations and animations. The students will in small groups analyze a product of their own choice (for example, electrical drill, mini-robot) where main components and function are identified. The work with product analysis is documented in a technical report with focus on production methods, material costs, sustainability and functionality. Thereafter, the students will develop a 3D-printed prototype of a simple mechanical product (for example, a syringe pump) based on a given product specification. The product will be based on a linear actuator controlled by a single-board computer and stepper motor. The project is finalized with a systematic evaluation of the prototype with documentation of the results in a test report.
Learning Objectives: A student who has met the objectives of the course will be able to: - Explain the characteristics of the projection (double-orthogonal and axonometric projection) and choose the most appropriate projection form for a given task. - Perform the drawing types, principles sketches and diagrams that describe machine construction and function and apply them to spatial visual drawings and sketches, mechanical engineering and design drawing. - Read a mechanical drawing and judge whether it is clear and unambiguous. - Produce a high-quality mechanical engineering drawing suitable for manufacture in an external workshop, including having demonstrated knowledge of relevant standards. - Model a product of multiple components in an advanced CAD system and apply the models as a basis for the production of simple machining drawings and Rapid Protyping of the models. - Use drawing (graphic modeling and communication) for problem solving, including proposition and presentation. - Demonstrate effective group collaboration, including clear communication, division of responsibility and constructive conflict management. - Systematically disassemble a mechanical product, identify main components and create bill of materials. - Identify components, materials, and analyze their properties in relation to function. - Document project work and results in technical reports, use technical terminology from a high professional level (objective, theory, methods, results, discussion and conclusion). - Visualize and present data using graphs, diagrams and tables.
